$$-\Delta u + \frac{u^{q}}{(u+\varepsilon)^{q+\alpha}} = \lambda u^{p} \ \text{in } \Omega, \qquad u = 0 \ \text{on } \partial\Omega,$$
and let $u_\varepsilon \in H_0^1(\Omega)$ denote a nonnegative minimizer of the associated energy functional
$$J_\varepsilon(v) = \frac{1}{2}\int_\Omega |\nabla v|^2\,dx + \int_\Omega F_\varepsilon(v)\,dx - \frac{\lambda}{p+1}\int_\Omega (v^+)^{p+1}\,dx,$$
where $F_\varepsilon$ is the primitive of $s\mapsto s_+^{q}/(s_++\varepsilon)^{q+\alpha}$ vanishing at $0$. Suppose that, along a subsequence $\varepsilon\to 0^+$, the minimizers $u_\varepsilon$ converge to a nonnegative function $u\in H_0^1(\Omega)$ that is a (weak) solution of the limit singular problem
$$-\Delta u + u^{-\alpha}\chi_{\{u>0\}} = \lambda u^{p} \ \text{in } \Omega, \qquad u = 0 \ \text{on } \partial\Omega.$$
Question: Is the limit solution $u$ necessarily strictly positive throughout $\Omega$?

Equip $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ (with $n \geq 2$) with the standard symplectic form $\omega = \sum_{i=1}^n dx_i \wedge dy_i$. Let $M \subset \mathbb{R}^{2n}$ be a smooth hypersurface (or a germ thereof). The restriction $\omega|_M$ has a one-dimensional kernel at every point of $M$, and the integral curves of this kernel distribution are called the characteristic curves of $M$. A characteristic curve is said to be planar if its image is contained in some affine 2-plane of $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$.

Determine how restrictive the condition is that every characteristic curve on $M$ is planar. More precisely, classify (or otherwise describe) all smooth hypersurface germs $M$ in the standard symplectic space $(\mathbb{R}^{2n}, \omega)$ for which all characteristic curves are planar.

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ ($N\ge 1$) be a bounded domain with smooth boundary, and let $d(x):=\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Omega)$. Fix real numbers $0<\alpha<\beta<1$ and $0<k<2$, and set $K(x):=d(x)^{-k}$. For a parameter $\lambda>0$, consider the singular semilinear Dirichlet problem
$$(\mathrm{III})\qquad -\Delta u \;=\; K(x)\bigl(\lambda u^{\beta}-u^{\alpha}\bigr)\quad\text{in }\Omega,\qquad u\ge 0\text{ in }\Omega,\qquad u=0\text{ on }\partial\Omega,$$
and, more generally, its $p$-Laplacian counterpart ($1<p<\infty$)
$$-\Delta_{p}u \;=\; K(x)\bigl(\lambda u^{\beta}-u^{\alpha}\bigr)\quad\text{in }\Omega,\qquad u\ge 0\text{ in }\Omega,\qquad u=0\text{ on }\partial\Omega,$$
where $\Delta_p u=\operatorname{div}(|\nabla u|^{p-2}\nabla u)$. A solution $u$ is said to have compact support if the set $\{x\in\Omega:u(x)>0\}$ is compactly contained in $\Omega$.

It is known that:
\begin{itemize}
\item if $k-\alpha<1$, then there exists $\lambda^{*}>0$ such that for every $\lambda>\lambda^{*}$ problem $(\mathrm{III})$ admits a strictly positive solution $u_{\lambda}$, and for $\lambda$ small no solution exists;
\item if $1<k-\alpha<2$, there exists $\lambda^{**}>0$ such that for every $\lambda>\lambda^{**}$ problem $(\mathrm{III})$ admits at least one solution with compact support.
\end{itemize}

Question: In the regime $k-\alpha<1$ (and analogously for the $p$-Laplacian generalization above), do solutions with compact support exist for problem $(\mathrm{III})$?

Let $M\subset\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ ($n\ge 2$) be a smooth strictly convex closed hypersurface bounding a convex domain, and let $\omega$ denote the standard symplectic form on $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$. The outer symplectic billiard map associated with $M$ is defined as follows: for a point $x\in\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ outside $M$, consider the characteristic line through a tangency point $y\in M$ such that the chord $xy$ is tangent to $M$ at $y$ along a direction in the kernel of $\omega|_{T_yM}$ (the symplectic characteristic direction); the image $T(x)$ is the point obtained by reflecting $x$ through $y$, i.e. $T(x)=2y-x$. A point $x$ is called $3$-periodic if $T^3(x)=x$ but $T(x)\ne x$.

Prove that the set of $3$-periodic points of the outer symplectic billiard map associated with any smooth strictly convex closed hypersurface $M\subset\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ has Lebesgue measure zero (Ivrii's conjecture for 3-periodic orbits of multidimensional outer symplectic billiards).

Let $\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n \geq 2$) be Euclidean space and let $\mathcal{L}$ denote the space of oriented lines (light rays) in $\mathbb{R}^n$. The space $\mathcal{L}$ has dimension $2n-2$ and inherits a canonical symplectic structure from the cotangent bundle $T^*\mathbb{R}^n$ via symplectic reduction (identifying an oriented line with the equivalence class of unit covectors along it).

A smooth hypersurface $M \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ (locally the graph of a smooth function of $n-1$ variables) defines a billiard (optical) reflection map: an oriented line that hits $M$ transversally is sent to its reflection across the tangent hyperplane at the point of incidence. This reflection is a local symplectomorphism of $(\mathcal{L}, \omega)$.

Define the set of optical symplectic transformations $\mathcal{O} \subset \mathrm{Symp}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathcal{L})$ to be the set of local symplectic transformations of $\mathcal{L}$ obtainable as finite compositions of billiard reflections in smooth mirrors.

Since a generic local symplectic transformation of $\mathcal{L}$ depends on a smooth function of $2n-2$ variables (e.g., a generating function or Hamiltonian), while a mirror is determined by a smooth function of $n-1$ variables, one expects $\mathcal{O}$ to be a proper, "small" subset of $\mathrm{Symp}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathcal{L})$.

Problem: Give an intrinsic characterization of the set $\mathcal{O}$ of optical symplectic transformations inside the full group of local symplectic transformations of the space of oriented lines. That is, find necessary and sufficient conditions on a local symplectomorphism $\Phi : \mathcal{L} \dashrightarrow \mathcal{L}$ for it to be expressible as a finite composition of billiard reflections in smooth hypersurfaces of $\mathbb{R}^n$.

Background. A real flat projective structure (also called a real projective structure) on a manifold M^n is a maximal atlas of charts to RP^n whose transition maps are restrictions of projective transformations in PGL(n+1, R). For a closed surface Σ_g of genus g > 1 carrying such a structure, the following decomposition theorem holds: there exists a (possibly empty) collection of pairwise disjoint simple closed geodesics C_1, …, C_k on Σ_g such that each connected component of Σ_g \ (C_1 ∪ … ∪ C_k) is either

(i) an annulus that is projectively covered by an affine half-space (an "elementary" annulus), or

(ii) the interior of a compact convex real projective surface with negative Euler characteristic (where a real projective surface is convex if its developing map is a diffeomorphism onto a properly convex domain in RP^2).

Moreover each curve C_i bounds either one or two annuli of type (i), and such a decomposition is unique.

Problem. Formulate and prove a 3-dimensional analogue of this theorem. Precisely: given a closed 3-manifold M^3 equipped with a real flat projective structure, find a canonical decomposition of M^3 along a finite collection of disjoint embedded surfaces (totally geodesic, or otherwise canonically defined) into pieces falling into an explicit finite list of model types — analogous to the elementary annuli and convex pieces in the surface case — and prove that such a decomposition exists and is unique.

A canonical decomposition theorem in higher dimensions has been developed by Choi: for closed real projective n-manifolds he established a canonical decomposition into (n−1)-convex pieces and concave affine pieces (math/9804110, Mémoires SMF 1999), and for closed affine 3-manifolds specifically, "Convex and concave decompositions of affine 3-manifolds" (Bull. Soc. 2020) proves that such a manifold is either an affine Hopf 3-manifold or decomposes canonically into concave affine submanifolds with incompressible boundary, toral π-submanifolds, and 2-convex affine manifolds. This provides a 3-dimensional analogue, though a decomposition fully parallel to the surface case (purely into "elementary" pieces and properly convex pieces) is not established in the same clean form, so the problem is partially solved.

Consider a one-dimensional Fermi–Pasta–Ulam–Tsingou (FPUT) chain of N classical oscillators with Hamiltonian
  H = Σ_{i=1}^{N} p_i^2/2 + Σ_{i=0}^{N} [ (1/2)(q_{i+1}-q_i)^2 + (α/3)(q_{i+1}-q_i)^3 + (β/4)(q_{i+1}-q_i)^4 ],
with fixed boundary conditions q_0 = q_{N+1} = 0. To drive the chain out of equilibrium, attach to a set of N_L oscillators on the left end a thermostat at temperature T_L and to a set of N_R oscillators on the right end a thermostat at temperature T_R < T_L (e.g. Langevin baths with friction γ, Nosé–Hoover baths, or stochastic collision baths characterized by a bath–chain coupling strength γ). Define the steady-state heat flux J(N; γ, N_L, N_R, protocol) measured by averaging the local current j_i = (1/2)(p_i + p_{i+1})·V'(q_{i+1}-q_i) in the bulk.

It is known that for such chains the finite-size thermal conductivity κ(N) = J(N) N/(T_L−T_R) diverges as N^α with an anomalous exponent α ∈ (0,1) in the asymptotic limit N → ∞.

Problem. Quantitatively characterize how the choice of thermostatting protocol — specifically the number N_L, N_R of thermostatted oscillators, the bath–chain coupling strength γ, and the type of thermostat — controls the finite-size corrections to the asymptotic scaling J(N) ~ N^{α−1}. In particular:
(a) Derive (analytically or via a controlled hydrodynamic/boundary-resistance analysis) the leading correction term in an expansion J(N) = N^{α−1}[A(γ, N_L, N_R) + B(γ, N_L, N_R) N^{−δ} + …], identifying δ > 0 and the dependence of A, B on the thermostat parameters.
(b) Determine which simulation protocols (choices of γ, N_L, N_R, and thermostat type) minimize finite-size corrections so that the asymptotic anomalous regime is reached at the smallest N, and prove that the extracted exponent α is independent of the protocol.
(c) Establish a procedure that remains reliable uniformly as N varies over several orders of magnitude.

Let $S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus $g \geq 2$ equipped with a real flat projective structure, i.e., a $(\mathrm{PGL}(3,\mathbb{R}), \mathbb{RP}^2)$-structure: a maximal atlas of charts into $\mathbb{RP}^2$ whose transition maps are restrictions of projective transformations. A celebrated theorem of S. Choi asserts that any such real projective structure on $S$ admits a canonical decomposition along a (possibly empty) disjoint union of simple closed curves into maximal convex sub-surfaces (the "convex/concave" decomposition), and Choi's proof of this decomposition is topological/combinatorial in nature.

Question: Provide an analytic proof of this decomposition theorem. More specifically, construct a geometric flow on the space of real projective structures on $S$ (or on associated geometric data such as developing maps, projective connections, or equivariant immersions) whose long-time behavior produces Choi's canonical decomposition of an arbitrary real flat projective structure into its maximal convex pieces along simple closed curves.

Let $M^n \subset \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ be a smooth, locally strictly convex hypersurface (so that its second fundamental form is definite and the Blaschke/equiaffine structure is well defined). At each point $p \in M$, the affine (Blaschke) normal vector $\xi(p)$ is the transverse vector field uniquely characterized by the conditions that (i) it induces the equiaffine volume form coinciding with the volume form of the affine metric (Berwald–Blaschke metric) $h$ obtained from the second fundamental form normalized by $|\det II|^{1/(n+2)}$, and (ii) the induced volume form is parallel with respect to the induced connection. Equivalently, if $M$ is locally given as a graph $x_{n+1} = f(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ with $\det(\partial^2 f) \ne 0$, the affine normal can be expressed in terms of $f$ and its first and second derivatives via classical formulas involving $|\det(\partial^2 f)|^{-1/(n+2)}$ and the inverse Hessian.

Devise an efficient numerical algorithm that, given access to a point $p \in M$ and to local first- and second-order data of $M$ near $p$ (for example, samples of a defining function or of a graph parametrization), computes an accurate approximation of the affine normal vector $\xi(p)$, with computational cost and numerical stability that remain practical when the ambient dimension $n+1$ is large. Analyze the conditioning, complexity, and error of such an algorithm.

Consider a one-dimensional chain of N classical particles with unit mass and nearest-neighbor interaction, governed by the Hamiltonian
  H = sum_{i=1}^{N} p_i^2/2 + sum_{i} V(q_{i+1} - q_i),
where the pair potential V is taken close to an integrable limit. Two canonical near-integrable settings are:
 (a) a perturbed harmonic chain, V(r) = (1/2) r^2 + epsilon U(r), with U a generic anharmonic potential and epsilon a small parameter;
 (b) a perturbed Toda chain, V(r) = V_Toda(r) + epsilon W(r), where V_Toda(r) = (a/b) e^{-b r} + a r (up to constants) is the integrable Toda potential and W is a generic non-Toda perturbation.
Place the chain in contact with two heat baths at temperatures T_L and T_R = T_L + Delta T at its ends, and let J(L) denote the steady-state heat flux as a function of the chain length L = N a (a the lattice spacing).

It is expected that, as L is increased, three regimes appear:
 (i) Ballistic regime for L < ell(epsilon): J is essentially independent of L.
 (ii) Kinetic / apparently diffusive finite-size regime for ell(epsilon) < L < ell_c(epsilon): J ~ 1/L (Fourier-like behavior).
 (iii) Asymptotic anomalous regime for L > ell_c(epsilon): the anomalous component J_A ~ L^{delta - 1} dominates, with some exponent delta in (0,1) characteristic of the universality class of FPUT-type chains.

The problem is to determine the two characteristic crossover length scales ell(epsilon) and ell_c(epsilon) and their dependence on the strength epsilon of the integrability-breaking perturbation, in both settings (a) and (b). In particular:
 1. Derive ell(epsilon), interpreted as a typical mean free path of the relevant quasiparticles (phonons in case (a), Toda solitons in case (b)), as a function of epsilon (e.g. determine whether ell(epsilon) ~ epsilon^{-alpha} for some alpha and identify alpha).
 2. Derive the second crossover scale ell_c(epsilon) > ell(epsilon) at which the anomalous hydrodynamic contribution overtakes the apparent diffusive behavior, again as a function of epsilon.
 3. Identify conditions under which the intermediate diffusive window (ii) is absent, so that the system crosses over directly from ballistic to anomalous transport.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question of the crossover length scales between ballistic, kinetic/diffusive, and anomalous regimes in near-integrable FPUT-type chains is treated as an open problem in current reviews. Partial results exist: scaling arguments (Lepri, Livi, Politi and collaborators; Di Cintio et al., PRL 125, 040604 (2020)) give heuristic estimates of the mean-free-path scale and indicate that a direct ballistic-to-anomalous crossover can arise from singular dependence of the anomalous transport coefficient. Recent works on weak integrability-breaking perturbations of Toda and on Lyapunov spectra of weakly nonintegrable FPUT/Toda dynamics (2024–2026) continue to investigate these scales, but a complete derivation of both ell(epsilon) and ell_c(epsilon) for general perturbations of the harmonic and Toda chains has not been established.

Background and definitions. Let $f: M^n \to \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ be a smooth, locally strongly convex hypersurface. There is a canonical transversal vector field $\xi$ on $M$, called the affine normal, determined (up to sign) by the requirements of equiaffine differential geometry (using the Blaschke metric induced by the second fundamental form normalized by the affine invariant). The hypersurface is called an affine sphere if all affine normals either pass through a single point (the center) or are mutually parallel. An affine sphere is called hyperbolic if the affine normals all point away from a common center on the concave side of the hypersurface; equivalently, after a suitable affine change of coordinates, $M$ can be written locally as the graph of a strongly convex function $u$ on a domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ satisfying the Monge–Ampère equation
$$\det(\partial_i \partial_j u) = \left(-\frac{1}{u}\right)^{n+2},$$
with $u < 0$ in $\Omega$ and $u = 0$ on $\partial \Omega$.

A convex cone $C \subset \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ is a nonempty open convex subset such that $\lambda x \in C$ for every $x \in C$ and every $\lambda > 0$, and which contains no entire line. A complete hyperbolic affine sphere $M$ is said to be asymptotic to the cone $C$ if $M$ is contained in $C$, is properly embedded, and the closure of $M$ in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ has boundary equal to $\partial C \cup \{0\}$.

Problem. Prove that for every convex cone $C \subset \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ (with vertex at the origin and containing no line), and every prescribed negative constant value of the affine mean curvature, there exists a complete hyperbolic affine sphere asymptotic to $C$ with that affine mean curvature.

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

Calabi's conjecture on the existence (and uniqueness) of a complete hyperbolic affine hypersphere asymptotic to any given non-degenerate convex cone was resolved by Cheng and Yau via their work on the real Monge–Ampère equation, with later refinements/alternative proofs by Li, Gigena, and others. The statement is now an established theorem.

Background and notation. Let M be a smooth closed connected manifold of dimension n, and let TM denote its tangent bundle. A connection ∇ on a vector bundle E → M is called flat if its curvature 2-form vanishes identically; equivalently, E admits a system of local trivializations with locally constant transition functions. Write χ(M) for the Euler characteristic of M and, for an oriented real vector bundle V of even rank, χ(V) for its Euler number (the integral of the Euler class over the base).

A theorem of Milnor asserts: if V is an oriented rank‑2 vector bundle over a closed orientable surface Σ_g of genus g ≥ 1 and V admits a flat connection, then |χ(Σ_g)| ≤ −(1/2)χ(V); in particular, for V = TΣ_g this forces no constraint beyond the flatness obstruction on the surface.

Problem. Investigate higher-dimensional analogues of Milnor's inequality for flat vector bundles over closed manifolds. Specifically, decide the following question:

Let M be a closed smooth manifold of dimension n ≥ 3 such that the tangent bundle TM admits a flat linear connection (curvature zero, torsion not assumed to vanish). Must χ(M) = 0?

If the answer is negative in general, determine under what additional natural hypotheses (e.g. the flat connection being torsion-free, i.e. M being an affine manifold) the conclusion χ(M) = 0 does hold.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Without the torsion-free assumption the question is settled negatively: Smillie (1977) constructed, in every even dimension n ≥ 4, closed manifolds whose tangent bundle admits a flat connection (with nonzero torsion) and whose Euler characteristic is nonzero. The torsion-free (affine) version, known as Chern's conjecture for affine manifolds — that a closed affine manifold has χ(M) = 0 — remains generally open, although it is established in special cases (e.g. special/unimodular affine manifolds by Klingler 2017, and complete affine manifolds by Kostant–Sullivan).

Let $X$ and $Y$ be (complex) Banach spaces and let $U \subset X$ be an open set. Consider an unknown operator $F : U \to Y$ that is holomorphic, i.e., Fréchet-differentiable in the complex sense on $U$, and assume $F$ lies in a suitable class $\mathcal{H}(U,Y)$ of bounded holomorphic operators. Given i.i.d. samples $\{(x_i, F(x_i))\}_{i=1}^n$ drawn from a probability measure $\mu$ on $U$ (the noiseless setting, i.e., outputs are observed exactly), one constructs an estimator $\widehat{F}_n$ via empirical risk minimization (ERM) over a hypothesis class $\mathcal{N}$ of neural operators of the form $\widehat{F} = \mathcal{D} \circ \Psi_\theta \circ \mathcal{E}$, where $\mathcal{E} : X \to \mathbb{R}^{d_E}$ is an encoder, $\mathcal{D} : \mathbb{R}^{d_D} \to Y$ is a decoder, and $\Psi_\theta : \mathbb{R}^{d_E} \to \mathbb{R}^{d_D}$ is a fully trainable feed-forward neural network whose every weight and bias is a free parameter optimized during training (as opposed to schemes in which $\Psi_\theta$ is partially fixed or only certain layers are trainable). The estimator solves
$$\widehat{F}_n \in \arg\min_{\widehat{F} \in \mathcal{N}} \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \|\widehat{F}(x_i) - F(x_i)\|_Y^2.$$
Define the worst-case expected $L^2(\mu;Y)$ generalization error
$$R_n := \sup_{F \in \mathcal{H}(U,Y)} \mathbb{E}\, \|\widehat{F}_n - F\|_{L^2(\mu;Y)}^2.$$
Question: Does there exist a choice of architecture $\mathcal{N}$ (with size possibly depending on $n$) such that the fully trainable ERM scheme achieves a convergence rate strictly faster than the Monte Carlo rate, i.e.,
$$R_n = o(n^{-1/2}) \quad \text{as } n \to \infty,$$
or is every fully trainable ERM scheme limited to a rate no faster than $n^{-1/2}$ on the class of holomorphic operators in the noiseless regime?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

This is Chern's conjecture (1955) for affine manifolds. It is known in special cases: dimension 2 (Benzécri, Milnor), complete affine manifolds (Kostant–Sullivan), special/unimodular affine manifolds (Klingler, 2017), and certain fundamental-group classes (Hirsch–Thurston, 1975). A 2020 preprint by Feng–Zhang claimed a general proof but was found flawed and retracted; the conjecture remains open in general as of 2026.

Let X and Y be separable Banach spaces and let K be a class of (possibly nonlinear) target operators F : X → Y. For an integer n ≥ 1 define the noiseless nonlinear sampling width

  s_n(K)_X := inf_{φ_1,…,φ_n ∈ X*, R : ℝ^n → Y} sup_{F ∈ K} sup_{x ∈ B_X} ‖F(x) − R(φ_1(x),…,φ_n(x); x)‖_Y,

where the infimum is over all choices of n bounded linear measurement functionals on X and all (possibly nonlinear) reconstruction maps R, and B_X is the unit ball of X.

For a noise level σ ≥ 0 and tail parameter η ∈ (0,1), define the noisy statistical nonlinear sampling width s̃_n^η(K; σ)_X as the smallest ε > 0 such that there exist measurement functionals φ_1,…,φ_n ∈ X* and a (possibly randomized) reconstruction map R̂ for which, given noisy measurements y_i = φ_i(x) + σ ξ_i with ξ_i i.i.d. standard noise (e.g. N(0,1)) and any input x ∈ B_X, one has

  sup_{F ∈ K} sup_{x ∈ B_X} Pr[ ‖F(x) − R̂(y_1,…,y_n; x)‖_Y > ε ] ≤ η.

The problem is to obtain a sharp two-sided characterization (matching upper and lower bounds, up to absolute constants) of the noisy minimax operator-learning rate s̃_n^η(K; σ)_X in terms of the noiseless width s_n(K)_X, the noise level σ, the sample size n, and the geometric/complexity parameters of the class K. In particular, identify the explicit dependence on σ that interpolates between the noiseless rate (σ = 0) and the noise-dominated regime, in analogy with the noise-aware minimax theory available for classical function approximation.

An affine flat structure on a smooth manifold $M^n$ is a maximal atlas of charts $\{(U_\alpha, \varphi_\alpha)\}$ with $\varphi_\alpha : U_\alpha 	o \mathbb{R}^n$ whose transition maps $\varphi_ eta \circ \varphi_\alpha^{-1}$ are restrictions of affine transformations $x \mapsto Ax + b$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ (with $A \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{R})$, $b \in \mathbb{R}^n$). Equivalently, $M$ admits a torsion-free flat affine connection on its tangent bundle. A hyperbolic 3-manifold is a complete Riemannian 3-manifold of constant sectional curvature $-1$; equivalently, a quotient $\Gamma  ackslash \mathbb{H}^3$ where $\Gamma \subset \mathrm{Isom}(\mathbb{H}^3)$ is a discrete torsion-free subgroup.

In dimension $2$, a result of Milnor implies that a closed surface admits an affine flat structure if and only if its Euler characteristic is zero; in particular, no closed hyperbolic surface admits an affine flat structure.

Problem. Prove that no closed hyperbolic 3-manifold admits an affine flat structure. That is, show that for every closed orientable 3-manifold $M$ carrying a complete hyperbolic Riemannian metric, the tangent bundle of $M$ does not admit any torsion-free flat affine connection.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The Markus conjecture (1962) remains widely open in general. One direction (completeness implies existence of a parallel volume form, in the compact case) is classical, but the converse is established only under additional hypotheses: e.g., Carrière's theorem for Lorentzian holonomy, results of Goldman–Hirsch for solvable holonomy of suitable rank, the convex case in low dimensions (Jo–Kim), and recent work on three-manifolds with centralizing holonomy. In dimension ≥ 3 the full conjecture is unresolved.

Let $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{Y}$ be separable Hilbert spaces and let $\varrho$ be a Borel probability measure on $\mathcal{X}$. For an operator $F:\mathcal{X}	o\mathcal{Y}$ define the $L^2_\varrho$-norm by $\|F\|_{L^2_\varrho}^2 := \int_{\mathcal{X}} \|F(x)\|_{\mathcal{Y}}^2\, d\varrho(x)$.

Let $K\subset L^2_\varrho(\mathcal{X};\mathcal{Y})$ be a compact class of operators. Consider an i.i.d. noisy sampling model: a learner queries inputs $x_1,\dots,x_n$ drawn i.i.d. from $\varrho$ and receives observations $y_i = F(x_i) + \xi_i$, where $\xi_i$ are i.i.d. centered noise variables on $\mathcal{Y}$ with noise level $\sigma>0$ (e.g.\ Gaussian with covariance $\sigma^2 I$). Allowing arbitrary (possibly nonlinear and randomized) reconstruction maps $\Phi_n$ that produce an estimator $\widehat F = \Phi_n((x_i,y_i)_{i=1}^n)$, define the statistical nonlinear sampling $n$-width
$$	ilde s_n^{\eta}(K;\sigma)_{L^2_\varrho} := \inf_{\Phi_n}\sup_{F\in K}  ig(\mathbb{E}\,\|F-\widehat F\|_{L^2_\varrho}^2 ig)^{1/2},$$
where $\eta$ encodes the noise model.

Now let $K$ be a holomorphic operator class of the following type. Fix a sequence $ oldsymbol{b}=(b_j)_{j\ge 1}\in \ell^p(\mathbb{N})$ for some $0<p<1$, and let $K=K( oldsymbol{b},\mathcal{Y})$ consist of all operators $F:\mathcal{X}	o\mathcal{Y}$ that admit a holomorphic extension to a Bernstein-type polyellipse $\mathcal{E}_{ oldsymbol{ho}}\supset \mathcal{X}$ with parameters controlled by $ oldsymbol{b}$, and that are uniformly bounded on this polyellipse. (These are the standard $( oldsymbol{b},\varepsilon)$-holomorphic classes for which deterministic adaptive $n$-widths in $L^2_\varrho$ are known to decay at rate $n^{-(1/p-1/2)}$, faster than the Monte-Carlo rate $n^{-1/2}$.)

Problem. Determine sharp upper and lower bounds (matching up to constants and logarithmic factors) for $	ilde s_n^{\eta}(K;\sigma)_{L^2_\varrho}$ as $n	o\infty$ for these holomorphic classes $K$. In particular, decide whether, in the presence of nontrivial sampling noise of level $\sigma>0$, the rate of $	ilde s_n^{\eta}(K;\sigma)_{L^2_\varrho}$ can still be strictly faster than the Monte-Carlo rate $n^{-1/2}$, or whether noise forces the rate to be $\Omega(n^{-1/2})$.

An affine structure on a smooth manifold $M$ is a maximal atlas of charts with values in $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose transition maps are restrictions of affine transformations of $\mathbb{R}^n$ (elements of $\mathrm{GL}(n,\mathbb{R})\ltimes\mathbb{R}^n$). Equivalently, it is a torsion-free flat affine connection on $M$. To each such structure on a connected manifold one associates a developing map $\mathrm{dev}\colon \widetilde{M}\to\mathbb{R}^n$ and a holonomy homomorphism $\rho\colon\pi_1(M)\to\mathrm{Aff}(\mathbb{R}^n)$, well defined up to conjugation. Two affine structures are equivalent if they are related by a diffeomorphism of $M$ preserving the affine atlases (isotopy is also a natural equivalence).

Let $\mathbf{T}^3=\mathbb{R}^3/\mathbb{Z}^3$ be the 3-dimensional torus. Provide a classification, up to equivalence, of all affine structures on $\mathbf{T}^3$ (not assumed complete), describing the moduli space of such structures together with their holonomy representations $\rho\colon\mathbb{Z}^3\to\mathrm{Aff}(\mathbb{R}^3)$ and developing images.

Let $\Sigma_g$ denote a closed orientable surface of genus $g \geq 2$, and let $S^1$ denote the circle. A complete affine structure on a smooth manifold $M^n$ is an atlas of charts into $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose transition maps are restrictions of affine transformations of $\mathbb{R}^n$, such that the developing map $\widetilde{M} \to \mathbb{R}^n$ is a diffeomorphism (equivalently, $M$ is affinely diffeomorphic to a quotient $\mathbb{R}^n/\Gamma$ where $\Gamma$ is a discrete subgroup of the affine group $\mathrm{Aff}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ acting properly discontinuously and freely on $\mathbb{R}^n$).

Prove or disprove: for every integer $g \geq 2$, the closed 3-manifold $\Sigma_g \times S^1$ admits no complete affine structure.

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

Closed 3-manifolds admitting complete affine structures were classified by Fried and Goldman: such a manifold must be finitely covered by a 2-torus bundle over the circle (i.e., its geometry is Euclidean, Nil, or Sol). Since $\Sigma_g \times S^1$ for $g \geq 2$ has a fundamental group that is not virtually polycyclic, it does not appear in this classification, so it cannot admit a complete affine structure. The conjecture therefore follows from the Fried–Goldman classification.

Let $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{Y}$ be separable infinite-dimensional Banach spaces (for instance, function spaces on bounded domains in Euclidean space), and let $\mathcal{F}\subset\{G:\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{Y}\}$ denote a target class of nonlinear operators. Classical operator-learning theory studies classes $\mathcal{F}$ defined through regularity assumptions on $G$, such as Lipschitz continuity, $C^k$-smoothness, Sobolev/Besov regularity on suitable encodings, or holomorphic/analytic dependence on parameters; for such classes one derives quantitative approximation rates and statistical learning bounds for neural-operator surrogates (e.g. DeepONet, Fourier neural operators, PCA-net, random feature operators).

Define an "architecture-oriented" operator class as follows. Fix a parametric family of neural-operator architectures
$$\mathcal{N} = \{\Phi_\theta:\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{Y} \mid \theta\in\Theta_n,\ n\in\mathbb{N}\},$$
indexed by a complexity parameter $n$ (e.g. number of parameters, width, depth, or number of trunk/branch basis functions), and a complexity functional $C:\mathcal{N}\to[0,\infty)$. For an admissible compact input set $K\subset\mathcal{X}$, a norm $\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal{Y}}$, and a rate function $\rho:\mathbb{N}\to(0,\infty)$ with $\rho(n)\to 0$, define

Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be an unbounded pseudoconvex domain (i.e., $\Omega$ is open, connected, and admits a continuous plurisubharmonic exhaustion function, but is not bounded). A Kähler metric $g$ on $\Omega$ is called Kähler-Einstein if its Ricci form satisfies $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = c\,\omega_g$ for some real constant $c$, where $\omega_g$ is the Kähler form of $g$; the metric is complete if the underlying Riemannian metric is geodesically complete.

For bounded pseudoconvex domains in $\mathbb{C}^n$, it is classical (Cheng–Yau, Mok–Yau) that a unique complete Kähler-Einstein metric of negative Ricci curvature always exists. The problem is to determine the analogous existence theory in the unbounded setting:

Find necessary and sufficient conditions on an unbounded pseudoconvex domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ which guarantee that $\Omega$ admits a complete Kähler-Einstein metric.

A combinatorial torus structure of dimension n is a simplicial (or cubical/PL) decomposition of the n-dimensional torus T^n = R^n/Z^n, with associated 1-skeleton viewed as a finite graph G embedded in T^n. The complement T^n \ G of such a graph in the torus is said to admit an affine structure if it can be endowed with an atlas of charts to R^n whose transition maps are restrictions of affine transformations of R^n (equivalently, a (Aff(R^n), R^n)-structure).

The problem is the following:

(a) Show that, for each fixed dimension n, there are only finitely many isomorphism classes of finite graphs G that arise as the 1-skeleton of a combinatorial torus structure on T^n whose complement T^n \ G admits an affine structure.

(b) Show that, for each fixed dimension n, there are only finitely many such combinatorial torus structures (up to combinatorial equivalence) whose complements admit affine structures.

(c) Give an explicit classification of all such graphs and combinatorial torus structures.

Setup. Let $D\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain and let $\varrho$ be a Borel probability measure on a separable Hilbert space $X$ of input functions on $D$ (the "data distribution"). For a target Banach space $Y$ of output functions on $D$, consider nonlinear operators $\Psi:X\to Y$, evaluated in the loss
$$\|\Psi-\widehat\Psi\|_{L^2_\varrho}^2 \;=\; \int_X \|\Psi(u)-\widehat\Psi(u)\|_Y^2\,d\varrho(u).$$

Two model classes of operators are of interest.

(1) Holomorphic class $\mathcal{H}(\boldsymbol b)\circ\iota$. Fix a sequence $\boldsymbol b=(b_j)_{j\ge 1}\in\ell^p$ for some $p\in(0,1)$, and an affine parametrization $\iota:U=[-1,1]^{\mathbb{N}}\to X$ with $\iota(\boldsymbol y)=\bar u+\sum_{j\ge 1} y_j\,\psi_j$, where $\|\psi_j\|_X\le b_j$. The class $\mathcal{H}(\boldsymbol b)$ consists of maps $f:U\to Y$ that admit a bounded holomorphic extension to a $(\boldsymbol b,\varepsilon)$-admissible Bernstein polyellipse around $U$, with uniform bound $\le 1$. Set $\mathcal{H}(\boldsymbol b)\circ\iota=\{f\circ\iota^{-1}:f\in\mathcal{H}(\boldsymbol b)\}$.

(2) Fourier neural operator class $\mathcal{K}^\alpha_{\mathrm{FNO}}$. For $\alpha>0$, $\mathcal{K}^\alpha_{\mathrm{FNO}}$ denotes the class of operators realizable as Fourier neural operators (a finite composition of affine lifting/projection layers and "Fourier layers" $v\mapsto\sigma(Wv+\mathcal{F}^{-1}(R\cdot\mathcal{F}v))$ with activation $\sigma$) whose architectural complexity (depth, width, number of retained Fourier modes, weight norms) is bounded by a budget controlled by a smoothness parameter $\alpha$.

Sampling width. For a class $\mathcal{K}$ of operators $X\to Y$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$, define the order-$n$ sampling width in $L^2_\varrho$ by
$$s_n(\mathcal{K})_{L^2_\varrho} \;=\; \inf_{u_1,\dots,u_n\in X}\;\inf_{R}\;\sup_{\Psi\in\mathcal{K}}\,\|\Psi-R(\Psi(u_1),\dots,\Psi(u_n))\|_{L^2_\varrho},$$
where $R$ ranges over all (possibly nonlinear) reconstruction maps from $Y^n$ to operators $X\to Y$.

Problem. Establish a quantitative separation between the minimax behavior of $\mathcal{H}(\boldsymbol b)\circ\iota$ and $\mathcal{K}^\alpha_{\mathrm{FNO}}$ in $L^2_\varrho$. Specifically, accomplish at least one of:

(a) Prove a lower bound on $s_n(\mathcal{K}^\alpha_{\mathrm{FNO}})_{L^2_\varrho}$ that is strictly larger (in its dependence on $n$) than the known upper bound on $s_n(\mathcal{H}(\boldsymbol b)\circ\iota)_{L^2_\varrho}$, thereby exhibiting a genuine sample-complexity gap; or

(b) Show that every operator in $\mathcal{H}(\boldsymbol b)\circ\iota$ can be approximated, with quantitative rates in $n$, by a Fourier neural operator from $\mathcal{K}^\alpha_{\mathrm{FNO}}$ (for an appropriate $\alpha=\alpha(\boldsymbol b)$), thereby showing that the FNO class essentially contains the holomorphic class.

In either case, decide whether the two classes exhibit genuinely different sample-complexity behavior in $L^2_\varrho$.

Let $X \subset \mathbb{CP}^3$ be a smooth quartic surface, i.e. the zero locus of a homogeneous polynomial of degree 4 in four complex variables that is nonsingular as a complex projective variety. Such an $X$ is a K3 surface: it is simply connected, has trivial canonical bundle $K_X \cong \mathcal{O}_X$, and admits a nowhere-vanishing holomorphic 2-form. By Yau's theorem, in every Kähler class on $X$ there exists a unique Ricci-flat Kähler metric $g$ (a Calabi–Yau metric), characterized by $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = 0$.

Problem. Exhibit, for some smooth quartic surface $X \subset \mathbb{CP}^3$ and some Kähler class $[\omega] \in H^{1,1}(X,\mathbb{R})$, an explicit closed-form expression (in terms of elementary, algebraic, or classical special functions of the ambient projective coordinates) for the Kähler potential, or equivalently the Kähler form $\omega$, of a Ricci-flat Kähler metric on $X$ representing $[\omega]$.

No explicit closed-form Ricci-flat (Calabi–Yau) metric on a smooth quartic K3 surface is known. Yau's theorem guarantees existence and uniqueness in each Kähler class, but only numerical approximations (e.g., Headrick–Wiseman and subsequent works) and asymptotic constructions near degenerations (e.g., near the Kummer/orbifold limit) are available. The problem of finding an explicit closed-form expression remains open as of 2026.

Let $A:\mathbb{R}^N\to\mathbb{R}^m$ be a linear measurement operator and let $\Sigma\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a (not necessarily convex) model set. Consider the inverse problem $y = A\hat x + e$, where $\hat x\in\Sigma$ and $e\in\mathbb{R}^m$ is a noise vector. Let $P_\Sigma:\mathbb{R}^N\to\Sigma$ be a generalized projection onto $\Sigma$ (a map satisfying $P_\Sigma(x)\in\Sigma$ for all $x$, and $P_\Sigma(x)=x$ for $x\in\Sigma$).

Define the secant set $\Sigma-\Sigma = \{x_1-x_2 : x_1,x_2\in\Sigma\}$. A linear operator $B$ is said to have restricted isometry constant $\delta(B)\in[0,1)$ on $\Sigma-\Sigma$ if
$$\|(I-B)(x_1-x_2)\|^2 \le \delta\,\|x_1-x_2\|^2 \quad \text{for all } x_1,x_2\in\Sigma.$$
The projection $P_\Sigma$ is said to satisfy a restricted Lipschitz condition with respect to $\Sigma$ if there exists a constant $C_\Sigma\ge 0$ such that
$$\|P_\Sigma(x) - P_\Sigma(x')\|\le C_\Sigma\|x-x'\| \quad \text{for appropriate pairs }(x,x'),$$
together with auxiliary control constants $\beta,\theta>0$ governing the interaction of $P_\Sigma$ with $\Sigma-\Sigma$.

Given step sizes $\mu,\lambda>0$, the classical Regularization by Denoising (RED) iterations are
$$x_{n+1} = x_n - \mu A^\top(Ax_n - y) - \lambda(x_n - P_\Sigma(x_n)).$$

Question: Under the standing assumptions that $A^\top A$ has a restricted isometry constant on $\Sigma-\Sigma$ and that $P_\Sigma$ satisfies a restricted Lipschitz property with respect to $\Sigma$, prove convergence of the RED iterates $\{x_n\}$ to a neighborhood of $\hat x$ (controlled by $\|e\|$) under hypotheses strictly less restrictive than the quasi-non-expansiveness sufficient condition
$$\delta\!\left(\tfrac{\mu}{\lambda+\theta}A^\top A\right)\beta + \tfrac{\theta}{\lambda+\theta}\,\delta\!\left(\tfrac{\mu}{\theta}A^\top A\right)C_\Sigma \le 1.$$
Equivalently, identify a weaker sufficient condition (or prove that none is needed beyond the RIC and restricted Lipschitz assumptions) guaranteeing convergence of the classical RED iteration in this non-convex model-set setting.

$$\|(I-B)(x_1-x_2)\|^2 \le \delta\,\|x_1-x_2\|^2 \quad \text{for all } x_1,x_2\in\Sigma.$$
The projection $P_\Sigma$ is said to satisfy a restricted Lipschitz condition with respect to $\Sigma$ if there exists a constant $C_\Sigma\ge 0$ such that 
$$\|P_\Sigma(x) - P_\Sigma(x')\|\le C_\Sigma\|x-x'\| \quad \text{for appropriate pairs }(x,x'),$$
together with auxiliary control constants $\beta,\theta>0$ governing the interaction of $P_\Sigma$ with $\Sigma-\Sigma$.

Given step sizes $\mu,\lambda>0$, the classical Regularization by Denoising (RED) iterations are
$$x_{n+1} = x_n - \mu A^\top(Ax_n - y) - \lambda(x_n - P_\Sigma(x_n)).$$

Question: Under the standing assumptions that $A^\top A$ has a restricted isometry constant on $\Sigma-\Sigma$ and that $P_\Sigma$ satisfies a restricted Lipschitz property with respect to $\Sigma$, prove convergence of the RED iterates $\{x_n\}$ to a neighborhood of $\hat x$ (controlled by $\|e\|$) under hypotheses strictly less restrictive than the quasi-non-expansiveness sufficient condition
$$\delta\!\left(\tfrac{\mu}{\lambda+\theta}A^\top A\right)\beta + \tfrac{\theta}{\lambda+\theta}\,\delta\!\left(\tfrac{\mu}{\theta}A^\top A\right)C_\Sigma \le 1.$$
Equivalently, identify a weaker sufficient condition (or prove that none is needed beyond the RIC and restricted Lipschitz assumptions) guaranteeing convergence of the classical RED iteration in this non-convex model-set setting.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The problem is explicitly posed as an open question regarding convergence of classical RED under RIC and restricted Lipschitz hypotheses in non-convex model-set recovery. No published resolution was located; existing RED convergence results rely on stronger conditions such as quasi-non-expansiveness or convex regularizers.

A K3 surface is a simply connected compact complex surface $X$ with trivial canonical bundle $K_X \cong \mathcal{O}_X$ and $h^{1}(X,\mathcal{O}_X)=0$. By Yau's solution of the Calabi conjecture, every Kähler class on $X$ contains a unique Ricci-flat Kähler metric, and any such metric is hyperkähler. Consider the set of all Ricci-flat Riemannian metrics on the underlying smooth 4-manifold of a K3 surface, taken modulo the action of the diffeomorphism group and modulo scaling.

Question: Is this set a single point? Equivalently, does the smooth 4-manifold underlying a K3 surface admit, up to diffeomorphism and rescaling, exactly one Ricci-flat Riemannian metric?

By Yau's solution of the Calabi conjecture, every Kähler class on $X$ contains a unique Ricci-flat Kähler metric, and any such metric is hyperkähler. status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

The answer is known to be negative: a K3 surface admits a large moduli space of Ricci-flat (hyperkähler) metrics, not a unique one. Yau's theorem yields uniqueness only within a fixed Kähler class on a fixed complex structure; varying the complex structure and Kähler class produces a 57-dimensional moduli space (58-dimensional including volume), whose structure has been studied (e.g., shown to be simply connected with rational cohomology of the K3 lattice automorphism group). Within a fixed Kähler class, uniqueness is a direct consequence of the Calabi–Yau theorem.

representations.normalized:
A multiparty quantum key agreement (MQKA) protocol is a cryptographic protocol in which n ≥ 3 mutually distrustful parties P_1, …, P_n, connected by quantum channels and by authenticated classical channels, jointly perform local quantum operations, measurements, and classical communication so as to produce a common bit string K ∈ {0,1}^ℓ, with the requirements that:

(i) Correctness: with high probability all honest parties output the same key K.
(ii) Fairness of contribution: every party contributes equally to K, in the sense that no proper subset S ⊊ {P_1, …, P_n} of (possibly dishonest) participants can, by itself, fix or bias the value of K beyond a negligible advantage.
(iii) External secrecy: any external eavesdropper interacting with the quantum and classical channels obtains only negligible information about K.
(iv) Robustness against insider collusion: even when up to t < n parties collude (and may share entanglement and arbitrary side information), they cannot determine, predict, or bias K beyond negligible advantage.

The problem is the following. Develop a composable security framework for MQKA, comparable in rigor and scope to the abstract-cryptography / Universal Composability style frameworks now standard for two-party quantum key distribution, satisfying all of the following:

(a) Define an ideal MQKA resource (functionality) that simultaneously formalizes external secrecy, fairness of contribution among all n parties, and resistance to arbitrary insider collusion of any subset of participants.

(b) Provide security definitions for concrete MQKA protocols expressed as the indistinguishability (in a suitable simulation-based or distinguishing-advantage sense) between the real protocol execution and the ideal MQKA resource, against adversaries that may corrupt any chosen subset of the n parties as well as the channels.

(c) Establish a composition theorem proving that any MQKA protocol meeting the above security definition can be safely used as a subroutine inside arbitrary larger cryptographic protocols, so that the resulting agreed key may be consumed by any subsequent protocol with at most a negligible loss in overall security.

(d) Exhibit at least one explicit MQKA protocol that provably realizes the ideal MQKA resource within this framework, with an explicit quantitative security bound.

Does such a composable security framework, together with a protocol realizing it, exist?

Question: Does there exist a natural geometric procedure (a "collapsing" or quotient construction reflecting degenerations such as bubbling, orbifold limits, or volume collapse with bounded curvature) that produces from $\mathcal{E}(M)$ a topological space with only finitely many connected components, in a way that is compatible with the geometry of Einstein metrics?

A Riemannian manifold $(M^n, g)$ of dimension $n \geq 2$ is called Einstein if its Ricci curvature tensor is a constant multiple of the metric, i.e. $\mathrm{Ric}_g = \lambda\, g$ for some constant $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$. Equivalently, the trace-free Ricci tensor vanishes; the constant $\lambda$ has the same sign as the scalar curvature $S_g = n\lambda$.

Provide a general construction method that produces Einstein metrics of negative scalar curvature. More precisely, describe a procedure that, given suitable topological or geometric input data (for example, a smooth manifold, possibly with additional structure such as a complex, conformal, or fibered structure), outputs a Riemannian metric $g$ on the underlying manifold satisfying $\mathrm{Ric}_g = \lambda g$ with $\lambda < 0$, in a way that is not restricted to locally homogeneous (in particular, locally symmetric) examples and that goes beyond the Aubin–Yau existence theorem for Kähler–Einstein metrics with negative first Chern class.

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

The Alekseevskii conjecture was proved by Christoph Böhm and Ramiro A. Lafuente in their work "Non-compact Einstein manifolds with symmetry" (arXiv:2107.04210), establishing that every homogeneous Einstein manifold with negative scalar curvature is diffeomorphic to a Euclidean space. Setting. Consider a multiparty quantum key agreement (MQKA) protocol in which N ≥ 3 spatially separated parties jointly generate a shared secret bit string K ∈ {0,1}^L through exchange of quantum states over noisy continuous-variable (CV) bosonic channels and authenticated classical communication. The protocol must satisfy:

(i) Correctness: with probability at least 1 − ε_c, all honest parties output the same key K.
(ii) Fairness: every honest party contributes equally to K, in the sense that no proper subset of parties can bias any bit of K.
(iii) Security: against any coalition of up to t < N dishonest parties and any external eavesdropper, the trace distance between the joint state of the key and the adversary's quantum side information and the ideal uniform-and-independent state is at most ε_s.

Bosonic encodings. For each CV mode, fix one of the following logical-qubit encodings into a single harmonic oscillator with quadratures (q̂, p̂):
 • GKP code: code states are (regularized) +1 eigenstates of the stabilizers e^{i 2√π q̂} and e^{i 2√π p̂}.
 • Cat code: even/odd superpositions of coherent states (|α⟩ ± |−α⟩)/N_±.
 • Binomial code: finite superpositions Σ_k √(C(N,k))/2^{N/2} |k(S+1)⟩ in the Fock basis with appropriate parameters (N, S).

Question. Does there exist an MQKA protocol with the following properties simultaneously?

(a) Logical-level execution: every key-generation operation (state preparation, entangling gate, measurement) is performed on logical qubits encoded in CV modes by one of the bosonic codes above.

(b) Fault tolerance: the logical Clifford operations and measurements used by the protocol admit a fault-tolerant implementation on the chosen bosonic code, with a syndrome-extraction circuit whose physical error per round is below the code's threshold.

(c) Distributed compatibility: the protocol remains executable when the N parties are connected by a network of lossy bosonic channels (transmissivity η < 1, thermal noise n̄ ≥ 0) together with local operations and classical communication, with no requirement of a central trusted node.

(d) Resource overhead: the number of physical bosonic modes, photons, and ancillas per generated secret bit is polynomial in N, log(1/ε_c), and log(1/ε_s).

(e) Fairness and security: properties (ii) and (iii) above hold with the stated parameters under a fully quantum adversary.

Provide such a protocol together with a proof of (a)–(e), or prove that no protocol simultaneously satisfying (a)–(e) exists for any of the three bosonic encodings.

Background. For a closed, oriented, smooth 4-manifold M, let χ(M) denote its Euler characteristic and τ(M) its signature. A Riemannian metric g on M is called Ricci-flat if its Ricci tensor vanishes identically, Ric(g) ≡ 0. The Hitchin–Thorpe inequality states that any closed oriented 4-manifold admitting an Einstein metric satisfies 2χ(M) ≥ 3|τ(M)|, with equality only for flat manifolds or for Ricci-flat Kähler metrics on (quotients of) the K3 surface.

Problem.
(a) Does there exist a closed, oriented, smooth 4-manifold M admitting a Ricci-flat Riemannian metric g such that the strict inequality 2χ(M) > 3|τ(M)| holds, beyond the already classically known examples (flat tori and K3-type manifolds, which lie on the equality boundary)? Equivalently, exhibit an "interesting" Ricci-flat 4-manifold satisfying this strict inequality, or prove that no such example exists.

(b) In particular, does the 4-sphere S^4 admit a Ricci-flat Riemannian metric?

Consider a software-defined quantum network modeled as a time-varying graph G(t) = (V, E(t)) whose vertices V represent quantum-capable nodes (each with a heterogeneous device profile specifying available qubit registers, gate sets, memory coherence times, measurement bases, and entanglement-generation rates) and whose edges E(t) carry quantum and classical channels with time-dependent capacities, fidelities, and latencies. A multiparty quantum key agreement (MQKA) protocol for a participant set S ⊆ V is an interactive procedure that outputs a common secret key k_S known to every member of S such that (i) every participant contributes equally to k_S (fairness), (ii) k_S is information-theoretically secret against any external eavesdropper and against any proper subset of dishonest insiders up to a specified threshold t < |S|, and (iii) the protocol terminates within a prescribed latency bound τ_S using only resources available on the induced subnetwork.

Let Π = {π_1, π_2, …} be a (possibly infinite) library of MQKA protocols, each π_i specified by its participant-size range, required topology (e.g. star, ring, complete, GHZ-distribution tree), per-round quantum and classical resource cost, achievable fairness model, security threshold, and latency profile.

Design a control-plane decision procedure A that, given as input
  • the current network state G(t) together with per-node device profiles,
  • a request (S, τ_S, σ_S, φ_S) consisting of a participant set S, a latency budget τ_S, a security level σ_S, and a fairness requirement φ_S,
  • a history H of past protocol executions with measured performance metrics,
outputs in polynomial time
  (a) a selected protocol π* ∈ Π (or a synthesized protocol expressed as a circuit/message-flow program),
  (b) a routing assignment of the quantum and classical messages of π* onto the edges of G(t),
  (c) a schedule that coexists with all other concurrently admitted MQKA sessions without enabling key-reuse attacks or violating resource contention constraints,
such that the realized execution of π* on G(t) provably satisfies the requested fairness, security threshold, and latency bound, and is competitive (within a guaranteed multiplicative factor) with the optimal offline choice over Π for the same request.

Does such a decision procedure A exist, and if so, what are the achievable competitive ratios and complexity bounds? In particular, is the joint problem of automated MQKA selection, routing, scheduling, and on-the-fly protocol synthesis decidable, and is it tractable under realistic resource and adversary models?

Let $X$ be a complete (non-compact) Kähler surface, possibly equipped with a Kähler–Einstein metric, and let $c_1$ and $c_2$ denote the first and second Chern forms associated with the Kähler metric. On a compact Kähler surface without boundary, the Chern numbers $\int_X c_1^2$ and $\int_X c_2$ are topological invariants. On a complete non-compact Kähler surface, the corresponding integrals $\int_X c_1^2$ and $\int_X c_2$ in general fail to be topological and pick up additional "boundary" contributions coming from the asymptotic geometry at infinity.

Determine, in explicit geometric and topological terms, the boundary contributions that appear in the Chern numbers $\int_X c_1^2$ and $\int_X c_2$ of a complete Kähler surface. In particular, give an explicit formula expressing these Chern integrals as a sum of a topological term and a boundary (asymptotic) term in the case where the metric on $X$ is Kähler–Einstein.

Consider a twin-field multiparty quantum key agreement (TF-MQKA) protocol defined as follows. Let n ≥ 3 mutually distrustful parties P_1, …, P_n each prepare phase-encoded weak coherent pulses |α e^{iϕ_k}⟩ with chosen phases ϕ_k ∈ [0, 2π), and transmit them through lossy quantum channels to a single central interference (measurement) station, treated as an untrusted relay. The station performs single-photon interference measurements whose detection statistics depend on the global phase combination e^{i(ϕ_1 + ⋯ + ϕ_n)}, and announces classical outcomes from which the parties distill a shared secret key K such that K is a symmetric function of (ϕ_1, …, ϕ_n).

Call the protocol strongly fair if no proper subset S ⊊ {1, …, n} of colluding parties can bias, predetermine, or learn nontrivial information about the final key K beyond what a single honest party contributes; that is, the distribution of K conditioned on any choice of inputs by S remains uniformly determined by the contributions of the honest parties. Call the protocol secure under an untrusted relay if no strategy by the central station (including arbitrary measurements and classical announcements) leaks information about K to an eavesdropper above a vanishing bound, and call it robust to multi-photon events if the security and key-rate analysis remains valid when two or more parties simultaneously contribute photons to the interference.

Problem: Construct, for arbitrary n, a TF-MQKA protocol of the above form that simultaneously
(i) achieves strong fairness against any coalition of up to n − 1 dishonest parties,
(ii) is provably secure against an untrusted central station,
(iii) correctly accounts for multi-photon contributions from multiple parties in its security proof, and
(iv) preserves the single-photon-interference distance-scaling advantage of two-party twin-field QKD (i.e. key rate scaling as O(√η) in the total channel transmittance η rather than O(η)),
or else prove that no such protocol can satisfy all four properties for sufficiently large n.

Consider a multiparty quantum key agreement (MQKA) protocol involving N ≥ 3 parties who wish to jointly establish a shared secret key such that (i) every participant contributes equally to the final key (fairness: no proper subset of parties can predetermine the key), and (ii) the protocol is secure against both external eavesdroppers and dishonest internal participants (with security quantified, e.g., by an exponentially small trace distance between the real protocol output and an ideal uniformly random key conditioned on the adversary's quantum side information). Standard MQKA protocols use qubit (d = 2) carriers. A high-dimensional MQKA protocol replaces these qubits with d-level qudits (d ≥ 3), encoding key information in mutually unbiased bases of ℂ^d and distributing multipartite entangled qudit states (e.g., generalized GHZ states |GHZ_d^N⟩ = (1/√d) Σ_{j=0}^{d-1} |j⟩^{⊗N}) among the N parties.

Problem. Design and rigorously analyze a high-dimensional MQKA protocol with the following properties, or prove that no such protocol exists under reasonable physical assumptions:

(a) For a fixed number M of transmitted quantum carriers and a fixed channel noise model (e.g., depolarizing channel with single-qudit error rate p, or a multipartite analogue), the asymptotic secret-key rate R(d, N, p) (bits of secure shared key per transmitted carrier) strictly exceeds the corresponding rate R(2, N, p) achievable by any qubit-based MQKA protocol on the same network, for some non-trivial regime of p.

Consider a multiparty quantum key agreement (MQKA) protocol involving N ≥ 3 parties who wish to jointly establish a shared secret key such that (i) every participant contributes equally to the final key (fairness: no proper subset of parties can predetermine the key), and (ii) the protocol is secure against both external eavesdroppers and dishonest internal participants (with security quantified, e.g., by an exponentially small trace distance between the real protocol output and an ideal uniformly random key conditioned on the adversary's quantum side information). A high-dimensional MQKA protocol replaces these qubits with d-level qudits (d ≥ 3), encoding key information in mutually unbiased bases of ℂ^d and distributing multipartite entangled qudit states (e.g., generalized GHZ states |GHZ_d^N⟩ = (1/√d) Σ_{j=0}^{d-1} |j⟩^{⊗N}) among the N parties.

The question is posed as an open research direction in multiparty quantum key agreement. While individual high-dimensional QKD and some bipartite/multiparty qudit-based key agreement schemes have been proposed in the literature, no comprehensive, fairness-preserving, composably secure high-dimensional MQKA protocol with a proven advantage in noise tolerance and key rate over qubit MQKA appears to be established. The status is best described as open.

Let $G \sim G(n, 1/2)$ denote the Erdős–Rényi random graph on the vertex set $\{1, \dots, n\}$ in which every edge of the complete graph $K_n$ is included independently with probability $1/2$. For a finite simple graph $H = (V, E)$, the Lovász theta number $\vartheta(H)$ is defined by
$$\vartheta(H) = \max \sum_{i,j \in V} \langle u_i, u_j \rangle,$$
where the maximum ranges over all unit vectors $c \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and families $(u_i)_{i \in V}$ of vectors in $\mathbb{R}^d$ (for any dimension $d \ge 1$) satisfying $\langle u_i, u_i \rangle = \langle c, u_i \rangle$ for every $i \in V$ and $\langle u_i, u_j \rangle = 0$ for every edge $\{i,j\} \in E$. Equivalently, $\vartheta(H)$ is the optimum of the standard semidefinite program associated with the Lovász number.

Prove or disprove the following asymptotic: as $n \to \infty$,
$$\mathbb{E}\,\vartheta(G) = (1 + o(1))\sqrt{n}.$$

Let $(M,\omega)$ be a closed symplectically aspherical symplectic manifold; that is, $\omega|_{\pi_2(M)}=0$ and $c_1(TM)|_{\pi_2(M)}=0$. A particular case of interest is the standard symplectic torus $(\mathbb{T}^{2n},\omega_0)$, where $\omega_0=\sum_{i=1}^n dx_i\wedge dy_i$ on $\mathbb{R}^{2n}/\mathbb{Z}^{2n}$.

Let $\varphi\colon M\to M$ be a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism, i.e. the time-one map of a (time-dependent) Hamiltonian flow generated by a smooth function $H\colon S^1\times M\to\mathbb{R}$. A periodic orbit of $\varphi$ of period $k\in\mathbb{N}$ is a fixed point of $\varphi^k$; it is called primitive if $k$ is the minimal such integer. Two primitive periodic orbits are geometrically distinct if their underlying sets of points in $M$ are different. For $N\in\mathbb{N}$, denote by $P(\varphi,N)$ the number of geometrically distinct primitive periodic orbits of $\varphi$ of period at most $N$.

Question: Suppose $\varphi$ has infinitely many geometrically distinct primitive periodic orbits. Is it true that there exists a constant $c=c(\varphi)>0$ such that
$$P(\varphi,N)\ \ge\ c\,N^2$$
for all sufficiently large $N$? Resolve this in the case $M=\mathbb{T}^{2n}$ and, more generally, for arbitrary closed symplectically aspherical $(M,\omega)$.

For closed symplectically aspherical manifolds, the Conley conjecture (existence of infinitely many periodic orbits for every Hamiltonian diffeomorphism) is established by Ginzburg and Hingston–Salamon–Hofer. Quantitative refinements give only generic results: for a $C^\infty$-generic Hamiltonian diffeomorphism the number of geometrically distinct primitive periodic orbits of period $\le N$ grows at least like $N/\log N$. A universal quadratic lower bound for every Hamiltonian diffeomorphism with infinitely many periodic orbits, including on the standard torus $\mathbb{T}^{2n}$, does not appear to have been established and is reported as open in recent surveys on Hamiltonian dynamics.

(b) More strongly, must $(M,\omega)$ be symplectomorphic to $(\mathbb{CP}^n,\omega_{\rm FS})$, where $\omega_{\rm FS}$ denotes the Fubini–Study symplectic form?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question is posed as an open problem in the area of positive sectional curvature within compatible symplectic/almost-Kähler geometry. Standard results (e.g., Synge-type theorems, Berger-type rigidity) constrain such manifolds, and the analogous Hopf-type conjecture for Kähler manifolds with positive sectional curvature is itself unresolved in general. No published proof was found that resolves either the diffeomorphism or symplectomorphism version of the question for almost-Kähler metrics, so it appears to remain open.

Let $(M^{2n}, \omega)$ be a symplectic manifold and $H: M \to \mathbb{R}$ a smooth Hamiltonian whose flow $\varphi_H^t$ is completely integrable, in the sense that there exist $n$ functionally independent Poisson-commuting smooth first integrals. A periodic orbit of $\varphi_H^t$ with prime period $T>0$ is called primitive, and two such orbits are geometrically distinct if their images in $M$ differ. For each $T>0$, let
$$N(T) \;=\; \#\bigl\{\text{geometrically distinct primitive periodic orbits of }\varphi_H^t\text{ with prime period} \le T\bigr\}.$$

Question. Does there exist a completely integrable Hamiltonian $H_0$ together with a smooth perturbation $H_\varepsilon = H_0 + \varepsilon K$ (with $\varepsilon$ small) such that the perturbed flow $\varphi_{H_\varepsilon}^t$ has exactly quadratic growth of its counting function, that is, there are constants $0 < c_1 \le c_2 < \infty$ with
$$c_1 T^2 \;\le\; N(T) \;\le\; c_2 T^2 \quad\text{for all sufficiently large } T?$$

Equivalently, can one perturb an integrable Hamiltonian system so as to produce examples in which the number of geometrically distinct primitive periodic orbits grows precisely quadratically (and not faster) in the period?

Setup. For a real matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times M}$ with rows $A_1,\dots,A_N$, and for any subset $S\subseteq [N]:=\{1,\dots,N\}$, let $A_S\in\mathbb{R}^{|S|\times M}$ denote the submatrix of rows indexed by $S$, and let $\sigma_M(A_S)$ denote its smallest (i.e., $M$-th) singular value (with $\sigma_M(A_S)=0$ when $|S|<M$). Define the stability quantity
$$\omega(A)\;=\;\min_{\substack{S\subseteq[N]\\ \operatorname{rank}(A_{S^c})<M}}\sigma_M(A_S),$$
where $S^c=[N]\setminus S$.

Specialize to $N=2M-1$, and consider the conjecture: there exist universal constants $C>0$ and $0<\beta<1$ such that for every $M\ge 2$ and every $A\in\mathbb{R}^{(2M-1)\times M}$ in which every $M$ rows are linearly independent,
$$\omega(A)\;\le\;C\,\max_{k\in[N]}\|A_k\|\,\beta^M.$$

Question. Let $A\in\mathbb{R}^{(2M-1)\times M}$ have i.i.d. standard Gaussian entries. Determine the typical value (e.g., the order of magnitude with high probability as $M\to\infty$) of $\omega(A)$. In particular, decide whether $\omega(A)$ satisfies a bound of the form $\omega(A)\le C\,\max_k\|A_k\|\,\beta^M$ with high probability, and if so identify the optimal admissible exponent $\beta\in(0,1)$.

Let $(M,\omega)$ be a compact Kähler manifold whose Ricci curvature is everywhere positive. By Mori's bend-and-break technique (originally developed in characteristic $p$ algebraic geometry and then transferred to characteristic zero), it is known that $M$ contains a rational curve, i.e., a non-constant holomorphic map $f:\mathbb{CP}^1\to M$.

Provide a proof of this existence statement that is genuinely differential-geometric in nature, relying directly on the Kähler metric and its positive Ricci curvature (for instance via geodesics, second variation of arc length, harmonic maps, minimal surfaces, Kähler–Ricci flow, or analogous geometric tools), rather than on Mori's reduction-modulo-$p$ bend-and-break argument.

status_assertions.value: open_status:unknown

The existence of a rational curve on any compact Kähler manifold of positive Ricci curvature is established (and the manifold is in fact projective and rationally connected, by Campana–Kollár–Miyaoka–Mori). However, the standard proofs all proceed through Mori's bend-and-break argument (reduction mod $p$ or its characteristic-zero analogue). I did not find a published purely differential-geometric proof avoiding bend-and-break, so the question of giving a "more geometric" proof appears to remain open as a methodological problem, though the existence statement itself is solved.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question is widely listed as an open problem in non-negative sectional curvature. Partial results are known: every vector bundle over a compact rank-one symmetric space admits non-negative sectional curvature after Whitney-summing with a trivial bundle of sufficiently high rank, and all vector bundles over $S^4$ (and non-spin bundles over $\mathbb{CP}^2$) carry such metrics. The general question for arbitrary simply connected non-negatively curved bases remains open.

A set of orthonormal bases $B_1, \dots, B_m$ of $\mathbb{C}^d$, with $B_k = \{v_1^{(k)}, \dots, v_d^{(k)}\}$, is called a collection of mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) if for every pair of distinct bases $k \ne \ell$ and every pair of indices $i, j \in \{1, \dots, d\}$,
$$|\langle v_i^{(k)}, v_j^{(\ell)} \rangle|^2 = \frac{1}{d}.$$
For $d = 6$, it is a long-standing open question whether more than three MUBs can exist; in particular, no seven MUBs in $\mathbb{C}^6$ are known. Encode the existence of seven MUBs in $\mathbb{C}^6$ as a system of polynomial equations in the real and imaginary parts of the entries of $7 \times 6$ vectors of $\mathbb{C}^6$, consisting of:
(i) the unit-norm and orthogonality constraints making each of the seven sets of six vectors an orthonormal basis of $\mathbb{C}^6$, and
(ii) the unbiasedness constraints $|\langle v_i^{(k)}, v_j^{(\ell)} \rangle|^2 = 1/6$ for all $k \ne \ell$ and all $i,j$.

A degree-$2t$ Sum-of-Squares (SoS) refutation of this system is an identity
$$-1 = \sigma_0(x) + \sum_a \sigma_a(x)\, p_a(x),$$
where $\{p_a = 0\}$ are the polynomial constraints above (or their natural reformulation), each $\sigma_a$ is a sum of squares of real polynomials, and the total degree of every term $\sigma_0$ and $\sigma_a p_a$ is at most $2t$.

Question: Does there exist a degree-$4$ Sum-of-Squares refutation certifying that no seven mutually unbiased bases exist in $\mathbb{C}^6$?

Novikov's theorem asserts that for any two closed oriented smooth manifolds $M$ and $N$ that are homeomorphic, the rational Pontryagin classes of their tangent bundles agree under the induced isomorphism on rational cohomology; equivalently, the rational Pontryagin classes $p_i(TM) \in H^{4i}(M;\mathbb{Q})$ of a closed smooth manifold are invariants of its underlying topological manifold structure. The known proofs proceed by topological/algebraic techniques (e.g., the original argument using surgery and the introduction of a fundamental group, signature operators on Lipschitz manifolds, and approaches via sheaves and algebraic $L$-theory).

Question: Is there a proof of Novikov's theorem on the homeomorphic invariance of the rational Pontryagin classes by purely geometric methods—for instance, by means of a geometric flow (a canonically defined evolution equation on geometric data attached to the manifold) which witnesses the topological invariance of the Pontryagin classes?

Let $N$ be a complete Kähler manifold with non-negative holomorphic bisectional curvature. Must there exist a compact totally geodesic complex submanifold $M \subset N$ and a holomorphic vector bundle $V \to M$ such that $N$ is biholomorphic to the total space of $V$?

(Here, the holomorphic bisectional curvature $H(X,Y)$ for $(1,0)$-type tangent vectors $X,Y$ is the sectional-curvature-like quantity $R(X,\bar X,Y,\bar Y)/(\|X\|^2\|Y\|^2)$, and "non-negative bisectional curvature" means $H(X,Y) \ge 0$ for all such $X,Y$. A submanifold $M \subset N$ is totally geodesic if every geodesic of $N$ tangent to $M$ at a point of $M$ stays in $M$. The question asks whether every such $N$ admits a "complex soul" structure, i.e., is biholomorphically the total space of a holomorphic vector bundle over such an $M$.)

The question asks whether every such $N$ admits a "complex soul" structure, i.e., is biholomorphically the total space of a holomorphic vector bundle over such an $M$.)

While progress has been made in special cases (e.g., maximal volume growth, low dimension, or under positivity), no general proof of the full statement appears in the literature, and recent surveys treat the broader uniformization program as still ongoing.

For a prime $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, the Paley graph $G_p$ is the graph whose vertex set is the finite field $\mathbb{F}_p$, with two distinct vertices $x,y \in \mathbb{F}_p$ joined by an edge if and only if $x - y$ is a nonzero quadratic residue modulo $p$ (this relation is symmetric because $-1$ is a square modulo $p$). Let $\omega(G_p)$ denote the clique number of $G_p$, i.e. the largest size of a subset $S \subseteq \mathbb{F}_p$ such that $x - y$ is a nonzero quadratic residue for every pair of distinct elements $x, y \in S$.

Determine whether $\omega(G_p)$ grows at most polylogarithmically in $p$. Specifically, do there exist absolute constants $C > 0$ and $k \geq 1$ such that
$$\omega(G_p) \leq C (\log p)^k$$
for every prime $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$? Equivalently, is $\omega(G_p) = O(\mathrm{polylog}(p))$?

The conjecture remains open. The best known unconditional upper bound is $\omega(G_p) \leq (1+o(1))\sqrt{p/2}$ due to Hanson and Petridis (2021), far from polylogarithmic. Recent work by Kunisky and Yu (2023) shows the degree-4 sum-of-squares relaxation has value at least $\Omega(p^{1/3})$, so SOS-based methods alone cannot establish a polylog bound at low degree. No proof or refutation of the polylogarithmic conjecture has been reported.

Recall the Soul theorem of Cheeger–Gromoll: every complete, connected, noncompact Riemannian manifold (M, g) of nonnegative sectional curvature admits a closed, totally convex, totally geodesic embedded submanifold S (a "soul"), and M is diffeomorphic to the total space of the normal bundle of S in M. There is also a complex analogue for complete Kähler manifolds of nonnegative holomorphic bisectional (or sectional) curvature, in which the soul is a complex submanifold and M is biholomorphic to a holomorphic vector bundle over it.

The original proof of Cheeger–Gromoll proceeds by analyzing the Busemann function associated with rays in M and invokes Toponogov's triangle comparison theorem.

Problem. Give a proof of the Soul theorem — in either its real Riemannian form or its complex Kähler form — that uses the Ricci flow
   ∂g(t)/∂t = −2 Ric(g(t)),   g(0) = g,
as its main tool, in place of the Busemann function / Toponogov comparison argument of Cheeger–Gromoll. That is, construct a Ricci-flow-based argument that produces the soul S ⊂ M and establishes that M is diffeomorphic (respectively biholomorphic) to the normal bundle of S.

Let $M$ be a complex manifold and let $E \to M$ be a holomorphic vector bundle of rank $r \geq 1$. The total space of $E$ is a complex manifold of dimension $\dim_{\mathbb{C}} M + r$. A Hermitian metric $g$ on a complex manifold $X$ is said to have positive holomorphic bisectional curvature if for every point $x \in X$ and every pair of nonzero $(1,0)$-tangent vectors $u, v \in T_x^{1,0} X$, the bisectional curvature
$$ R(u, \bar u, v, \bar v) > 0. $$
The metric is Kähler if its associated $(1,1)$-form is closed.

Determine, as completely as possible, the holomorphic vector bundles $E \to M$ whose total space admits a complete Kähler (respectively, Hermitian) metric of positive holomorphic bisectional curvature. In particular:

(a) Give necessary and sufficient conditions on the pair $(M, E)$ for the existence of such a metric on the total space of $E$.

(b) Treat the case in which the base $M$ is a Hermitian symmetric space.

(c) Identify whether a stability condition on the bundle $E$ (for instance, slope stability with respect to a chosen polarization on $M$) must be imposed, and if so, formulate the precise stability hypothesis required.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The general question appears to remain open. Recent partial results characterize complete Kähler metrics of nonnegative bisectional curvature on total spaces of line bundles over elliptic curves, and study positive holomorphic sectional curvature on certain line bundles (e.g., Hirzebruch manifolds), but no general criterion in terms of the base and a stability condition on the bundle is known. and the left-invariant frame
$$X_1=\partial_x-	frac{y}{2}\partial_z,\qquad X_2=\partial_y+	frac{x}{2}\partial_z,\qquad X_3=\partial_z.$$
Fix a parameter $\varepsilon>0$ and consider the family of Riemannian time-optimal control problems $P_\varepsilon$:
$$\dot q=u_1X_1+u_2X_2+\varepsilon u_3 X_3,\qquad u=(u_1,u_2,u_3)\in U=\{u\in\mathbb{R}^3:u_1^2+u_2^2+u_3^2\le 1\},$$
$$q(0)=q_0=(0,0,0),\qquad q(t_1)=q_1,\qquad t_1	o\min.$$

vanish.

\[ x_{n+1} \;=\; \frac{A}{x_n^{2}} \;+\; \frac{1}{\sqrt{x_{n-1}}}, \qquad n=0,1,2,\ldots, \]
where $A>0$ is a real parameter and the initial values $x_{-1},x_0$ are arbitrary positive real numbers. The equation possesses a unique positive equilibrium $\bar{x}>0$, namely the unique positive solution of $\bar{x}=A/\bar{x}^{2}+1/\sqrt{\bar{x}}$.

Question: Assume $0<A<\tfrac{15}{4}$. Is the positive equilibrium $\bar{x}$ globally asymptotically stable, i.e., is $\bar{x}$ locally stable and does every solution $\{x_n\}_{n\geq -1}$ with positive initial values satisfy $\lim_{n\to\infty} x_n=\bar{x}$?

Let M = H be the three-dimensional Heisenberg group, identified with R^3 with coordinates q = (x, y, z), equipped with the left-invariant vector fields
  X1 = ∂/∂x − (y/2) ∂/∂z,   X2 = ∂/∂y + (x/2) ∂/∂z,   X3 = ∂/∂z = [X1, X2].

For each ε > 0, consider the Riemannian time-optimal control problem P_ε:
  q̇ = u1 X1(q) + u2 X2(q) + ε u3 X3(q),   (u1, u2, u3) ∈ R^3,   u1^2 + u2^2 + u3^2 ≤ 1,
  q(0) = q0,   q(t1) = q1,   t1 → min,
where the left-invariant Riemannian metric g_ε is the one making (X1, X2, (1/ε) X3) orthonormal (equivalently, the control bound corresponds to a quadratic admissible velocity set).

Consider also the limiting sub-Riemannian problem P0:
  q̇ = u1 X1(q) + u2 X2(q),   u1^2 + u2^2 ≤ 1,   q(0) = q0,   q(t1) = q1,   t1 → min.

Denote by d_ε (resp. d_0) the associated time-optimal (i.e. Riemannian, resp. sub-Riemannian Carnot–Carathéodory) distance from the identity e ∈ H, and by
  S_ε(r) = { q ∈ H : d_ε(e, q) = r },   S_0(r) = { q ∈ H : d_0(e, q) = r },
the corresponding spheres of radius r > 0.

Recall that a family of closed subsets {A_ε}_{ε>0} of a metric space (X, d) converges to A_0 in the Kuratowski sense as ε → 0 if both:
 (i) every limit point of sequences x_{ε_n} ∈ A_{ε_n} with ε_n → 0 lies in A_0;
 (ii) every point of A_0 is the limit of some sequence x_{ε_n} ∈ A_{ε_n} with ε_n → 0.

Question: For every fixed r > 0, does S_ε(r) converge to S_0(r) in the Kuratowski sense as ε → 0?

Let $Q$ be a closed (compact, without boundary) smooth manifold, and let $T^*Q$ denote its cotangent bundle equipped with the canonical symplectic form $\omega = d\lambda$, where $\lambda$ is the Liouville $1$-form. Fix a Riemannian metric on $Q$, and let
$$D^*Q = \{(q,p) \in T^*Q : \|p\|_q \le 1\}$$
denote the associated unit disk cotangent bundle, a compact symplectic manifold with boundary.

For a symplectic manifold $(M,\omega)$ and a subset $A \subseteq M$, the $\pi_1$-sensitive Hofer–Zehnder capacity $c_{HZ}^\circ(A,M)$ is defined as the supremum of $\max H - \min H$ over all smooth compactly supported Hamiltonians $H : M \to \mathbb{R}$ with support in $A$ such that the Hamiltonian flow of $H$ has no non-constant contractible (in $M$) periodic orbit of period $\le 1$. Equivalently, one allows admissible Hamiltonians whose fast periodic orbits are required to be contractible loops in $M$.

Recall that a topological space $X$ is called a $K(\pi,1)$ (aspherical) if its higher homotopy groups $\pi_k(X)$ vanish for all $k \ge 2$.

Question: Is it true that for every closed smooth manifold $Q$ which is not a $K(\pi,1)$, the $\pi_1$-sensitive Hofer–Zehnder capacity $c_{HZ}^\circ(D^*Q, T^*Q)$ is finite?

Let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, and let $\chi$ denote the quadratic (Legendre) character on $\mathbb{F}_p$, extended by $\chi(0)=0$. The Paley equiangular tight frame is the collection of $N=p$ unit vectors in $\mathbb{C}^n$ (with $n=(p-1)/2$, or equivalently the $p\times n$ Paley ETF matrix obtained by an explicit normalization of rows of the Paley conference matrix) such that the inner product of any two distinct vectors has modulus exactly $\sqrt{(N-n)/(n(N-1))}=1/\sqrt{p}$ and the frame is tight.

Equivalently, form the $n \times p$ matrix $\Phi$ whose columns are these unit vectors. For an integer $m \le p$ and a subset $S \subset \{1,\dots,p\}$ with $|S|=m$, let $\Phi_S$ denote the $n \times m$ submatrix of $\Phi$ with columns indexed by $S$, and let $\kappa(\Phi_S)$ denote its condition number (the ratio of its largest to its smallest singular value).

Question: Does there exist a constant $\varepsilon > 0$ and a constant $C < \infty$ such that, for all sufficiently large primes $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ and for $m = \lfloor p^{1/2+\varepsilon}\rfloor$, every subset $S \subset \{1,\dots,p\}$ with $|S|=m$ satisfies
$$\kappa(\Phi_S) \le C ?$$

Equivalently, does the Paley equiangular tight frame satisfy the restricted isometry property at sparsity $m \asymp p^{1/2+\varepsilon}$, breaking the square-root bottleneck?

The conjecture is widely cited as open.
