Let $K$ be a field equipped with a non-trivial non-Archimedean absolute value $|\cdot|$, and let $E$ be a finite-dimensional Banach space over $K$ (with norm $\|\cdot\|$). Two nonzero subspaces $E_1, E_2 \subseteq E$ are said to be orthogonal, and $E$ is called the orthogonal direct sum $E_1 \perp E_2$, if $E = E_1 \oplus E_2$ as a vector space and
$$\|x_1 + x_2\| = \max(\|x_1\|,\|x_2\|) \quad \text{for all } x_1 \in E_1,\ x_2 \in E_2.$$
A nonzero subspace $E_1 \subseteq E$ is called prime if there is no proper nonzero subspace $E_2 \subseteq E$ such that $E = E_1 \perp E_2$ (equivalently, $E_1$ admits no nontrivial orthogonal complement in $E$, except $E_1 = E$ itself which is allowed).

It is known that every finite-dimensional non-Archimedean Banach space $E$ admits a decomposition

$$E = P_1 \perp \cdots \perp P_n = Q_1 \perp \cdots \perp Q_m,$$

Let K be a non-archimedean (complete) valued field with non-trivial valuation |·|, and let E be a normed K-vector space (a "p-adic normed space"); thus the norm satisfies the strong triangle inequality ‖x+y‖ ≤ max(‖x‖,‖y‖).

Two vectors x, y ∈ E are called orthogonal if ‖αx + βy‖ = max(‖αx‖, ‖βy‖) for all α, β ∈ K. More generally, two subspaces M, N ⊆ E are orthogonal if ‖m + n‖ = max(‖m‖, ‖n‖) for all m ∈ M and n ∈ N. A closed subspace N ⊆ E is called an orthogonal complement of a closed subspace M ⊆ E if E = M ⊕ N (algebraic direct sum) and M, N are orthogonal in the above sense.

Call E Hilbertian if every one-dimensional linear subspace of E admits an orthogonal complement.

A normed K-vector space E is called cartesian if it is isomorphic, as a normed space, to a finite or countable orthogonal direct sum of one-dimensional normed K-spaces — equivalently, E possesses an orthogonal base, i.e. a (Schauder) base (e_i)_{i∈I} such that for every finitely supported family of scalars (α_i) one has ‖Σ α_i e_i‖ = max_i ‖α_i e_i‖.

Question: Is every cartesian normed K-space Hilbertian? That is, if E has an orthogonal base, must every one-dimensional subspace of E possess an orthogonal complement?

Setting. Let f: X → Y be a proper morphism of locally complete intersection type between (suitable) schemes (or, more generally, let X be a relative scheme over a locally ringed topos Y satisfying analogous relative hypotheses). Assume that on the K-theory groups K'(X) of coherent sheaves there is a natural λ-ring structure, and let T_f denote the relative cotangent complex of f. Define the Todd class Td(T_f) of f by means of this relative cotangent complex (via the usual formal series in its Chern classes).

Problem.
(a) Prove a Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch formula of the form
    ch(f_* α) = f_*(ch(α) · Td(T_f))
for every α ∈ K'(X), without assuming that f is projective (i.e., not requiring a factorization through a projective bundle or any global immersion into a smooth Y-scheme).

(b) Establish the analogous formula for proper morphisms in the categories of complex analytic spaces and of rigid analytic spaces, going beyond the case of a single locally free sheaf on a nonsingular compact complex variety mapped to a point.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The algebraic part has been substantially advanced: O'Brian–Toledo–Tong (1985) established a Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch formula for proper holomorphic maps of complex manifolds; Navarro & Navarro (2017, "On the Riemann–Roch formula without projective hypothesis") proved GRR for proper maps between smooth schemes via A^1-homotopy techniques; and Navarro proved a Riemann–Roch theorem for homotopy-invariant K-theory and projective lci morphisms between finite-dimensional noetherian schemes, without smoothness. Recent works (e.g., Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch for complex analytic ∞-prestacks, 2026) continue extending the complex/rigid-analytic case. A fully general GRR for arbitrary proper lci morphisms in the relative-topos and rigid-analytic settings as originally envisaged is not uniformly settled, so the problem is best classified as partially solved.

Let $K$ be a non-trivially valued non-archimedean (complete) field, and let
$$\ell^1(K) = \Big\{ (x_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}} : x_n \in K, \ \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} |x_n| < \infty \Big\}$$
be the Banach space over $K$ equipped with the norm $\|(x_n)\|_1 = \sum_{n} |x_n|$. A norm $\|\cdot\|$ on a $K$-vector space $E$ is called an ultranorm (non-archimedean norm) if it satisfies the strong triangle inequality $\|x+y\| \le \max(\|x\|,\|y\|)$ for all $x,y \in E$. The space $\ell^1(K)$ is said to be ultrametrizable (as a topological vector space) if there exists an ultranorm on $\ell^1(K)$ that defines the same topology as the norm $\|\cdot\|_1$.

Question: Does there exist an ultranorm on $\ell^1(K)$ that is equivalent to the standard $\ell^1$-norm, i.e., is $\ell^1(K)$ ultrametrizable?

Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian 4-manifold satisfying the Einstein field equations, and let $T^{ab}$ denote a smooth, symmetric, divergence-free stress-energy tensor on $M$ satisfying suitable energy conditions (e.g., the dominant energy condition). Consider a one-parameter family of "test bodies" modeled by stress-energy tensors $T^{ab}_\varepsilon$ (for $\varepsilon > 0$) supported in spatially compact, timelike worldtubes $W_\varepsilon \subset M$ whose spatial diameters and total mass-energies tend to zero as $\varepsilon \to 0$, while remaining strictly positive (i.e., the bodies are small but finite, not idealized point particles). Assume each $T^{ab}_\varepsilon$ is conserved ($\nabla_a T^{ab}_\varepsilon = 0$) and satisfies the dominant energy condition.

Prove that, in an appropriate precise sense to be formulated, the worldtubes $W_\varepsilon$ converge as $\varepsilon \to 0$ to a timelike curve $\gamma$ in $M$ that is a geodesic of the spacetime metric $g$; equivalently, formulate and prove a rigorous theorem stating that very small but finite (extended, non-test-particle-idealized) test bodies in general relativity move on spacetime geodesics, including the back-reaction and finite-size corrections in a controlled way.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Several theorems address this question. The Geroch–Jang theorem (1975) and refinements by Ehlers–Geroch (2004) prove that sufficiently small test bodies satisfying suitable energy conditions follow timelike geodesics, treated via limiting sequences of extended bodies. More recently, gravitational self-force programs (Gralla–Wald, Pound, and others) provide rigorous derivations in the small-mass limit. Thus the problem is partially solved: precise theorems exist under specific hypotheses, but a fully general formulation including all matter models and back-reaction effects continues to be refined.

Let $(M, g)$ be a 4-dimensional Lorentzian manifold satisfying the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = 0$. Under a 3+1 decomposition with spatial slices $\Sigma_t$ carrying induced Riemannian metric $\gamma_{ij}$ and second fundamental form $K_{ij}$, the Einstein equations split into:

(i) Evolution equations: a system of PDEs giving $\partial_t \gamma_{ij}$ and $\partial_t K_{ij}$ in terms of $\gamma_{ij}$, $K_{ij}$, lapse $N$, and shift $\beta^i$.

(ii) Constraint equations: the Hamiltonian constraint $R(\gamma) + (\mathrm{tr}_\gamma K)^2 - |K|^2_\gamma = 0$ and the momentum constraint $\nabla^j(K_{ij} - (\mathrm{tr}_\gamma K)\gamma_{ij}) = 0$.

A fundamental property of the continuum system is that if the constraints hold on the initial slice, they are preserved by the evolution.

Problem: Construct a numerical (finite-difference, finite-element, or lattice) discretization of the Einstein evolution equations on a discretization of spacetime such that the discrete analogues of the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints are exactly preserved by the discrete time evolution whenever they are satisfied by the discrete initial data, and prove that solutions of this scheme converge, as the discretization parameter tends to zero, to a long-time smooth solution of the vacuum Einstein equations on a maximal globally hyperbolic development of admissible initial data.

The problem of designing provably constraint-preserving numerical schemes for the Einstein equations with a rigorous long-time convergence proof remains open. Recent progress includes structure-preserving finite-element discretizations of the linearized Einstein equations via Hodge-Dirac/divdiv complexes (2025) and constraint-damping reformulations (Z4/CCZ4) used in practical numerical relativity, but these either treat only linearized models or lack a full mathematical proof of long-time convergence to a solution of the nonlinear vacuum Einstein equations.

Let $X$ be a smooth quasi-projective scheme over a field. Denote by $A(X) =  igoplus_p A^p(X)$ the Chow ring of cycles modulo rational equivalence, graded by codimension. Let $K'(X) = K_0'(X)$ be the Grothendieck group of coherent sheaves on $X$ (which, by smoothness, coincides with $K_0(X)$ and is a ring). Equip $K'(X)$ with two decreasing filtrations:

(i) the topological filtration by codimension of supports, $F^p_{\mathrm{top}} K'(X)$, generated by classes of coherent sheaves whose support has codimension $\geq p$, with associated graded ring $\mathrm{Gr}'_{\mathrm{top}}(X)$;

(ii) the $\lambda$-filtration (Grothendieck's $\gamma$-filtration) $F^p_\gamma K'(X)$, with associated graded ring $\mathrm{Gr}'(X)$.

There are natural ring homomorphisms
$$\varphi : A(X) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Gr}'_{\mathrm{top}}(X), \qquad \psi : \mathrm{Gr}'_{\mathrm{top}}(X) \longrightarrow A(X),$$
whose compositions in either order equal multiplication by an integer factor (built from $(p-1)!$ in codimension $p$) modulo torsion, in the standard comparison formulas linking $A(X)$, $\mathrm{Gr}'_{\mathrm{top}}(X)$, and $\mathrm{Gr}'(X)$.

Question: Do these comparison formulas relating $\varphi$ and $\psi$ hold exactly (integrally), and not merely modulo torsion? In particular, is the map
$$\varphi^2 : A^2(X) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Gr}'^{\,2}_{\mathrm{top}}(X)$$
an isomorphism for every smooth quasi-projective $X$ (including, e.g., the case $\dim X = 3$)?

Let $(M, g)$ be a $(3+1)$-dimensional asymptotically flat Lorentzian spacetime admitting a notion of future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$, on which one may speak of cuts (cross-sections of $\mathscr{I}^+$ diffeomorphic to a 2-sphere). A spacelike hypersurface $\Sigma \subset M$ is said to be of constant mean curvature (CMC) if its mean curvature $H$ with respect to the future-directed timelike unit normal is constant on $\Sigma$. Such a $\Sigma$ is said to be asymptotic to a given cut $\mathcal{C} \subset \mathscr{I}^+$ if $\Sigma$ extends out to null infinity and its trace at $\mathscr{I}^+$ coincides with $\mathcal{C}$.

Problem. Extending the standard a priori estimates and existence theory for maximal ($H=0$) hypersurfaces to the CMC ($H = \mathrm{const} \neq 0$) setting:

(a) Prove the existence of a CMC hypersurface $\Sigma$ in $(M,g)$ that is asymptotic to a prescribed cut $\mathcal{C}$ of future null infinity.

(b) Determine the weakest asymptotic conditions on the geometry near $\mathscr{I}^+$ (e.g., decay/regularity of the Bondi data, peeling properties, smoothness of $\mathscr{I}^+$) under which the existence in (a) holds, and show that these conditions are sharp.

Let $G$ be a semi-simple, simply connected linear algebraic group over the field of complex numbers $\mathbb{C}$, and let $G(\mathbb{C})$ denote its associated compact (real) Lie group (equivalently, the underlying complex manifold endowed with its classical topology). Let $A(G) = \bigoplus_{i\ge 0} A^i(G)$ denote the Chow ring of $G$ (the ring of algebraic cycles on $G$ modulo rational equivalence), and let $H^{*}(G(\mathbb{C}), \mathbb{Z})$ denote its integral singular cohomology ring. There is a natural cycle-class ring homomorphism
$$ \mathrm{cl} : A(G) \longrightarrow H^{*}(G(\mathbb{C}), \mathbb{Z}), $$
which doubles degrees ($A^i(G) \to H^{2i}(G(\mathbb{C}),\mathbb{Z})$).

(1) Is the homomorphism $\mathrm{cl}$ injective for every such $G$?

(2) More precisely, let $A^{+}(G) = \bigoplus_{i>0} A^i(G)$. It is known that the torsion primes of $G(\mathbb{C})$ (the primes $p$ for which $H^{*}(G(\mathbb{C}),\mathbb{Z})$ has $p$-torsion) are exactly the primes dividing the order of the finite group $A^{+}(G)$. Does the cycle map $\mathrm{cl}$ in fact detect $A^{+}(G)$ in a manner compatible with this coincidence of torsion primes — for instance, is $\mathrm{cl}$ restricted to $A^{+}(G)$ injective?

As a known partial fact one may use: for $G = G_2$ over $\mathbb{C}$, the cycle map $\mathrm{cl}$ is non-zero in positive degrees.

Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth $(3+1)$-dimensional Lorentzian manifold and let $\Omega \subset M$ be a boost-type domain, that is, a domain of the form
$$\Omega = \{(t,x)\in \mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{R}^3 : |t| < \alpha\,|x| + \beta,\ |x|>R\}$$
for some constants $\alpha\in(0,1)$, $\beta>0$, $R>0$, on which $g$ is asymptotically Minkowskian (i.e., in the standard coordinates, $g_{\mu\nu}-\eta_{\mu\nu}$ together with appropriate derivatives decays to zero as $|x|\to\infty$ at a suitable rate uniform in the boost cone).

A spacelike hypersurface $\Sigma \subset \Omega$ is called a maximal surface if it has vanishing mean curvature with respect to $g$.

Prove (or disprove) the following: every maximal surface $\Sigma$ contained in such a boost-type domain $\Omega$ is necessarily asymptotically flat (in the sense that the induced Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$ approaches the Euclidean metric at infinity with the appropriate decay), and moreover $\Sigma$ must coincide with one of the maximal slices previously constructed in this setting (in particular, $\Sigma$ is unique up to the action of the asymptotic boost/translation symmetries).

Let X be a smooth quasi-projective variety over a field k. Denote by K'(X) = K_0(X) the Grothendieck group of coherent sheaves (equivalently, of locally free sheaves, since X is smooth), endowed with its natural ring structure and with the λ-ring structure given by exterior powers. Let F^•K'(X) be the associated γ-filtration (equivalently, the Chern filtration), and set
   Gr'(X) := ⊕_{p≥0} F^p K'(X) / F^{p+1} K'(X),
the associated graded ring. For each vector bundle E on X and each integer p ≥ 0, one has Chern classes c_p^{K}(E) ∈ Gr'(X) defined via the λ-operations. Let A(X) = ⊕_p A^p(X) denote the Chow ring of X (cycles modulo rational equivalence with the intersection product), and let c_p(E) ∈ A^p(X) denote the Chow-theoretic Chern classes.

(a) Does there exist a graded ring homomorphism
        g : Gr'(X) ⟶ A(X)
that sends c_p^{K}(E) to c_p(E) for every vector bundle E on X and every p ≥ 0?

(b) (Topological analogue.) Let X be a compact topological space. Let K'(X) be the topological K-theory ring, equipped with its λ-operations and γ-filtration, and let Gr'(X) be the associated graded ring, with Chern classes c_p^{K}(E) ∈ Gr'(X) for each complex vector bundle E on X. Does there exist a graded ring homomorphism
        Gr'(X) ⟶ H^{2*}(X, ℤ) = ⊕_p H^{2p}(X, ℤ)
sending c_p^{K}(E) to the ordinary integral Chern class c_p(E) ∈ H^{2p}(X, ℤ) for every complex vector bundle E on X?

Rationally, the comparison maps are isomorphisms via the Chern character / Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch. Integrally, the relationship between the γ-filtration on K-theory and the Chow ring (resp. integral cohomology in the topological case) is delicate: it is known that the associated graded for the γ-filtration is in general only related to CH(X) by a surjection up to torsion, and recent works (e.g. Karpenko–Merkurjev on Chow filtrations on representation rings, Yagita's notes on filtrations of K-theory, Totaro's work on Chow rings of classifying spaces) show that the existence of a natural integral ring map Gr_γ K(X) → CH(X) sending Chern classes to Chern classes does not hold in full generality and depends on subtle conditions (e.g. whether the E_∞-page of the Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence is generated by Chern classes). The precise question as posed by Grothendieck for arbitrary smooth quasi-projective X (and for arbitrary compact spaces) does not appear to be resolved by a definitive yes/no in the literature found.

Background. A *gem* (graph-encoded manifold) of dimension 4 is a finite, regular, edge-5-colored multigraph $(\Gamma,\gamma)$ with color set $\Delta_4=\{0,1,2,3,4\}$ such that, for each $i\in\Delta_4$, the subgraph $\Gamma_{\hat i}$ obtained by deleting all edges of color $i$ encodes the boundary of a regular neighborhood of the vertex of color $i$ in the associated colored triangulation; equivalently, the dual ball-complex $K(\Gamma)$ is a closed PL 4-manifold $M^4$. For each unordered pair $\{i,j\}\subset\Delta_4$, a *bicolored cycle of colors $\{i,j\}$* is a connected component of the subgraph of $\Gamma$ induced by edges of colors $i$ and $j$; such a component is an even-length cycle alternating in colors $i$ and $j$.

A trisection of a closed orientable PL 4-manifold $M^4$ is a decomposition $M^4=X_1\cup X_2\cup X_3$ where each $X_h$ is a 4-dimensional 1-handlebody, the pairwise intersections $X_h\cap X_{h+1}$ are 3-dimensional handlebodies, and the triple intersection $\Sigma=X_1\cap X_2\cap X_3$ is a closed orientable surface; the trisection is described by a *trisection diagram* consisting of three cut systems of curves on $\Sigma$.

Suppose Proposition P below produces, from any gem $(\Gamma,\gamma)$ of a closed orientable PL 4-manifold satisfying a combinatorial condition (⋆) on the cyclic ordering of the five colors around each vertex, a *gem-induced trisection* of $M^4=K(\Gamma)$ whose central surface, handlebody decompositions, and cut systems are each realized by certain explicit families of bicolored cycles of $\Gamma$.

Problem. Design and prove correctness of an algorithm that, given as input a 5-edge-colored multigraph $(\Gamma,\gamma)$ representing a closed PL 4-manifold:

(a) decides in finite (and ideally polynomial) time whether the edge-ordering condition (⋆) of Proposition P is satisfied by $(\Gamma,\gamma)$; and

(b) when (⋆) holds, outputs the explicit lists of bicolored cycles of $(\Gamma,\gamma)$ that determine a trisection diagram $(\Sigma;\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$ of the gem-induced trisection of $M^4$.

Provide complexity bounds for both subroutines.

A trisection of a closed orientable PL 4-manifold $M^4$ is a decomposition $M^4=X_1\cup X_2\cup X_3$ where each $X_h$ is a 4-dimensional 1-handlebody, the pairwise intersections $X_h\cap X_{h+1}$ are 3-dimensional handlebodies, and the triple intersection $\Sigma=X_1\cap X_2\cap X_3$ is a closed orientable surface; the trisection is described by a *trisection diagram* consisting of three cut systems of curves on $\Sigma$.

Suppose Proposition P below produces, from any gem $(\Gamma,\gamma)$ of a closed orientable PL 4-manifold satisfying a combinatorial condition (⋆) on the cyclic ordering of the five colors around each vertex, a *gem-induced trisection* of $M^4=K(\Gamma)$ whose central surface, handlebody decompositions, and cut systems are each realized by certain explicit families of bicolored cycles of $\Gamma$.

Problem. Design and prove correctness of an algorithm that, given as input a 5-edge-colored multigraph $(\Gamma,\gamma)$ representing a closed PL 4-manifold:

(a) decides in finite (and ideally polynomial) time whether the edge-ordering condition (⋆) of Proposition P is satisfied by $(\Gamma,\gamma)$; and

(b) when (⋆) holds, outputs the explicit lists of bicolored cycles of $(\Gamma,\gamma)$ that determine a trisection diagram $(\Sigma;\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$ of the gem-induced trisection of $M^4$.

Provide complexity bounds for both subroutines.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question is posed as an open algorithmic problem in recent surveys on gems and trisections of PL 4-manifolds (2025). Related work (e.g., "Estimating trisection genus via gem theory", arXiv:2504.04434, and "Trisections of PL 4-manifolds arising from colored triangulations", arXiv:2312.01902) develops the theoretical framework but does not provide a published, fully implemented algorithm with proven correctness for both detection of condition (⋆) and extraction of the bicolored-cycle data of the trisection diagram. No source confirming a complete solution was found.

Let $f : X \to Y$ be a regular closed immersion of codimension $1$ between schemes of finite type over $\mathbb{C}$. Assume no regularity (smoothness or non-singularity) hypothesis on $Y$.

Recall that for $f$ a regular immersion between smooth varieties one has a cohomological Gysin homomorphism
$$f^{!}_{\mathrm{coh}} : H^{*}(X) \longrightarrow H^{*+2}(Y)$$
(where $H^{*}$ denotes a suitable cohomology theory, e.g. singular cohomology of the associated analytic space, or $\ell$-adic/Betti/Hodge cohomology), and a $K$-theoretic Gysin homomorphism
$$f^{!}_{K} : K_{0}(X) \longrightarrow K_{0}(Y),$$
related to one another, via the Chern character $\mathrm{ch}$ and the Todd class, by a commutative Riemann–Roch comparison square
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
K_{0}(X) & \xrightarrow{\;f^{!}_{K}\;} & K_{0}(Y) \\
\downarrow{\scriptstyle \mathrm{ch}(-)\cdot \mathrm{Td}(X)} & & \downarrow{\scriptstyle \mathrm{ch}(-)\cdot \mathrm{Td}(Y)} \\
H^{*}(X) & \xrightarrow{\;f^{!}_{\mathrm{coh}}\;} & H^{*+2}(Y).
\end{array}
$$

Question: When $Y$ is allowed to be singular (only of finite type over $\mathbb{C}$), can one construct a cohomological Gysin homomorphism $f^{!}_{\mathrm{coh}}$ with reasonable functorial properties such that the above Riemann–Roch comparison square remains commutative? Equivalently, give a plausible definition of such a homomorphism, or prove that no such well-behaved construction can exist.

Fix an integer $n\ge 2$. Consider the overdetermined eigenvalue problem
$$\Delta u + \lambda u = 0 \text{ in } \Omega,\qquad u = 0 \text{ on } \partial\Omega,\qquad \langle \nabla u,\nu\rangle = \text{const on } \partial\Omega,$$
where $\nu$ is the outward unit normal. The straight cylinder $\Omega_0 = \{(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}:|x|<1\}$ admits the radial first Dirichlet eigenfunction, which trivially satisfies the overdetermined condition.

Assume there exists a smooth one-parameter bifurcation branch $s\mapsto (w_s,T_s)$, defined for $s$ in a neighborhood of $0$, of nontrivial periodic perturbations of $\Omega_0$, where $w_s:\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a smooth function with $w_0\equiv 0$ and $T_s>0$ with $T_0$ equal to the bifurcation period, such that the modified cylinder
$$\Omega_s = \Bigl\{(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\,:\, |x| < 1 + s\cos\!\bigl(2\pi t/T_s\bigr) + s\,w_s\!\bigl(2\pi t/T_s\bigr)\Bigr\}$$
carries a positive $T_s$-periodic $C^{2,\alpha}$ solution $u_s$ of the overdetermined problem above for some eigenvalue $\lambda_s>0$.

Viewed as a bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^n\times(\mathbb{R}/T_s\mathbb{Z})$, is $\Omega_s$, for all sufficiently small $s\ne 0$, a local minimizer of the first Dirichlet eigenvalue functional $\Omega\mapsto \lambda_1(\Omega)$ among domains of the same volume on the flat manifold $\mathbb{R}^n\times(\mathbb{R}/T_s\mathbb{Z})$?

Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian 4-manifold satisfying the Einstein field equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g) - \tfrac{1}{2}R(g)\,g + \Lambda\,g = T$, where $T$ is the energy-momentum tensor. Recall the following standard conditions:

- (Timelike convergence / strong energy condition) $\mathrm{Ric}(X,X) \ge 0$ for every timelike vector $X$.
- (Dominant energy condition) For every future-directed causal vector $X$, the vector $-T^{\mu}{}_{\nu} X^{\nu}$ is future-directed causal; equivalently, $T(X,Y) \ge 0$ for all future-directed causal $X,Y$, and energy flows along causal directions.

The classical Penrose–Hawking singularity theorems guarantee causal geodesic incompleteness of $(M,g)$ under hypotheses that include the timelike convergence condition together with a suitable causal/initial condition (e.g. existence of a closed trapped surface, a compact Cauchy hypersurface, or a point whose future null cone reconverges).

Problem. Formulate and prove a singularity theorem of Penrose–Hawking type whose curvature/matter hypothesis is the dominant energy condition rather than the timelike convergence condition. That is, establish that, under appropriate causal and trapping hypotheses together with the dominant energy condition (and possibly the Einstein equations with a specified cosmological constant or matter model), the spacetime $(M,g)$ must be causally geodesically incomplete.

The literature establishes singularity theorems under various energy conditions (null, weak, strong/timelike convergence, and averaged/quantum versions), and recent work derives Hawking-type theorems from worldvolume or quantum energy inequalities. Consider the overdetermined elliptic problem on perturbed cylinders in $\mathbb{R}^{N+1}$ ($N\ge 1$). For a positive number $T>0$ and a small parameter $s$, let
$$\Omega_{s,T,w}=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^N\times\mathbb{R}:|x|<1+s\cos(2\pi t/T)+s\,w(2\pi t/T)\},$$
where $w$ is a $2\pi$-periodic, even function with zero mean. Seek $(u,\Omega)$ such that
$$-\Delta u=\lambda_n u\ \text{in }\Omega,\qquad u=0\ \text{on }\partial\Omega,\qquad \partial_\nu u=\text{const}\ \text{on }\partial\Omega,$$
where $\lambda_n$ is the $n$-th radial Dirichlet eigenvalue of $-\Delta$ on the unit ball $B_1\subset\mathbb{R}^N$, and $\nu$ is the outward unit normal to $\partial\Omega$.

Suppose that there is a critical period $T^*(n)$ at which a local bifurcation from the trivial branch (the straight cylinder $B_1\times\mathbb{R}$ with the radial eigenfunction associated to $\lambda_n$) occurs, producing a smooth one-parameter family
$$s\longmapsto (w_s,\,T_s),\qquad w_0=0,\ T_0=T^*(n),$$
of nontrivial solutions to the overdetermined problem above (with $w_s$ in a suitable space of even, zero-mean periodic functions).

Determine the type of bifurcation at $T^*(n)$: namely, decide whether
$$\left.\frac{\partial T_s}{\partial s}\right|_{s=0}<0\ (\text{subcritical}),\quad =0\ (\text{critical}),\quad \text{or}\ >0\ (\text{supercritical}).$$

Let $n\ge 2$ and consider the Banach space $X = C^{2,\alpha}_{\mathrm{even},0}(\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})$ of $2\pi$-periodic, even, real-valued $C^{2,\alpha}$ functions with zero mean. For $v\in X$ with $v>-1$ and $T>0$, define the perturbed cylinder
$$\Omega^{v} = \{(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\times\mathbb{R} : |x| < 1 + v(2\pi t/T)\}.$$
A pair $(v,T)\in X\times(0,\infty)$ is called a nontrivial solution if there exist $\lambda>0$ and a positive $T$-periodic (in $t$) function $u\in C^{2,\alpha}(\overline{\Omega^{v}})$ satisfying the overdetermined problem
$$\Delta u + \lambda u = 0 \text{ in } \Omega^{v}, \qquad u = 0 \text{ on } \partial\Omega^{v}, \qquad \partial_{\nu}u = \text{const on } \partial\Omega^{v}.$$
Let $\mathcal{O} = \{v\in X : v>-1\}\times(0,\infty)$. Suppose that, for some integer $n\ge 2$ and some $T^{*}(n)>0$, the point $(0,T^{*}(n))$ is a local bifurcation point from which a local branch of nontrivial solutions emanates.

Consider the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$ for a Lorentzian 4-manifold $(M,g)$, with Cauchy initial data $(\Sigma_0, h_0, K_0)$ that is asymptotically flat: $\Sigma_0$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3$ minus possibly finitely many balls, $h_0$ is a Riemannian metric and $K_0$ a symmetric 2-tensor on $\Sigma_0$ satisfying the vacuum constraint equations
$$R(h_0)+(\mathrm{tr}_{h_0}K_0)^2-|K_0|_{h_0}^2=0,\qquad \mathrm{div}_{h_0}K_0-d(\mathrm{tr}_{h_0}K_0)=0,$$
and approaching the standard flat data at spatial infinity in a suitably weighted sense. A foliation $\{\Sigma_t\}_{t\ge 0}$ of (a portion of) the maximal Cauchy development by spacelike Cauchy hypersurfaces is called a maximal slicing if every leaf has vanishing mean curvature, $\mathrm{tr}_{h_t}K_t=0$. The maximal slicing gauge couples this foliation condition to a lapse-shift system: the lapse $N$ solves the elliptic equation
$$\Delta_{h_t}N = N\,|K_t|_{h_t}^2,\qquad N\to 1\ \text{at infinity},$$
and the shift is chosen (e.g. as a minimal-distortion or zero shift) so that the evolution of $h_t,K_t$ given by the ADM equations preserves $\mathrm{tr}_{h_t}K_t=0$.

A globally naked singularity is, informally, a singular event in the maximal Cauchy development whose causal future contains a complete future-directed null geodesic reaching past null infinity; its absence is the content of weak cosmic censorship. A maximal-surface barrier is a smooth maximal hypersurface (or family of such) lying in the Cauchy development whose causal future contains all future singular behavior, so that singularities are "shielded" from infinity by the barrier.

Problem. Establish a long-time existence theorem for the Cauchy problem of the asymptotically flat vacuum Einstein equations evolved in the maximal slicing gauge described above, valid for arbitrarily large initial data, with conclusions strong enough to imply both:
(i) no globally naked singularity forms in the maximal Cauchy development; and
(ii) every singularity that forms is contained in the causal future of a maximal-surface barrier within the foliation.

Specifically, prove existence of a smooth maximal foliation $\{\Sigma_t\}_{t\in[0,T^*)}$ of a globally hyperbolic region $\mathcal{D}\subset M$ such that either $T^*=\infty$ and $\mathcal{D}$ contains a neighborhood of future null infinity, or else as $t\uparrow T^*$ the leaves $\Sigma_t$ converge to a smooth maximal hypersurface beyond which the geometry degenerates only in the trapped (black-hole) region, in either case ruling out (i) and ensuring (ii).

representations.normalized:
Consider a discrete-time linear periodic system of period $K\ge 1$ with state-space realization
$$x_{k+1}=A_k x_k + B_k u_k,\qquad y_k=C_k x_k + D_k u_k,$$
where the matrix sequences $\{A_k\},\{B_k\},\{C_k\},\{D_k\}$ are $K$-periodic (i.e., $A_{k+K}=A_k$, etc.) and may have time-varying dimensions. Let $G$ denote the corresponding periodic input–output operator on $\ell_2$. An inner–outer factorization of $G$ is a representation $G = G_i G_o$ in which $G_i$ is a $K$-periodic inner operator (i.e., $G_i^\sim G_i = I$, with $G_i^\sim$ the conjugate operator) and $G_o$ is a $K$-periodic outer operator (i.e., causal with a causal pseudo-inverse on the range). The factorization is said to be "standard" when the periodic feedthrough matrices $D_k$ have full row (or column) rank uniformly in $k$ and $G$ has no zeros on the unit circle; otherwise it is "non-standard" (e.g., rank-deficient or singular feedthrough, zeros on the unit circle, or zeros at infinity).

Problem. Devise an algorithm that, for the general non-standard case, computes an inner–outer factorization $G = G_i G_o$ of an arbitrary discrete-time $K$-periodic system, returning $K$-periodic state-space realizations of the inner factor $G_i$ and the outer factor $G_o$. The algorithm must operate intrinsically on the periodic data $\{(A_k,B_k,C_k,D_k)\}_{k=0}^{K-1}$ — without reducing the problem to a single time-invariant lifted system — and must be numerically reliable and efficient with computational cost comparable to other state-of-the-art periodic-system algorithms (e.g., based on periodic QR/QZ-type orthogonal transformations and periodic Riccati/Schur computations).

Let $X$ be a noetherian scheme (or a sufficiently nice algebraic variety/scheme on which étale cohomology with $\mathbb{Z}_\ell(i)$ coefficients is defined) and let $Y \subseteq X$ be a closed subset with open complement $U = X \setminus Y$. Let $L^\bullet$ be a perfect complex of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules whose restriction $L^\bullet|_U$ is acyclic (equivalently, zero in the derived category of $U$), so that all cohomology sheaves $\mathcal{H}^j(L^\bullet)$ are supported on $Y$.

(a) Construct, for every $i \geq 0$, Chern classes with support
$$c_i^Y(L^\bullet) \in H_Y^{2i}(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(i))$$
(or in the analogous ordinary cohomology with support in $Y$), that are functorial in $(X,Y,L^\bullet)$, additive on distinguished triangles in the appropriate Grothendieck-group sense, and such that under the canonical "forget supports" map
$$H_Y^{2i}(X,\mathbb{Z}_\ell(i)) \longrightarrow H^{2i}(X,\mathbb{Z}_\ell(i))$$
the class $c_i^Y(L^\bullet)$ is sent to the ordinary $i$-th Chern class $c_i(L^\bullet)$ of the perfect complex $L^\bullet$.

(b) Using such classes $c_i^Y(L^\bullet)$, formulate and prove a refined version of the cohomological Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch theorem — both the version with denominators and the version without denominators — that incorporates families of supports, i.e. that takes place naturally in cohomology with support and recovers the usual Riemann–Roch formula after forgetting supports.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Localized/supported Chern classes for perfect complexes acyclic off a closed subset have been constructed in various settings (e.g. via MacPherson-style local Chern character constructions of Baum–Fulton–MacPherson, Iversen, and Bloch, and more recently in motivic/refined Gysin frameworks). The Riemann–Roch theorem without denominators has been proved by Jouanolou and extended into motivic homotopy theory and higher K-theory. However, a fully general formulation incorporating families of supports and giving a strengthened cohomological Riemann–Roch with supports remains an active topic; no single reference appears to settle the question in the broad generality stated.

Consider a discrete-time linear periodic system of period K ≥ 1, given by

  x(k+1) = A(k) x(k) + B(k) u(k),
  y(k)   = C(k) x(k) + D(k) u(k),

where A(k), B(k), C(k), D(k) are real matrices that are periodic in k with period K (so A(k+K)=A(k), etc.), and the system is assumed to be uniformly exponentially stable. Such a system has an associated time-varying Hankel operator H mapping past inputs to future outputs, whose induced ℓ²-operator norm is the Hankel norm ‖·‖_H of the system.

Given a target McMillan degree profile {r(k)}_{k=0}^{K-1} that is strictly less than the corresponding state dimension profile, the optimal Hankel-norm approximation problem asks for a stable discrete-time periodic system Ĝ of the prescribed reduced degree profile that minimizes ‖G − Ĝ‖_H, where G is the original periodic system.

Problem. Develop a numerically reliable and computationally efficient algorithm that, given the periodic state-space data {A(k), B(k), C(k), D(k)}_{k=0}^{K-1}, computes such an optimal (or near-optimal) Hankel-norm approximant Ĝ in the periodic setting, with proven backward-stability or comparable numerical reliability guarantees and complexity scaling gracefully in K and the state dimensions.

Call a smooth Lorentzian 4-manifold $(M,g)$ a purely radiative vacuum spacetime if it satisfies the Einstein vacuum equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$ and admits a smooth conformal compactification: there exists a manifold-with-boundary $\widetilde M$ with smooth metric $\widetilde g = \Omega^2 g$ and boundary defining function $\Omega\ge 0$, such that the conformal boundary contains a past null infinity $\mathscr I^-$ and a future null infinity $\mathscr I^+$, both of which are smooth and complete (every null geodesic generator extends to its full affine range), and such that the past timelike infinity $i^-$ and future timelike infinity $i^+$ are regular points of the conformal extension at which $\widetilde g$ is smooth. Require further that the spacetime carries no incoming or outgoing matter and no incoming radiation other than gravitational radiation generated by the geometry itself (i.e., it is genuinely a vacuum solution with the conformal data being purely radiative), and that the ADM/Bondi mass is strictly positive.

Either construct an explicit example of such a purely radiative vacuum spacetime with positive mass, or prove that at least one such spacetime exists.

$$E_k x_{k+1} = A_k x_k + B_k u_k,\qquad y_k = C_k x_k + D_k u_k,\qquad k\in\mathbb{Z},$$

(a) controller design (find a periodic controller making the closed-loop transfer match $T_{\mathrm{ref}}$);
(b) observer design (find a periodic observer producing an estimate that matches a reference response); and
(c) fault-detection filter design (find a periodic residual generator whose response to faults matches a prescribed reference while rejecting disturbances).

Consider the vacuum Einstein initial-value problem: an initial data set consists of a smooth Riemannian 3-manifold $(\Sigma, h)$ together with a symmetric 2-tensor $K$ on $\Sigma$ satisfying the vacuum constraint equations
$$R_h - |K|_h^2 + (\mathrm{tr}_h K)^2 = 0, \qquad \mathrm{div}_h K - d(\mathrm{tr}_h K) = 0,$$
where $R_h$ is the scalar curvature of $h$. A development of $(\Sigma, h, K)$ is a smooth, globally hyperbolic Lorentzian 4-manifold $(M, g)$ solving the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = 0$, together with an embedding $\iota : \Sigma \hookrightarrow M$ as a Cauchy hypersurface, such that $\iota^* g = h$ and the second fundamental form of $\iota(\Sigma)$ in $(M, g)$ equals $K$.

Address the following two questions:

(a) Are there regularity conditions on the initial data $(\Sigma, h, K)$ (weaker than those needed for the classical maximal globally hyperbolic development) that guarantee the existence of a development but for which uniqueness (in the appropriate sense, up to isometry) fails?

(b) Does there exist smooth vacuum initial data $(\Sigma, h, K)$ whose vacuum Einstein evolution develops a singularity, beyond which the spacetime can be extended in more than one inequivalent way as a globally hyperbolic vacuum solution?

Consider a discrete-time linear periodic system

  x(k+1) = A(k) x(k) + B(k) u(k),    A(k+P) = A(k),  B(k+P) = B(k),

with period P ≥ 1. A periodic linear matrix inequality (periodic LMI) is a finite collection of constraints of the form

  F_0(k) + Σ_{i=1}^{m} x_i(k) F_i(k) ≻ 0,    k = 0, 1, …, P − 1,

where for each k the symmetric matrices F_i(k) ∈ S^{n×n} are given P-periodic data, and the unknowns are P-periodic symmetric matrix variables X(k) = X(k+P) (or, equivalently, scalar decision variables x_i(k)) coupled across k by the periodic system dynamics (typical examples include periodic Lyapunov inequalities A(k)ᵀ X(k+1) A(k) − X(k) + Q(k) ≺ 0 with X(k) = X(k+P) ≻ 0, and their Bounded Real / KYP-type variants).

Problem. Design numerically efficient algorithms that solve such periodic LMIs by exploiting the periodic structure (rather than lifting the system to a single, large time-invariant LMI of dimension proportional to P), with computational cost and storage scaling favorably in the period P and the state dimension n, and with provable numerical stability. In particular, give an algorithm that:

(i) decides feasibility of the periodic LMI system above;
(ii) when feasible, produces a P-periodic symmetric solution X(0), …, X(P−1);
(iii) avoids forming the lifted block-diagonal LMI of size nP × nP whenever possible, and admits structure-preserving (e.g., periodic Schur / periodic QZ based) implementations.

Prove convergence and analyze the per-iteration complexity of the proposed algorithm.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question is a form of the logarithmic Green–Griffiths / Lang conjecture for complements of normal-crossings divisors in projective space. Known unconditional algebraic-degeneracy results require very high degree bounds (e.g. effective bounds of the form $d \geq n^{(n+1)^{n+5}}$ for generic hypersurfaces), and the sharp threshold $\deg(D)\geq n+2$ remains unresolved in general; only partial results (generic divisors, special configurations of hyperplanes/hypersurfaces) are available.

Consider a continuous-time linear periodic (LTP) state-space system

  dx(t)/dt = A(t) x(t) + B(t) u(t),
  y(t)     = C(t) x(t) + D(t) u(t),

where A(t), B(t), C(t), D(t) are real matrix-valued functions of period T > 0 (i.e., A(t+T) = A(t), and similarly for B, C, D). For such a system, the frequency response is described by the harmonic transfer function (equivalently, the frequency-response operator obtained from the EMP/harmonic-balance representation), which assigns to each frequency ω in a fundamental band an infinite-dimensional operator relating input harmonics u_k e^{i(ω + kΩ)t} (Ω = 2π/T) to output harmonics y_k e^{i(ω + kΩ)t}.

Problem. Devise numerically reliable algorithms that, given the periodic data (A(·), B(·), C(·), D(·)) in a standard representation (e.g. truncated Fourier series, piecewise-constant, or sampled coefficients), compute, in a computationally efficient way, the frequency response of the system at a prescribed grid of frequencies ω, with provable error bounds and complexity that scales favorably with the harmonic truncation order, the state dimension, and the number of evaluation frequencies.

In particular, produce algorithms that avoid forming and decomposing the full doubly-infinite Toeplitz-like operator at each frequency, exploit structure (sparsity, decay/roll-off of harmonics, monodromy/Floquet factorizations) of the periodic data, and achieve efficiency comparable to that available for the time-invariant case.

Let $V = \mathbb{R}\times S^3$ be equipped with a smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ such that $(V,g)$ is a globally hyperbolic, maximally extended (i.e., maximal globally hyperbolic) solution of either the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$, or the Einstein–Maxwell equations
$$\mathrm{Ric}(g)-\tfrac12 R(g)\,g = 8\pi T[F],\qquad dF=0,\quad d\star F=0,$$
where $F$ is a 2-form on $V$ and $T[F]_{\mu\nu}=F_{\mu\alpha}F_\nu{}^\alpha-\tfrac14 g_{\mu\nu}F_{\alpha\beta}F^{\alpha\beta}$.

A spacelike hypersurface $\Sigma\subset V$ is called maximal if its mean curvature with respect to the future-directed unit normal vanishes identically. The spacetime $(V,g)$ is said to admit a constant-mean-curvature (CMC) foliation if there exists a smooth foliation of $V$ by closed spacelike Cauchy hypersurfaces, each having (spatially) constant mean curvature, with the value of that mean curvature serving as a smooth time function on $V$. A big bang (resp. big crunch) is an incomplete past (resp. future) boundary at which suitable curvature invariants of $g$ blow up.

Prove the following: every such $(V,g)$ contains a maximal hypersurface and possesses both a big bang and a big crunch. Let $V = \mathbb{R}\times S^3$ be equipped with a smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ such that $(V,g)$ is a globally hyperbolic, maximally extended (i.e., maximal globally hyperbolic) solution of either the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$, or the Einstein–Maxwell equations
$$\mathrm{Ric}(g)-\tfrac12 R(g)\,g = 8\pi T[F],\qquad dF=0,\quad d\star F=0,$$
where $F$ is a 2-form on $V$ and $T[F]_{\mu\nu}=F_{\mu\alpha}F_\nu{}^\alpha-\tfrac14 g_{\mu\nu}F_{\alpha\beta}F^{\alpha\beta}$.

A spacelike hypersurface $\Sigma\subset V$ is called maximal if its mean curvature with respect to the future-directed unit normal vanishes identically. The spacetime $(V,g)$ is said to admit a constant-mean-curvature (CMC) foliation if there exists a smooth foliation of $V$ by closed spacelike Cauchy hypersurfaces, each having (spatially) constant mean curvature, with the value of that mean curvature serving as a smooth time function on $V$. A big bang (resp. big crunch) is an incomplete past (resp. future) boundary at which suitable curvature invariants of $g$ blow up.

Prove the following: every such $(V,g)$ contains a maximal hypersurface and possesses both a big bang and a big crunch. Equivalently, decide whether any maximal globally hyperbolic vacuum or Einstein–Maxwell solution on $\mathbb{R}\times S^3$ can fail to admit a CMC foliation. Treat in particular the spatially homogeneous Bianchi IX case, in which $g$ is invariant under a transitive left action of $SU(2)$ on each $\{t\}\times S^3$.

Consider a continuous-time linear periodic system
\[
\dot x(t) = A(t)x(t) + B(t)u(t),\qquad t\in\mathbb{R},
\]
where $A:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ and $B:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}$ are piecewise continuous and $T$-periodic, i.e. $A(t+T)=A(t)$ and $B(t+T)=B(t)$ for some fixed period $T>0$. The pair $(A(\cdot),B(\cdot))$ is assumed to be stabilizable in the periodic sense: there exists a piecewise continuous $T$-periodic feedback gain $F:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ such that the monodromy matrix $\Phi_{A+BF}(T,0)$ of the closed-loop system $\dot x = (A(t)+B(t)F(t))x$ has spectral radius strictly less than $1$.

Develop an effective numerical algorithm that, working directly in the periodic continuous-time setting (without first reducing the problem to a single time-invariant lifted system or to its discrete-time monodromy representation), computes such a $T$-periodic stabilizing feedback gain $F(\cdot)$. The algorithm should:
(i) take as input numerically tractable representations of $A(\cdot)$ and $B(\cdot)$ (e.g.\ truncated Fourier series, piecewise polynomial samples, or evaluations along one period);
(ii) return a $T$-periodic feedback $F(\cdot)$ in a comparable representation;
(iii) guarantee, under standard regularity hypotheses on $(A,B)$, that the resulting closed-loop monodromy matrix is Schur-stable; and
(iv) be efficient and numerically reliable in the sense that its computational cost and conditioning scale gracefully with $n$, $m$, and the complexity of the representation of $A(\cdot)$, $B(\cdot)$.

Does such an effective stabilization algorithm exist for general continuous-time linear periodic systems?

There has been substantial progress on stabilization and pole assignment for linear periodic systems. Methods include periodic Lyapunov differential equation–based feedback, variation-of-constant discretization plus sequential pole placement, parametric periodic state feedback for the discrete-time case, and LMI-based approaches. However, most general-purpose continuous-time algorithms still proceed via discretization or lifting; truly direct, efficient, numerically reliable continuous-time periodic stabilization algorithms with the same maturity as the discrete-time case have only partially been developed.

Let $f:\mathbb{C}^m \to \mathbb{P}^n$ be a holomorphic mapping. For an effective divisor $D$ on $\mathbb{P}^n$ whose support does not contain the image of $f$, let $N(D,r)$ denote the counting function of $f^{-1}(D)$ and $T(r)$ the (Cartan) characteristic function of $f$, defined in the usual sense of Nevanlinna value-distribution theory. For a complete linear system $|D|$ on $\mathbb{P}^n$ with measure $d\mu$ induced by a unitary structure, let $\delta(D)=1-\limsup_{r\to\infty} N(D,r)/T(r)$ be the Nevanlinna defect.

Construct, for every pair $(m,n)$ with $1\le m\le n$, a non-empty class $\mathcal{F}_{m,n}$ of holomorphic maps $f:\mathbb{C}^m \to \mathbb{P}^n$ such that all of the following hold:

(i) (First Main Theorem inequality) For every $f \in \mathcal{F}_{m,n}$ and every effective divisor $D$ on $\mathbb{P}^n$ whose support omits $f(\mathbb{C}^m)$,
$$N(D,r) \le T(r) + O(1).$$

(ii) (Liouville-type defect relation) For every $f \in \mathcal{F}_{m,n}$ and every complete linear system $|D|$ on $\mathbb{P}^n$,
$$\int_{D \in |D|} \delta(D)\, d\mu(D) = 0.$$

(iii) (Functorial restriction) For every $f \in \mathcal{F}_{m,n}$ and every linear embedding $\iota:\mathbb{C}^k \hookrightarrow \mathbb{C}^m$ with $1\le k\le m$, the restriction $f \circ \iota$ belongs to $\mathcal{F}_{k,n}$.

Determine whether such a class $\mathcal{F}_{m,n}$ exists in higher codimension (i.e., when $m<n$), and if so, give an explicit characterization that is broad enough to be geometrically and analytically natural.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The problem of identifying a natural subclass of holomorphic mappings from $\mathbb{C}^m$ to $\mathbb{P}^n$ in higher codimension that simultaneously satisfies a First Main Theorem inequality, a Liouville-type integrated defect relation, and a functorial restriction property is a long-standing program in higher-dimensional Nevanlinna theory. Existing approaches (Griffiths, Ahlfors, Stoll, and the differentiably non-degenerate framework) handle special cases (equidimensional or non-degenerate maps), and the Ahlfors theorem is noted as one of the few global treatments of higher codimension. No general construction satisfying all three properties simultaneously appears in the literature; the question remains open.

Consider a continuous-time linear periodic system
\[
\dot{x}(t) = A(t)\,x(t) + B(t)\,u(t), \qquad t \in \mathbb{R},
\]
where $x(t) \in \mathbb{R}^n$, $u(t) \in \mathbb{R}^m$, and the matrix-valued maps $A:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ and $B:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}$ are piecewise continuous and $T$-periodic, i.e. $A(t+T)=A(t)$ and $B(t+T)=B(t)$ for some fixed period $T>0$. For a $T$-periodic state-feedback gain $F:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, the closed-loop system $\dot{x}(t) = (A(t)+B(t)F(t))\,x(t)$ has monodromy matrix
\[
\Phi_F(T,0) = \text{state-transition matrix from $0$ to $T$ of } A(\cdot)+B(\cdot)F(\cdot),
\]
whose eigenvalues (the characteristic multipliers of the closed-loop system) determine its Floquet/Lyapunov exponents and stability behaviour. Define the closed-loop "poles" of the periodic system as these characteristic multipliers (or, equivalently, the corresponding characteristic exponents).

Pole-assignment problem. Given a self-conjugate set $\Lambda = \{\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n\} \subset \mathbb{C}$, develop a numerical algorithm that, under suitable controllability hypotheses on $(A(\cdot),B(\cdot))$, computes a $T$-periodic feedback gain $F(\cdot)$ such that the characteristic multipliers of $A(\cdot)+B(\cdot)F(\cdot)$ coincide with $\Lambda$, and that does so:

(i) efficiently, with computational cost comparable to that of the best modern pole-assignment methods for time-invariant systems;

(ii) reliably, in a numerically stable manner that avoids explicit formation of the monodromy matrix or other ill-conditioned intermediate quantities;

(iii) directly in the continuous-time periodic setting, without recourse to lifting the system to a time-invariant or discrete-time equivalent.

Does such an algorithm exist, and if so, provide one with a complete numerical analysis (stability, conditioning, complexity, and robustness of the assignment)?

Consider a continuous-time linear periodic system on the real line, in which all coefficient matrices are continuous and T-periodic for some fixed period T>0. A periodic differential linear matrix inequality (PDLMI) on such a system is a constraint of the form

    F(t, X(t), \dot X(t)) \prec 0   for all t \in \mathbb{R},

where the unknown is a continuously differentiable, symmetric, T-periodic matrix-valued function X: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{S}^n (i.e. X(t+T) = X(t) and X(t)^\top = X(t)), and F is an affine map in (X, \dot X) whose coefficient matrices are continuous and T-periodic in t. A typical instance is the Lyapunov-type PDLMI

    A(t)^\top X(t) + X(t) A(t) + \dot X(t) + Q(t) \prec 0,   X(t+T) = X(t), X(t) \succ 0,

with continuous T-periodic A, Q.

Develop new computational methods (algorithms, with associated convergence and numerical reliability guarantees) for deciding feasibility of, and computing periodic solutions X(\cdot) to, general periodic differential linear matrix inequalities of the above type. In particular, design procedures that (i) handle the infinite-dimensional periodicity constraint without naive time gridding losing the periodic structure, (ii) exploit structural properties of the periodic coefficients (such as monodromy, characteristic multipliers, or representations via piecewise polynomial / Fourier / spline bases for X), and (iii) admit provable accuracy bounds on the computed X(\cdot) relative to the continuous PDLMI.

Several computational approaches to differential LMIs have appeared since the question was raised, including outer-linearization convex programming methods, piecewise-quadratic ansätze, and discretization-based reductions to standard LMI systems (e.g. Gershon-type and sampled-data DLMI methods, and the JOTA 2020 piecewise-polynomial scheme). This is the Green-Griffiths(-Lang) conjecture specialized to surfaces of general type. It is known to be open in general for surfaces of general type, but has been established in important cases: McQuillan proved it for projective surfaces of general type satisfying $c_1^2 > c_2$ (positive second Segre number), via the foliation/Ahlfors-Nevanlinna theory approach. Further partial results exist for surfaces with additional structure (e.g., certain foliated surfaces, Shimura surfaces, and generic high-degree hypersurfaces in higher dimensions by Diverio-Merker-Rousseau and Demailly). The general case for arbitrary surfaces of general type remains unresolved.

A vacuum Robinson–Trautman spacetime is a four-dimensional Lorentzian manifold admitting a shear-free, twist-free, expanding null geodesic congruence and satisfying the vacuum Einstein equations R_{μν}=0. In suitable coordinates (u, r, x^A) on a manifold of the form M = N × R_u × R_r (with N a closed 2-surface), the metric takes the form
   g = -H(u,r,x) du^2 - 2 du dr + r^2 h_{AB}(u,x) dx^A dx^B,
where h(u,·) is a smooth family of Riemannian metrics on N conformal to a fixed reference metric, and H = K(u,x) - 2m(u)/r - 2r (∂_u log Ω), with K the Gauss curvature of h and m(u) the mass function. The vacuum field equations reduce to the Robinson–Trautman equation
   12 m ∂_u (log Ω) = Δ_h K,
where Δ_h is the Laplace–Beltrami operator of h. Assume N is the 2-sphere S^2, the underlying manifold is S^2 × R (so the spatial cross-sections are spheres), and the mass m is a positive constant.

(a) Prove that any such vacuum Robinson–Trautman solution on S^2 × R with positive mass is isometric to the Schwarzschild metric (equivalently, h is, up to diffeomorphism, the round metric on S^2 and Ω is constant in u).

(b) Formulate and decide the analogous rigidity statement for the Einstein–Maxwell Robinson–Trautman equations, i.e. when the vacuum equations are replaced by the Einstein equations coupled to a source-free Maxwell field aligned with the null congruence: determine whether the only solutions on S^2 × R with positive mass are the Reissner–Nordström metrics.

By a theorem of Siu and Yeung, a nonconstant holomorphic map from the complex line to an abelian variety must intersect every ample divisor (in fact the defect vanishes). Combined with the classical Bloch theorem describing the Zariski closure of such an entire curve as a translate of an abelian subvariety, this resolves the question affirmatively for effective divisors on abelian varieties.

A probability density $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to[0,\infty)$ is called logconcave if $\log f$ is concave on its support (with the convention $\log 0=-\infty$), and isotropic if a random vector $X$ with density $f$ satisfies $\mathbb{E}[X]=0$ and $\mathbb{E}[XX^\top]=I_n$ (the $n\times n$ identity matrix). For such a vector $X$, write $\|X\|^2=\sum_{i=1}^n X_i^2$ and $\mathrm{Var}_f(\|X\|^2)=\mathbb{E}[\|X\|^4]-(\mathbb{E}[\|X\|^2])^2$.

Prove or disprove: there exists an absolute constant $C>0$ (independent of $n$ and of $f$) such that, for every dimension $n\geq 1$ and every isotropic logconcave density $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$,
$$\mathrm{Var}_f(\|X\|^2)\leq C\,n.$$

Let $(M,g_0,K_0)$ be a smooth vacuum cosmological initial data set, where $M$ is a closed (compact, without boundary) connected $3$-manifold, $g_0$ is a Riemannian metric on $M$, and $K_0$ is a symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor on $M$ representing the second fundamental form. Assume that the data are of constant-mean-curvature (CMC) type, i.e. $\operatorname{tr}_{g_0} K_0$ is a constant on $M$, and that $(g_0,K_0)$ satisfies the vacuum Einstein constraint equations
$$R(g_0) - |K_0|_{g_0}^2 + (\operatorname{tr}_{g_0}K_0)^2 = 0, \qquad \operatorname{div}_{g_0} K_0 - d(\operatorname{tr}_{g_0} K_0) = 0.$$
Assume further that the Ricci curvature of $g_0$ is positive definite, i.e. $\operatorname{Ric}(g_0) > 0$ as a quadratic form on $TM$.

Let $(\mathcal{M},\mathbf{g})$ denote the maximal globally hyperbolic vacuum development of $(M,g_0,K_0)$, foliated (in a neighborhood of the initial slice) by CMC hypersurfaces $\Sigma_t$ with induced metric $g(t)$ and second fundamental form $K(t)$, with $g(0)=g_0$, $K(0)=K_0$.

Prove that the Einstein evolution preserves Ricci positivity in the following sense: there exists a (maximal) interval of CMC time on which the induced spatial metric $g(t)$ satisfies $\operatorname{Ric}(g(t)) > 0$ for every $t$ for which $\Sigma_t$ is defined. Equivalently, show that positivity of the spatial Ricci curvature on the initial CMC slice is propagated by the vacuum Einstein evolution along the CMC foliation.

$$\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} x\, f(x)\,dx = 0, \qquad \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} x_i x_j\, f(x)\,dx = \delta_{ij} \text{ for all } 1\le i,j\le n.$$

$$f(0) \le C^n\,?$$

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

Bourgain's slicing (hyperplane) conjecture, equivalent to the existence of a universal constant C with f(0) ≤ C^n for every isotropic logconcave density on R^n, was affirmatively resolved in late 2024. Klartag and Lehec, building on a stochastic-localization small-ball bound of Qingyang Guan and stability estimates of Eldan–Mikulincer, established the conjecture; an alternative proof via small-ball estimates was given by Bizeul (arXiv:2501.06854, 2025).

Let $\mathcal{M}$ denote the class of complete, connected, smooth, asymptotically flat Riemannian 3-manifolds $(M,g)$ with nonnegative scalar curvature, where asymptotic flatness is taken in the standard sense: outside a compact set, $M$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3 \setminus \overline{B}$ via a chart in which the metric satisfies $g_{ij} = \delta_{ij} + O(|x|^{-\tau})$ with appropriate decay $\tau > 1/2$ on derivatives so that the ADM mass
$$m_{ADM}(M,g) = \lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{1}{16\pi}\int_{S_r}(\partial_j g_{ij} - \partial_i g_{jj})\,\nu^i\,dA$$
is well defined and finite. Assume in addition that either $M$ has no boundary or $\partial M$ is a (possibly empty) union of minimal 2-spheres (an outermost horizon).

Consider sequences $(M_k,g_k,p_k) \in \mathcal{M}$ of pointed asymptotically flat 3-manifolds satisfying:
(i) a uniform mass bound $m_{ADM}(M_k,g_k) \le m_0 < \infty$;
(ii) a uniform geometric bound, for instance a uniform lower bound on the volumes of unit balls $\mathrm{Vol}(B_1(p_k)) \ge v_0 > 0$, together with uniform asymptotic decay constants in the definition of asymptotic flatness.

Prove that any such sequence admits a subsequence which converges, in a suitable weak topology on the space of asymptotically flat Riemannian 3-manifolds (e.g., pointed Gromov–Hausdorff or Sormani–Wenger intrinsic flat convergence), to a limit pointed metric space $(M_\infty, d_\infty, p_\infty)$. Determine the optimal regularity class to which the limit belongs (for example: Riemannian manifold of class $C^0$, $W^{1,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, or integral current space with nonnegative generalized scalar curvature in a weak sense), and verify that the ADM mass is lower semicontinuous along the convergence.

The general weak compactness question for asymptotically flat 3-manifolds with bounded mass and bounded geometry has seen substantial progress but is not fully resolved. Partial results include intrinsic-flat convergence and Gromov-Hausdorff stability theorems by Lakzian–Sormani, Huang–Lee–Sormani, Allen–Sormani, and others, including stability of the positive mass theorem (recent work by Dong–Song, Kazaras, et al., culminating in Stability of Euclidean 3-space, Inventiones 2024). However, a complete weak compactness theorem identifying optimal limiting regularity remains open in general.

Let $(M^3, g)$ be a smooth, complete, asymptotically flat Riemannian 3-manifold with nonnegative scalar curvature, having a single end on which $g$ approaches the Euclidean metric in the standard asymptotically flat sense, so that the ADM mass $m_{ADM}(M,g)$ is well defined. For a closed oriented surface $\Sigma \subset M$ with mean curvature $H$ and area $|\Sigma|$, define the Hawking (Geroch) mass
$$m_H(\Sigma) = \sqrt{\frac{|\Sigma|}{16\pi}}\left(1 - \frac{1}{16\pi}\int_\Sigma H^2\, d\mu\right).$$
Geroch's argument shows that if $\{\Sigma_t\}_{t\in[0,\infty)}$ is a smooth foliation of (an end of) $M$ by 2-spheres evolving by inverse mean curvature flow $\partial_t x = H^{-1}\nu$, then $m_H(\Sigma_t)$ is monotone non-decreasing, and $m_H(\Sigma_t) \to m_{ADM}$ as $t\to\infty$ provided the leaves become asymptotically round.

Carry out the following program to obtain a proof of the positive mass theorem in this setting:

(a) Prove that for any such $(M^3,g)$ (under suitable additional hypotheses to be made precise, e.g. existence of a sufficiently small or area-minimizing initial 2-sphere), there exists a smooth foliation $\{\Sigma_t\}$ of $M$ minus a compact set by 2-spheres which (i) starts from a surface $\Sigma_0$ with $m_H(\Sigma_0) \geq 0$, (ii) solves inverse mean curvature flow for all $t \geq 0$, and (iii) becomes asymptotically round at infinity so that $m_H(\Sigma_t) \to m_{ADM}$.

(b) Using the existence of this foliation together with Geroch's monotonicity formula, conclude that $m_{ADM}(M,g) \geq 0$, with equality only if $(M,g)$ is isometric to Euclidean $\mathbb{R}^3$.

(a) Prove that for any such $(M^3,g)$ (under suitable additional hypotheses to be made precise, e.g. existence of a sufficiently small or area-minimizing initial 2-sphere), there exists a smooth foliation $\{\Sigma_t\}$ of $M$ minus a compact set by 2-spheres which (i) starts from a surface $\Sigma_0$ with $m_H(\Sigma_0) \geq 0$, (ii) solves inverse mean curvature flow for all $t \geq 0$, and (iii) becomes asymptotically round at infinity so that $m_H(\Sigma_t) \to m_{ADM}$.

(b) Using the existence of this foliation together with Geroch's monotonicity formula, conclude that $m_{ADM}(M,g) \geq 0$, with equality only if $(M,g)$ is isometric to Euclidean $\mathbb{R}^3$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Geroch's monotonicity of the Hawking mass under smooth inverse mean curvature flow has long been known; the central difficulty was producing the required foliation, since smooth IMCF generically develops singularities. Huisken and Ilmanen (J. Differential Geom. 59 (2001), 353–437) developed a theory of weak (level-set) solutions of inverse mean curvature flow and used Geroch monotonicity to prove the Riemannian Penrose inequality for a single horizon component, which in particular yields a proof of the Riemannian positive mass theorem along Geroch's lines. Existence of smooth IMCF foliations under stronger hypotheses has been established in subsequent works (e.g. Huisken–Ilmanen, and later constructions of smooth IMCF foliations on asymptotically flat 3-manifolds). Thus the program is essentially carried out via weak solutions; existence of fully smooth Geroch foliations on general asymptotically flat 3-manifolds remains a delicate problem.

In general relativity, given a spacelike 2-surface $\Sigma$ bounding a compact spacelike region in a 4-dimensional spacetime $(M,g)$ satisfying the Einstein equations, several inequivalent definitions of the quasi-local mass (or quasi-local energy-momentum) associated with $\Sigma$ have been proposed, including (but not limited to) the Hawking mass, the Bartnik mass, the Brown–York mass, the Hawking–Horowitz energy, the Penrose (twistorial) mass, the Liu–Yau mass, the Wang–Yau mass, and the Kijowski–Epp–Liu–Yau type expressions. Each is constructed so as to: (i) be non-negative under suitable energy conditions, (ii) vanish in flat spacetime for appropriate surfaces, and (iii) tend to the ADM mass and the Bondi mass under limits of surfaces approaching spatial infinity and null infinity, respectively.

Determine and explain the precise mathematical relationships among these definitions. In particular, for a general bounding 2-surface $\Sigma$ in a spacetime obeying the dominant energy condition, establish inequalities, equalities, or limiting equivalences that relate the various quasi-local mass functionals to one another, identify the geometric and physical conditions under which any two of them coincide, and clarify whether there exists a single universal quasi-local mass functional that reduces to or bounds the others in appropriate regimes.

Let $\mathbb{U}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disk. For analytic functions $f,F:\mathbb{U}\to\mathbb{C}$, recall that $f$ is subordinate to $F$, written $f\prec F$, if there exists an analytic self-map $\omega:\mathbb{U}\to\mathbb{U}$ with $\omega(0)=0$ such that $f(z)=F(\omega(z))$ for all $z\in\mathbb{U}$. A function $F$ analytic in $\mathbb{U}$ is called convex in $\mathbb{U}$ if it is univalent there and $F(\mathbb{U})$ is a convex subset of $\mathbb{C}$.

Suppose
$$f(z)=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} a_k z^k \prec F(z)=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} b_k z^k$$
in $\mathbb{U}$, where $F$ is convex in $\mathbb{U}$. It is known that for every positive integer $n\ge 1$ and every even integer $p\ge 2$,
$$\sum_{k=1}^{n} |a_k|^p \le \sum_{k=1}^{n} |b_k|^p.$$

Determine the set of real exponents $p\ge 2$ for which this inequality holds for every $n\ge 1$ and every such pair $f\prec F$ with $F$ convex. In particular, does the inequality remain valid for a set of exponents $p\ge 2$ strictly larger than the even integers (for example, on a dense subset, or on an interval, or for all real $p\ge 2$)?

Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple planar graph with maximum degree $\Delta$. A distant-2 coloring of $G$ is a function $c\colon V\to\mathbb{N}$ such that $c(u)\neq c(v)$ whenever the graph distance between $u$ and $v$ is $1$ or $2$ (equivalently, a proper vertex coloring of the square $G^2$). Let $\chi_2(G)$ denote the minimum number of colors in any distant-2 coloring of $G$.

Prove or disprove the following bounds:
(a) If $4 \le \Delta \le 7$, then $\chi_2(G) \le \Delta + 5$.
(b) If $\Delta \ge 8$, then $\chi_2(G) \le \lfloor 3\Delta/2 \rfloor + 1$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Wegner's conjecture on the chromatic number of the square of a planar graph remains open for all maximum degrees Δ ≥ 4. The case Δ = 3 (not part of this question) was settled by Thomassen and independently by Hartke–Jahanbekam–Thomas. For Δ = 4 the best known upper bound is 12 (Bousquet–Deschamps–de Meyer–Pierron), still above the conjectured 9. Havet, van den Heuvel, McDiarmid, and Reed proved the conjecture asymptotically (i.e., χ(G²) ≤ (3/2)Δ(1+o(1))) for large Δ, but the exact bound ⌊3Δ/2⌋+1 has not been established.

For an integer $d \ge 1$, let $Q_d$ denote the $d$-dimensional hypercube graph: its vertex set is $\{0,1\}^d$, and two vertices are adjacent if and only if they differ in exactly one coordinate. An orientation of $Q_d$ is an assignment of a direction to each edge, producing a directed graph; it is called a strong orientation if the resulting digraph is strongly connected (i.e., for any ordered pair of vertices $u,v$ there is a directed path from $u$ to $v$). A directed cycle of length $\ell$ in an oriented graph is a sequence $v_0, v_1, \dots, v_{\ell-1}, v_\ell = v_0$ of distinct vertices (except $v_0 = v_\ell$) such that each $(v_i, v_{i+1})$ is a directed edge.

Question: Does there exist an absolute integer constant $c$, independent of $d$, such that for every $d \ge 2$ and every strong orientation of $Q_d$, the resulting digraph contains a directed cycle of length at most $c$?

A graph G on n vertices is called t-degenerate if every subgraph of G contains a vertex of degree at most t. A radio labeling (in this setting) of G is an injective assignment L : V(G) → ℤ⁺ of positive integers to the vertices such that |L(u) − L(v)| ≥ 2 whenever u and v are adjacent in G; the span of L is max_{v ∈ V(G)} L(v).

A pre-labeling L′ is an injective assignment of positive integers to a (possibly empty) subset S ⊆ V(G); a radio labeling L of G extends L′ if L(v) = L′(v) for every v ∈ S. Define
   M = max( n, max_{v ∈ S} L′(v) ).

Prove or disprove: for every t-degenerate graph G on n vertices and every pre-labeling L′ of a subset of V(G), there exists a radio labeling of G that extends L′ and has span at most M + 3t.

A tournament is a directed graph $T=(V,A)$ obtained by orienting each edge of a complete undirected graph; equivalently, for every pair of distinct vertices $u,v\in V$ exactly one of the arcs $(u,v)$ or $(v,u)$ belongs to $A$. A spanning out-arborescence (out-branching) of $T$ rooted at a vertex $y$ is a spanning subdigraph $B^+\subseteq T$ that is a tree when its arcs are regarded as undirected edges, and in which every vertex except $y$ has exactly one entering arc (so there is a unique directed path from $y$ to every other vertex). A spanning in-arborescence (in-branching) of $T$ rooted at a vertex $x$ is defined analogously but with every vertex except $x$ having exactly one outgoing arc (so there is a unique directed path from every vertex to $x$). A leaf of a branching is a vertex whose out-degree (in the out-branching) or in-degree (in the in-branching) within the branching is zero. Two branchings are arc-disjoint if they share no arc.

Problem. Determine the computational complexity, and provide a structural characterization, of the following decision problem:

Input: a tournament $T$, two (not necessarily distinct) vertices $x,y\in V(T)$, and a non-negative integer $k$.

Question: does $T$ contain a spanning in-arborescence $B^-$ rooted at $x$ and a spanning out-arborescence $B^+$ rooted at $y$ such that $B^-$ and $B^+$ are arc-disjoint and each of $B^-$ and $B^+$ has at most $k$ leaves?

Without the leaf restriction, the existence of arc-disjoint in- and out-branchings with prescribed roots in a tournament (and more generally in semicomplete digraphs) is known to admit a polynomial-time decision algorithm (Bang-Jensen's conjecture, established for tournaments and extended to semicomplete digraphs in 2023). The status therefore appears to be unresolved based on available sources.

For an oriented graph $D$ and a subset $X\subseteq V$, the inversion of $X$ in $D$ is the oriented graph obtained from $D$ by reversing every arc whose two endpoints both lie in $X$.

Define the inversion graph $\mathcal{L}(G)$ as follows: its vertex set is the set of all orientations of $G$, and two orientations $D_1,D_2$ are joined by an edge of $\mathcal{L}(G)$ if and only if there exists a set $X\subseteq V$ such that inverting $X$ in $D_1$ yields $D_2$.

Let $\Delta(G)$ denote the maximum degree of $G$, and let $\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{L}(G))$ denote the diameter of $\mathcal{L}(G)$.

(a) Determine $\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{L}(G))$ as a function of $G$.

(b) In particular, decide whether the inequality
$$\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{L}(G)) \le \Delta(G)$$
holds for every graph $G$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The conjecture diam(L(G)) ≤ Δ(G) was formulated by Havet, Hörsch and Rambaud, who proved the upper bound 2Δ − 1 in general and verified the conjecture for Δ = 3 with computer assistance. Subsequent work has established the bound Δ + log Δ for triangle-free graphs and obtained results relating inversion diameter to treewidth and to 2-edge-colored homomorphisms, but the full conjecture remains open.

A graph G = (V, E) is called a cograph if it can be constructed from single vertices by repeated applications of disjoint union and complete join (equivalently, G contains no induced path on four vertices).

A radio labeling (also called L(2,1)-distance-2 labeling in the strict-injective sense used here) of G is an injective assignment f: V → ℤ_{>0} of pairwise distinct positive integers to the vertices such that |f(u) − f(v)| ≥ 2 whenever uv ∈ E. The span of f is max_{v∈V} f(v), and an optimum radio labeling is one of minimum span.

For a fixed nonnegative integer l, the problem p-RL(l) is defined as follows. An instance consists of a graph G together with a partial labeling f₀: S → ℤ_{>0}, where S ⊆ V satisfies |S| = l and f₀ is injective and respects the radio-labeling constraint on the vertices in S. The task is to compute a radio labeling f of G that extends f₀ (i.e. f(v) = f₀(v) for all v ∈ S) and has minimum span among all such extensions.

Determine the computational complexity of p-RL(l) when the input graph G is restricted to be a cograph: for each fixed l ≥ 1, is p-RL(l) on cographs solvable in polynomial time, or is it NP-hard?

Let CMSO denote counting monadic second-order logic over relational structures. A tournament is a directed graph T=(V(T),E(T)) such that for every pair of distinct vertices x,y exactly one of (x,y) or (y,x) belongs to E(T). The clique-width of a tournament is defined analogously to the undirected case, using the operations of introducing a single-labeled vertex, taking disjoint union, adding all arcs in one direction between vertices of two given labels, and relabeling.

Given a finite set C of colors, a C-coloring of T is a map λ:V(T)→C; the resulting structure (T,λ) is regarded as a relational structure equipping the tournament with unary predicates indexed by C. A CMSO formula φ(x,y) with two free first-order variables and access to the predicates of (T,λ) interprets a total order on V(T) if the binary relation

  { (x,y) ∈ V(T)×V(T) : (T,λ) ⊨ φ(x,y) }

is a strict total order on V(T).

Question: Fix a class 𝒞 of tournaments of bounded clique-width. Do there exist a finite set of colors C and a CMSO formula φ(x,y) such that, for every tournament T ∈ 𝒞, one can choose a coloring λ:V(T)→C with the property that φ interprets a total order on V(T) inside (T,λ)?

Let G=(V,E) be a finite simple graph. A radio labeling of G is an injective function f: V → ℤ_{>0} such that for every pair of distinct vertices u,v ∈ V,
   |f(u) − f(v)| ≥ diam(G) + 1 − d_G(u,v),
where d_G denotes the graph distance and diam(G) is the diameter of G. The span of f is max_{v∈V} f(v); a minimum-span radio labeling is one minimizing this quantity.

In the problem p-RL(*), the input consists of a graph G together with a partial labeling, i.e. an injective function f_0 : S → ℤ_{>0} defined on an arbitrary subset S ⊆ V (the number |S| of pre-labeled vertices is part of the input and is not bounded). The task is to extend f_0 to a radio labeling f of all of G of minimum possible span (or to decide, in the decision version, whether such an extension with span at most a given integer K exists).

Determine the computational complexity of p-RL(*) when G is restricted to:
 (a) the class of planar graphs;
 (b) the class of graphs of treewidth at most w, for fixed w.

(For comparison, when the number of pre-labeled vertices is bounded by a fixed constant l, the corresponding problem p-RL(l) is known to be polynomial-time solvable on both classes.)

Let $D=(V,A)$ be a finite digraph. A linear ordering (enumeration) $L$ of $V$ is a bijection from $V$ to $\{1,2,\dots,|V|\}$. A directed path $v_{i_1}\to v_{i_2}\to\cdots\to v_{i_r}$ in $D$ is said to be forward in $L$ if $L(v_{i_1})<L(v_{i_2})<\cdots<L(v_{i_r})$, i.e., its vertices appear in $L$ in the same order as the orientation of the path.

A family of orderings $L_1,\dots,L_k$ of $V(D)$ is called a forward cover of $D$ if for every pair of distinct vertices $u,v\in V(D)$ there exists an index $\ell\in\{1,\dots,k\}$ such that $L_\ell$ contains a forward path from $u$ to $v$, or there exists an index $\ell'\in\{1,\dots,k\}$ such that $L_{\ell'}$ contains a forward path from $v$ to $u$.

Determine the smallest integer $k$ (if any) such that every digraph $D$ admits a forward cover of size $k$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Recent work on "forward covers" of digraphs poses this exact question and conjectures that every strong digraph on n vertices admits a forward cover of size O(log n); the conjecture is established for bi-oriented graphs, but the general problem (and in particular whether a constant k suffices, or any tight bound) appears to remain open.

Let $D=(V,A)$ be a digraph. A directed path-decomposition of $D$ is a sequence $(X_1,X_2,\dots,X_r)$ of subsets of $V$ (called bags) such that:
(1) $\bigcup_{i=1}^{r} X_i = V$;
(2) for every vertex $v\in V$, the set of indices $\{i : v\in X_i\}$ forms a contiguous interval $[a_v,b_v]\subseteq\{1,\dots,r\}$;
(3) for every arc $(u,v)\in A$, there exist indices $i\le j$ with $u\in X_i$ and $v\in X_j$ (equivalently, $a_u\le b_v$).
The width of such a decomposition is $\max_{1\le i\le r}|X_i|-1$, and the directed pathwidth of $D$, denoted $\mathrm{dpw}(D)$, is the minimum width over all directed path-decompositions of $D$.

It is known that, for every fixed integer $k$, deciding whether $\mathrm{dpw}(D)\le k$ can be solved in time $n^{O(k)}$ on an $n$-vertex digraph (an XP algorithm).

Question: Does there exist a fixed-parameter tractable (FPT) algorithm for computing the directed pathwidth parameterized by the width? Equivalently, is there a computable function $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ and a constant $c$ such that, given a digraph $D$ on $n$ vertices and a positive integer $k$, one can decide whether $\mathrm{dpw}(D)\le k$ in time $f(k)\cdot n^{c}$?

XP algorithms running in $n^{O(k)}$ are known, and FPT results exist only for special classes (e.g., semi-complete digraphs/tournaments via FPT-approximation, or under alternative parameterizations such as vertex cover number), but no FPT algorithm for general digraphs has been reported.

Let $D \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded planar region (representing a geographic area), and let $Z : D 	imes [h_{\min}, h_{\max}] 	o \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ be an unknown nonnegative measurable function representing the local concentration (e.g., grade or density) of a spatially distributed underground resource such as coal or a mineral at horizontal location $x \in D$ and depth $h$. Define the total reserve as
$$R \;=\; \int_{D} \int_{h_{\min}}^{h_{\max}} Z(x,h)\, dh\, dx.$$
A sampling design consists of choosing a finite collection of borehole locations $x_1,\dots,x_n \in D$ (possibly chosen at random according to some probability law, or sequentially based on previous observations) and, at each $x_i$, observing $Z(x_i,h)$ on a depth interval (or on a finite set of depths) within $[h_{\min}, h_{\max}]$, possibly with measurement error.

Develop a theory of sampling for mapping the function $Z$ and for estimating the total reserve $R$. Specifically:

(a) Formulate a probabilistic model for $Z$ (for instance, treating $Z$ as a realization of a random field with prescribed mean and covariance structure) under which sampling designs and estimators can be compared.

(b) Construct an estimator $\widehat R$ of $R$ based on the sample $\{(x_i, Z(x_i,\cdot))\}_{i=1}^n$, and determine its bias, variance, and mean square error as functions of the sampling design and the underlying spatial covariance.

(c) Determine optimal (or admissible) sampling designs that minimize the mean square error of $\widehat R$ for fixed sample size $n$, including comparisons between simple random, systematic/grid, stratified, and adaptive sequential designs.

(d) Provide a method for producing a map (an estimate of $Z$ as a function of $(x,h)$) together with a quantitative measure of the mapping accuracy, and relate the optimal design for mapping to the optimal design for estimating $R$.
