Let $D \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded planar region (representing a geographic area), and let $Z : D 	imes [h_{\min}, h_{\max}] 	o \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ be an unknown nonnegative measurable function representing the local concentration (e.g., grade or density) of a spatially distributed underground resource such as coal or a mineral at horizontal location $x \in D$ and depth $h$. Define the total reserve as
$$R \;=\; \int_{D} \int_{h_{\min}}^{h_{\max}} Z(x,h)\, dh\, dx.$$
A sampling design consists of choosing a finite collection of borehole locations $x_1,\dots,x_n \in D$ (possibly chosen at random according to some probability law, or sequentially based on previous observations) and, at each $x_i$, observing $Z(x_i,h)$ on a depth interval (or on a finite set of depths) within $[h_{\min}, h_{\max}]$, possibly with measurement error.

Develop a theory of sampling for mapping the function $Z$ and for estimating the total reserve $R$. Specifically:

(a) Formulate a probabilistic model for $Z$ (for instance, treating $Z$ as a realization of a random field with prescribed mean and covariance structure) under which sampling designs and estimators can be compared.

(b) Construct an estimator $\widehat R$ of $R$ based on the sample $\{(x_i, Z(x_i,\cdot))\}_{i=1}^n$, and determine its bias, variance, and mean square error as functions of the sampling design and the underlying spatial covariance.

(c) Determine optimal (or admissible) sampling designs that minimize the mean square error of $\widehat R$ for fixed sample size $n$, including comparisons between simple random, systematic/grid, stratified, and adaptive sequential designs.

(d) Provide a method for producing a map (an estimate of $Z$ as a function of $(x,h)$) together with a quantitative measure of the mapping accuracy, and relate the optimal design for mapping to the optimal design for estimating $R$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The general question of developing sampling methodology for mapping spatially distributed underground resources has been substantially addressed since its original posing through the development of geostatistics (kriging, variogram modeling) by Matheron and others, and through later work on optimal spatial sampling designs and adaptive/sequential designs in mining and environmental statistics. However, no single closed solution exists; many specific subproblems (optimal designs under realistic covariance models, adaptive designs, non-stationary fields) remain active research topics. The problem as posed is therefore partially solved.

A digraph $D=(V,A)$ is a finite directed graph (loops and multiple arcs are excluded). A directed path is a sequence of distinct vertices $v_0,v_1,\dots,v_k$ together with the arcs $v_0v_1,v_1v_2,\dots,v_{k-1}v_k$. A linear forest in $D$ is a subdigraph whose arc set is a disjoint union of (the arc sets of) directed paths; equivalently, a spanning subdigraph in which every vertex has in-degree at most $1$ and out-degree at most $1$, and whose underlying graph is acyclic.

A partition of the arc set $A$ into two linear forests is a decomposition $A=A_1\sqcup A_2$ such that, for each $i\in\{1,2\}$, the spanning subdigraph $(V,A_i)$ is a linear forest.

Necessarily, in any such decomposition every vertex of $D$ must have in-degree at most $2$ and out-degree at most $2$. The problem is the following:

Is it true that every digraph $D$ with maximum in-degree at most $2$ and maximum out-degree at most $2$ admits a partition of its arc set into two linear forests? Equivalently, design an algorithm that, given such a digraph $D$, decides whether $A(D)$ can be partitioned into two linear forests, and produces such a partition when one exists.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The problem is connected to the linear arboricity of digraphs introduced by Nakayama and Péroche (1987), whose conjecture (every $d$-regular digraph has linear arboricity $d+1$) was disproved in 2017 for symmetric complete digraphs by He et al. A 2024 dichotomy result by Aubian, Hörsch et al. shows that decomposing a digraph into a $k$-bounded and an $\ell$-bounded directed linear forest is polynomial when $k+\ell\le 3$ and NP-complete otherwise, indicating that the unrestricted version of decomposition into two linear forests is computationally hard. The general existence question for digraphs of maximum in- and out-degree two is still not fully settled.

Background. In semantic subtyping, types are interpreted as subsets of a model of values, and the subtyping relation S ≤ T is defined as set-theoretic inclusion of the interpretations. The type algebra is closed under union, intersection, and negation, and includes type constructors such as the (covariant/contravariant) arrow constructor S → T (for functions), product constructors, the covariant write-channel constructor ch⁺(T), and the contravariant read/write-channel constructor ch⁻(T). Polymorphism is added by allowing type variables α to occur in types.

Two main approaches to polymorphic semantic subtyping have been studied:
  (i) a substitution-based approach, in which a polymorphic subtyping judgement S ≤ T holds when σ(S) ≤ σ(T) for every ground-type substitution σ; and
  (ii) a marking approach, in which type variables are interpreted as markings/tags placed on subparts of values, indicating the parameterized regions; subtyping is then defined directly on these tagged interpretations. The marking approach has so far been developed primarily for covariant constructors (e.g. products, ch⁺), where it yields a tractable and semantically natural polymorphic discipline.

Problem. Develop a practical and semantically well-motivated discipline of parametric polymorphism for semantic subtyping in the presence of contravariant type constructors. Concretely, address the following:

  1. Extend the marking approach to the contravariant arrow constructor →, so as to obtain a polymorphic semantic subtyping relation that supports a fully polymorphic version of a language with higher-order functions (in the spirit of CDuce). The extension should provide a sound and decidable subtyping algorithm and a corresponding type system.

  2. Extend the marking approach to the contravariant channel constructor ch⁻, and analyse how it combines with ch⁺. In particular, determine whether markings can replace or eliminate the side condition of atomicity that is currently required when ch⁻ is mixed with ch⁺.

  3. Identify a fragment of the marking-based polymorphic discipline in which (some of) the substitution-based interpretation of polymorphic subtyping can be recovered, i.e., where S ≤ T in the marking sense coincides with σ(S) ≤ σ(T) for all admissible substitutions σ.

  4. Propose programming-language-level restrictions on the definition of polymorphic functions (e.g., on where type variables may occur, on the shape of polymorphic abstractions, or on type-inference patterns) such that the resulting language is simultaneously: expressive enough for practical programming, simple enough to be implementable with reasonable algorithmic complexity, and compatible with the semantic interpretation of polymorphic types.

Does such a discipline exist, and if so, give an explicit definition together with the corresponding subtyping algorithm and type system?

Let $D=(V,E)$ be a finite digraph. For a vertex $v\in V$, the out-neighborhood of $v$ is $N^+(v)=\{u\in V:(v,u)\in E\}$, and the out-degree of $v$ is $|N^+(v)|$. The maximum out-degree of $D$ is $\Delta^+(D)=\max_{v\in V}|N^+(v)|$. A subset $X\subseteq V$ is called an in-dominating set of $D$ if every vertex $v\in V\setminus X$ has at least one out-neighbor in $X$ (i.e. $N^+(v)\cap X\neq\emptyset$). For $X\subseteq V$, let $D[X]$ denote the sub-digraph induced by $X$, and let $\chi(D[X])$ denote the chromatic number of the underlying undirected graph of $D[X]$ (obtained by ignoring edge directions and removing multiplicities).

Prove or disprove: for every integer $k\ge 2$ and every digraph $D$ with maximum out-degree at most $k$, there exists an in-dominating set $X\subseteq V(D)$ such that
$$\chi(D[X])\le \log_2 k.$$

Background. In the semantic-subtyping methodology, a type system is given an interpretation by mapping each type t to a set ⟦t⟧ in some universe of values, in such a way that the subtyping relation s ≤ t coincides with set inclusion ⟦s⟧ ⊆ ⟦t⟧, and the boolean type constructors (union, intersection, negation) are interpreted by the corresponding set-theoretic operations. A model for a given grammar of types is an assignment ⟦·⟧ that (i) is well-defined on every (possibly infinite/regular) type expression generated by the grammar, (ii) validates the set-theoretic interpretation of the boolean connectives, and (iii) gives the desired meanings to the non-boolean type constructors (e.g., products, arrows, channel types, reference types).

When the grammar is restricted to finitely many occurrences of certain constructors along any infinite branch of a regular type, models are known to exist. However, when one allows fully recursive types built using channel constructors ch(t) (as in the π-calculus) or reference constructors ref(t) (as in languages with mutable state), the natural set-theoretic extension becomes inconsistent and no model in the above sense is known to exist.

Problem.
(a) Determine whether the non-existence of a set-theoretic model for recursive types built with channel and/or reference constructors reflects a methodological limitation of the semantic-subtyping approach (i.e., a different mathematical framework could yield a satisfactory model), or instead reflects an intrinsic semantic obstruction shared by every reasonable interpretation of these constructors.

(b) More generally, give a characterization — in terms of the algebraic, order-theoretic, or categorical properties of the type constructors — of those recursive extensions of a semantically defined type system that admit a model and those that do not. Equivalently, identify necessary and sufficient conditions on a constructor F (such as variance, monotonicity, or contractivity properties) under which the recursive closure of a semantic type system that includes F admits a set-theoretic model compatible with the boolean connectives.

Define a class $\mathcal{C}$ of finite simple undirected graphs by the following inductive rules:

1. The single-vertex graph $K_1$ belongs to $\mathcal{C}$.
2. The single-edge graph $K_2$ belongs to $\mathcal{C}$.
3. (Gluing rule.) If $G_1, G_2 \in \mathcal{C}$ and $S \subseteq V(G_1)$, $T \subseteq V(G_2)$ are subsets of vertices with $|S| = |T| \le 2$ such that, when $|S| = 2$, both pairs of vertices (the two vertices of $S$ in $G_1$ and the two vertices of $T$ in $G_2$) are non-adjacent in their respective graphs, then the graph obtained by taking the disjoint union of $G_1$ and $G_2$ and identifying the vertices of $S$ with the vertices of $T$ (via some bijection $S \to T$), without adding any new edges, also belongs to $\mathcal{C}$.

Question: Does there exist a graph $G \in \mathcal{C}$ whose chromatic number $\chi(G)$ equals $4$? Either exhibit such a graph explicitly, or prove that every graph in $\mathcal{C}$ satisfies $\chi(G) \le 3$.

- $G$ is triangle-free if it contains no three mutually adjacent vertices (no subgraph isomorphic to $K_3$).

- $G$ is 3-colorable if there exists a map $c: V(G) \to \{1,2,3\}$ such that $c(u) \ne c(v)$ whenever $uv \in E(G)$.

Decide whether the following statement is true: every finite simple graph $G$ that is triangle-free and contains no 3-connected subgraph is 3-colorable.

Consider type systems based on semantic subtyping, in which types are built from basic types using unions, intersections, negations, products, and arrows, and are interpreted set-theoretically as subsets of a universe of values, with the subtyping relation defined by set-theoretic inclusion of denotations. In such systems, in order to type values composed of functional components, one typically needs to deduce negated arrow types for them: for instance, if f has type Int→Int, the system should be able to derive ¬(Bool→Bool) for f, even though Int→Int is not a subtype of ¬(Bool→Bool), so subsumption alone does not suffice. Two known approaches to handle this are: (i) requiring the model to have "enough points" so that negated arrow types can be deduced explicitly via dedicated typing rules, and (ii) representing the minimum type of a λ-abstraction as a (possibly infinite) intersection of its declared arrow type with all negated arrow types compatible with it, leading to schematic or infinitary type representations. These devices appear, for example, in the system CDuce and in local variants of a calculus π of set-theoretic types, where the full (non-local) version of π avoids the issue.

Question: Is the use of "enough points" together with explicit deduction rules for negated types — or, alternatively, the use of infinitary/schematic type representations — an unavoidable feature of any semantic-subtyping type system that includes negation types and full higher-order functions? Equivalently, can one design a semantic-subtyping type system with union, intersection, negation, and arrow types that:
(a) enjoys the minimum typing property (every typeable expression has a least type, in particular for λ-abstractions),
(b) has a purely set-theoretic model interpretation (without "enough points" hypotheses or schematic infinite intersections), and
(c) correctly deduces all required negated arrow types for functional values?

If yes, exhibit such a system; if no, prove that any such type system must rely on either an "enough points" assumption with explicit negation typing rules or on infinitary/schematic representations of types.

Background. The semantic subtyping methodology defines a subtyping relation t ≤ s between types by interpreting types as sets ⟦t⟧ in a suitable model and stipulating that t ≤ s holds iff ⟦t⟧ ⊆ ⟦s⟧ (equivalently, ⟦t ∧ ¬s⟧ = ∅). Types are typically closed under Boolean connectives, and the model is built so that the resulting subtyping relation is decidable and matches the intended typing of values. This approach has been successfully developed for functional languages with arrows, products, and recursive types, and for the π-calculus with channel types built from read/write capabilities and Boolean combinations.

Problem. Extend the semantic-subtyping methodology to dependent type systems in a way that produces a genuinely semantic (set-theoretic, model-based) characterization of the subtyping relation, rather than one defined by syntactic normalization or rewriting rules. Concretely:

(a) Construct a set-theoretic (or otherwise extensional) interpretation ⟦·⟧ of the types of a π-calculus equipped with channel-dependent types — i.e. channel types whose carried-message type may depend on values transmitted on the channel — together with Boolean type connectives, such that the induced relation t ≤ s ⇔ ⟦t⟧ ⊆ ⟦s⟧ is decidable, sound, and complete with respect to a natural operational semantics of the calculus.

(b) Carry out the analogous program for the first-order dependent type theory λΠ (the logical framework LF), namely the simply typed λ-calculus extended with dependent product types Πx:A. B(x). Provide a model in which types denote sets of well-typed terms (or values), closed under suitable Boolean operations, and define subtyping by set inclusion in the model, obtaining a characterization that is independent of the syntactic conversion/normalization rules of λΠ.

Determine whether such semantic characterizations exist and, if so, exhibit them; otherwise identify precise obstructions that prevent the semantic-subtyping methodology from being lifted to these dependent settings.

Let $\Sigma_g$ denote a closed oriented surface of genus $g$, and let $\Sigma_{g,n}$ denote a compact oriented surface of genus $g$ with $n$ boundary components. Write $\mathrm{Map}_g$ for the mapping class group of $\Sigma_g$ (orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms modulo isotopy) and $\mathrm{Map}_{g,n}$ for the mapping class group of $\Sigma_{g,n}$ (with diffeomorphisms required to fix the boundary pointwise, modulo isotopies that fix the boundary pointwise). For a simple closed curve $c$ in the surface, let $\tau_c \in \mathrm{Map}$ denote the right-handed (positive) Dehn twist about $c$, and for a boundary component, let $\delta$ denote the Dehn twist about a curve parallel to that boundary.

A **mapping class group factorization** is an ordered tuple $(\tau_{c_1}, \tau_{c_2}, \ldots, \tau_{c_k})$ of positive Dehn twists whose product (in the given order) equals a prescribed element — typically the identity in $\mathrm{Map}_g$ or the boundary multitwist $\delta$ in $\mathrm{Map}_{g,n}$.

Two factorizations $(t_1, \ldots, t_k)$ and $(t_1', \ldots, t_k')$ are declared equivalent if one can be transformed into the other by a finite sequence of the following moves:

1. **Hurwitz moves** at position $i$ (for $1 \le i \le k-1$):
$$(t_1,\ldots, t_i, t_{i+1}, \ldots, t_k) \;\longleftrightarrow\; (t_1, \ldots, t_i t_{i+1} t_i^{-1},\; t_i, \ldots, t_k),$$
together with the inverse move $(t_1,\ldots, t_i, t_{i+1}, \ldots) \leftrightarrow (t_1,\ldots, t_{i+1}, t_{i+1}^{-1} t_i t_{i+1}, \ldots)$.

2. **Global conjugation** by an element $\varphi$ of the mapping class group:
$$(t_1, \ldots, t_k) \;\longleftrightarrow\; (\varphi t_1 \varphi^{-1}, \ldots, \varphi t_k \varphi^{-1}).$$

**Question.** Is the Hurwitz problem for mapping class group factorizations decidable? That is, does there exist an algorithm which, given two factorizations of the same element of $\mathrm{Map}_g$ (or of $\delta \in \mathrm{Map}_{g,n}$) by positive Dehn twists, determines in finite time whether they are equivalent under Hurwitz moves and global conjugation? Moreover, are there useful invariants or criteria that can be used in practice to certify either equivalence or inequivalence of two such factorizations?

A web search reveals only partial progress: criteria for Hurwitz equivalence in restricted settings (e.g. quasipositive factorizations of 3-braids, reflection factorizations in specific complex reflection groups, semi-frame factorizations) and decidability results for related but distinct problems such as Thurston equivalence of branched coverings via centralizers in the mapping class group. Let $\gamma^3_2$ denote the tautological (canonical) $2$-plane bundle over the Grassmannian $G_2(\mathbb{R}^3)\cong\mathbb{RP}^2$, whose fiber over a point $L\in G_2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ is the $2$-dimensional linear subspace $L\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ itself.

A continuous field of convex figures in $\gamma^3_2$ is a continuous assignment $L\mapsto K(L)$ that to every fiber $L$ associates a planar convex body $K(L)\subset L$ (continuity is with respect to the Hausdorff metric, after identifying nearby fibers via the bundle structure).

For a planar convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^2$, let $\delta_L(K)$ denote its lattice packing density, i.e. the supremum, over all lattices $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ such that the translates $\{K+\lambda:\lambda\in\Lambda\}$ have pairwise disjoint interiors, of the upper density of $\bigcup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}(K+\lambda)$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$.

Define
$$\delta^* \;=\; \inf_{\{K(L)\}}\;\sup_{L\in G_2(\mathbb{R}^3)}\delta_L\bigl(K(L)\bigr),$$
where the infimum is taken over all continuous fields of convex figures in $\gamma^3_2$.

It is known that $\delta^*\geq 3/4$ and that this lower bound is not sharp. Determine the exact value of $\delta^*$.

Let $f: X \to S^2$ be a Lefschetz fibration on a smooth 4-manifold $X$, with critical values $\{p_1, \dots, p_n\} \subset S^2$ and regular fiber $\Sigma$ a closed oriented surface. Fix a base point $* \in S^2 \setminus \{p_1, \dots, p_n\}$ and a system of vanishing arcs, yielding a monodromy factorization $\tau_{c_1} \tau_{c_2} \cdots \tau_{c_n}$ in the mapping class group $\mathrm{Mod}(\Sigma)$, where each $c_i \subset \Sigma$ is the vanishing cycle associated with the critical value $p_i$ and $\tau_{c_i}$ is the right-handed Dehn twist along $c_i$.

A matching path for $f$ is an embedded arc $\eta \subset S^2 \setminus \{p_1, \dots, p_n\}$ whose two endpoints lie at distinct critical values $p_i, p_j$, with the property that parallel transport along $\eta$ (using a chosen symplectic/horizontal connection on the fibration over the complement of the critical values) carries the vanishing cycle at one endpoint to a simple closed curve in the fiber that is freely homotopic (equivalently, isotopic) to the vanishing cycle at the other endpoint.

Problem: Given the Lefschetz fibration $f$ presented through its monodromy factorization by positive Dehn twists, give an algorithm — or a combinatorial/topological criterion expressed purely in terms of the factorization — that enumerates all matching paths of $f$ up to isotopy in $S^2 \setminus \{p_1, \dots, p_n\}$.

Setup. Let $f\colon X\to S^2$ be a Lefschetz fibration with regular fiber a closed oriented surface $\Sigma_g$ of genus $g$, with $n$ critical values $p_1,\dots,p_n\in S^2$ and a chosen base point $p_0$. Choosing a Hurwitz system of arcs from $p_0$ to the $p_i$, the monodromy of $f$ is encoded as an ordered tuple $(\tau_1,\dots,\tau_n)$ of right-handed Dehn twists in the mapping class group $\mathrm{Mod}(\Sigma_g)$ whose product equals the monodromy of $f$ along $\partial D^2$. Two such factorizations describe the same Lefschetz fibration if and only if they are related by:
(i) Hurwitz moves: $(\dots,\tau_i,\tau_{i+1},\dots)\leftrightarrow(\dots,\tau_i\tau_{i+1}\tau_i^{-1},\tau_i,\dots)$ or its inverse; and
(ii) global simultaneous conjugation: $(\tau_1,\dots,\tau_n)\mapsto(\phi\tau_1\phi^{-1},\dots,\phi\tau_n\phi^{-1})$ for some $\phi\in\mathrm{Mod}(\Sigma_g)$.

The braid group $B_n$ on $n$ strands acts on ordered $n$-tuples by Hurwitz moves. Define the automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(f)$ of the Lefschetz fibration to be the subgroup of $B_n$ consisting of those braids $\beta$ whose Hurwitz action on $(\tau_1,\dots,\tau_n)$ produces a tuple that is globally conjugate (in $\mathrm{Mod}(\Sigma_g)$) to $(\tau_1,\dots,\tau_n)$.

A matching path for $f$ is an embedded arc $\gamma\subset S^2$ joining two critical values $p_i,p_j$ (and avoiding the others) such that the vanishing cycles associated to $p_i$ and $p_j$ along $\gamma$ are isotopic in the fiber; such an arc determines a Lagrangian sphere in $X$. The group $\mathrm{Aut}(f)$ acts on the set of matching paths up to isotopy.

Question. Does there exist a finite generating set $\{\beta_1,\dots,\beta_k\}$ of $\mathrm{Aut}(f)$ together with a finite collection of matching paths $\{\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_m\}$ such that every matching path of $f$ is in the orbit of some $\gamma_j$ under the subgroup of $\mathrm{Aut}(f)$ generated by $\beta_1,\dots,\beta_k$?

representations.normalized:
An initial data set for the Einstein vacuum equations is a triple $(M,g,K)$ where $M$ is a smooth $3$-manifold, $g$ is a smooth Riemannian metric on $M$, and $K$ is a smooth symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor field on $M$ satisfying the vacuum constraint equations
$$R_g + (\mathrm{tr}_g K)^2 - |K|_g^2 = 0, \qquad \mathrm{div}_g K - d(\mathrm{tr}_g K) = 0,$$
where $R_g$ is the scalar curvature of $g$. The data $(M,g,K)$ is called asymptotically flat if there is a compact set $C \subset M$ and a diffeomorphism from $M\setminus C$ to $\mathbb{R}^3 \setminus \overline{B}$ (for some closed ball $\overline{B}$) in which
$$g_{ij} = \delta_{ij} + O(|x|^{-1}), \qquad K_{ij} = O(|x|^{-2}),$$
together with appropriate decay of derivatives, so that the ADM mass and momentum are well defined.

A smooth closed $2$-surface $\Sigma \subset M$ is called an apparent horizon (a marginally outer trapped surface, MOTS) if its outward null expansion vanishes:
$$\theta_+ := H_\Sigma + \mathrm{tr}_\Sigma K = 0,$$
where $H_\Sigma$ denotes the mean curvature of $\Sigma$ with respect to its outward unit normal in $(M,g)$ and $\mathrm{tr}_\Sigma K$ is the trace of $K$ restricted to $\Sigma$.

Question. Does there exist an asymptotically flat vacuum initial data set $(M,g,K)$ such that $M$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3$ and such that $M$ contains an apparent horizon?

Let $\Sigma_{g,n}$ denote a compact oriented surface of genus $g$ with $n$ boundary components, and let $\mathrm{Map}_{g,n}$ denote its mapping class group (orientation-preserving self-diffeomorphisms fixing the boundary pointwise, modulo isotopy). A positive Dehn twist is the right-handed Dehn twist along a simple closed curve in the interior of $\Sigma_{g,n}$. Let $\mathrm{Map}^+_{g,n}\subseteq\mathrm{Map}_{g,n}$ be the sub-semigroup generated by all positive Dehn twists.

A positive factorization of an element $T\in\mathrm{Map}^+_{g,n}$ is an ordered tuple $(t_1,\dots,t_k)$ of positive Dehn twists with $T=t_1\cdots t_k$. Two such factorizations are called Hurwitz equivalent if one can be obtained from the other by a finite sequence of Hurwitz moves
$$(\dots,t_i,t_{i+1},\dots)\;\longleftrightarrow\;(\dots,t_i t_{i+1} t_i^{-1},\,t_i,\dots),$$
and globally conjugate if one is obtained from the other by simultaneous conjugation of every factor by a fixed element of $\mathrm{Map}_{g,n}$.

Geometrically, equivalence classes of positive factorizations of $T$ (up to Hurwitz moves and global conjugation) correspond to isomorphism classes of Lefschetz fibrations over the disk with regular fiber $\Sigma_{g,n}$ and boundary monodromy $T$, equivalently to Stein fillings of the contact 3-manifold supported by the open book with monodromy $T$.

Problem: Determine the elements $T\in\mathrm{Map}^+_{g,n}$ for which the set of positive factorizations of $T$ admits a classification up to Hurwitz equivalence and global conjugation. In particular, characterize those $T$ for which such a factorization is unique, and those $T$ for which there are only finitely many equivalence classes.

Let $\Sigma_{g,n}$ denote a compact oriented surface of genus $g$ with $n$ boundary components, and let $\mathrm{Map}_{g,n}$ denote its mapping class group (orientation-preserving self-diffeomorphisms fixing the boundary pointwise, modulo isotopy). A positive Dehn twist is the right-handed Dehn twist along a simple closed curve in the interior of $\Sigma_{g,n}$. Let $\mathrm{Map}^+_{g,n}\subseteq\mathrm{Map}_{g,n}$ be the sub-semigroup generated by all positive Dehn twists.

A positive factorization of an element $T\in\mathrm{Map}^+_{g,n}$ is an ordered tuple $(t_1,\dots,t_k)$ of positive Dehn twists with $T=t_1\cdots t_k$. Two such factorizations are called Hurwitz equivalent if one can be obtained from the other by a finite sequence of Hurwitz moves
$$(\dots,t_i,t_{i+1},\dots)\;\longleftrightarrow\;(\dots,t_i t_{i+1} t_i^{-1},\,t_i,\dots),$$
and globally conjugate if one is obtained from the other by simultaneous conjugation of every factor by a fixed element of $\mathrm{Map}_{g,n}$.

Geometrically, equivalence classes of positive factorizations of $T$ (up to Hurwitz moves and global conjugation) correspond to isomorphism classes of Lefschetz fibrations over the disk with regular fiber $\Sigma_{g,n}$ and boundary monodromy $T$, equivalently to Stein fillings of the contact 3-manifold supported by the open book with monodromy $T$.

Problem: Determine the elements $T\in\mathrm{Map}^+_{g,n}$ for which the set of positive factorizations of $T$ admits a classification up to Hurwitz equivalence and global conjugation. In particular, characterize those $T$ for which such a factorization is unique, and those $T$ for which there are only finitely many equivalence classes.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The general classification of positive Dehn twist factorizations up to Hurwitz equivalence and global conjugation remains an active and largely open research problem in symplectic 4-manifold topology. Partial results exist for specific monodromies (e.g., uniqueness or finiteness for boundary-parallel twists in low genus, and Stein-filling finiteness results in particular contact families), but a general characterization of which $T$ admit unique or finitely many factorizations is not known, and even decidability of Hurwitz equivalence is open.

Let $(M, g, K)$ be a smooth initial data set for the vacuum Einstein equations, where $M$ is a 3-manifold, $g$ is a Riemannian metric on $M$, and $K$ is a symmetric (0,2)-tensor on $M$ satisfying the vacuum constraint equations. Suppose $\Sigma \subset M$ is a smooth closed two-sided surface that is an apparent horizon at time $t=0$, that is, $\Sigma$ is (a connected component of the boundary of) the trapped region in $(M,g,K)$, equivalently a marginally outer trapped surface (MOTS) for which the outgoing null expansion $\theta_+ = H_\Sigma + \mathrm{tr}_\Sigma K$ vanishes. Let $(\mathcal{M}, \mathbf{g})$ denote the maximal globally hyperbolic vacuum development of $(M, g, K)$, and consider any smooth foliation of a neighborhood of $M$ in $\mathcal{M}$ by spacelike Cauchy hypersurfaces $M_t$ with $M_0 = M$.

Question: Must there exist, for every such foliation (or for some natural foliation) and for every sufficiently small $t > 0$, an apparent horizon $\Sigma_t \subset M_t$ that depends continuously on $t$ with $\Sigma_0 = \Sigma$? In other words, does an apparent horizon necessarily persist under Einstein evolution of the initial data, or can one exhibit an explicit vacuum initial data set with an apparent horizon whose Einstein evolution contains a Cauchy slice arbitrarily close to the initial slice on which no apparent horizon homologous to $\Sigma$ exists?

Background and setup. A compact symplectic 6-manifold (X,ω) with [ω/2π] integral admits, after blowing up finitely many points, "approximately holomorphic" singular maps f : X → CP^2 whose critical locus is a symplectic curve D ⊂ CP^2 with only nodes and cusps as singularities, and whose fibers are symplectic surfaces (possibly with degenerations along D). The monodromy of the smooth fibration X \ f^{-1}(D) → CP^2 \ D yields a representation

   ρ : π_1(CP^2 \ D) ⟶ Map(Σ_g),

where Map(Σ_g) is the mapping class group of a closed oriented surface of genus g equal to the generic fiber genus, and ρ satisfies prescribed local monodromy relations near each node and cusp of D and around the line at infinity. Two such pairs (D, ρ) are considered equivalent if they are related by Hurwitz moves and global conjugation in Map(Σ_g) together with isotopy of D through nodal–cuspidal symplectic curves.

Problem. Develop a theory, parallel to the use of positive factorizations in mapping class groups for symplectic 4-manifolds via Lefschetz pencils, that classifies compact symplectic 6-manifolds (up to symplectic deformation and blow-up) by equivalence classes of pairs (D, ρ : π_1(CP^2 \ D) → Map(Σ_g)) of the type above. Specifically:

(i) Show that every compact integral symplectic 6-manifold gives rise, after finitely many blow-ups, to such a pair (D, ρ), uniquely determined up to the equivalence above for sufficiently large degree of f.

(ii) Identify a complete set of algebraic conditions (local monodromy types at nodes, cusps, tangencies, and at infinity, together with the global relation forced by π_1(CP^2 \ D)) characterizing those representations ρ that arise from compact symplectic 6-manifolds.

(iii) Use this correspondence to extract effective topological or symplectic invariants of compact symplectic 6-manifolds (analogous to those obtained from Lefschetz fibration factorizations in dimension 4).

The question is part of a program initiated by Auroux, Donaldson, and Katzarkov to extend, to dimension 6, the dictionary between symplectic 4-manifolds and mapping class group factorizations. Available sources (Auroux's surveys on open questions about symplectic manifolds and singular plane curves, and the work on singular Lefschetz pencils) discuss this as a proposed direction rather than an established theory; no published classification or general structural theorem of the kind requested has been found. The problem appears to remain open.

Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth, complete, asymptotically flat Riemannian $3$-manifold with nonnegative scalar curvature, and let $m_{\mathrm{ADM}}(M,g)$ denote its ADM mass. Suppose $\Sigma \subset M$ is a stable minimal $2$-sphere. Prove the Penrose inequality
$$\operatorname{area}(\Sigma) \;\le\; 16\pi\, m_{\mathrm{ADM}}(M,g)^2.$$

Furthermore, formulate and prove an appropriate generalization to initial data sets that are not time-symmetric. Specifically, let $(M,g,k)$ be an asymptotically flat initial data set for the Einstein equations satisfying the dominant energy condition, where $g$ is a Riemannian metric on the $3$-manifold $M$ and $k$ is a symmetric $2$-tensor representing the second fundamental form of $M$ in the ambient spacetime, with ADM energy-momentum $(E,P)$ and ADM mass $m_{\mathrm{ADM}} = \sqrt{E^2 - |P|^2}$. Let $\Sigma \subset M$ be an outermost marginally outer trapped surface (apparent horizon). Show that
$$\operatorname{area}(\Sigma) \;\le\; 16\pi\, m_{\mathrm{ADM}}^2,$$
with equality characterizing initial data in the Schwarzschild spacetime.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The Riemannian (time-symmetric) Penrose inequality was proved by Huisken–Ilmanen (single horizon, 2001) and by Bray (general, 2001). The full spacetime Penrose inequality for non-time-symmetric initial data sets remains open in general; recent work (e.g., 2025) has established a spacetime Penrose inequality only with a suboptimal constant, and proofs exist under symmetry assumptions such as spherical symmetry. The sharp spacetime version is therefore still an open problem.

Definitions. A linearly ordered topological space (LOTS) is a triple $(X,\tau,<)$ where $<$ is a linear order on $X$ and $\tau$ is the open-interval topology induced by $<$. A generalized ordered space (GO-space) is a triple $(X,\sigma,<)$ where $<$ is a linear order on $X$ and $\sigma$ is a Hausdorff topology on $X$ that has a base consisting of order-convex sets; equivalently, a GO-space is a topological subspace of some LOTS. A topological space is perfect if every closed subset is a $G_\delta$. The local density of a topological space $X$ is the smallest cardinal $\kappa$ such that every point of $X$ has a neighborhood of density $\le\kappa$.

Question. Fix a cardinal $\kappa$ with $\kappa>\omega_1$. Is it consistent with ZFC that for every perfect GO-space $X$ of local density $\le\kappa$ there exists a perfect LOTS $Y$ and a topological embedding $h:X\to Y$? Here $h$ is not required to be order-preserving, and $h[X]$ is not required to be open, closed, or dense in $Y$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The GO-embedding problem (whether every perfect GO-space embeds into a perfect LOTS) is a long-standing question in set-theoretic topology. The dense-embedding version was answered negatively by Bennett–Lutzer (1995), but the general embedding version (without requiring density, openness, closedness, or monotonicity) for local density $\le\kappa>\omega_1$ remains open, with no announced consistency result located in current sources.

Let $(M, g, K)$ be an initial data set for the vacuum Einstein equations, where $M$ is a smooth $3$-manifold, $g$ a Riemannian metric on $M$, and $K$ a symmetric $2$-tensor satisfying the Einstein constraint equations
$$R(g) - |K|_g^2 + (\mathrm{tr}_g K)^2 = 0, \qquad \mathrm{div}_g K - d(\mathrm{tr}_g K) = 0.$$
Suppose $M$ is the interior of a compact manifold-with-boundary $\overline{M}$ whose boundary $\partial M$ represents future null infinity, and that $(M,g)$ is asymptotically hyperbolic in the sense that there exists a defining function $\rho$ for $\partial M$ and a smooth metric $\bar g = \rho^2 g$ on $\overline{M}$ with $|d\rho|_{\bar g} = 1$ on $\partial M$. Suppose further that $\mathrm{tr}_g K$ is constant on $M$ (a CMC slice), modeling a hyperboloidal hypersurface meeting future null infinity transversally.

In the conformal method one prescribes a conformal background $(\tilde g, \sigma, \tau)$ — where $\tilde g$ is a Riemannian metric on $M$, $\sigma$ a transverse-traceless symmetric $2$-tensor with respect to $\tilde g$, and $\tau$ the prescribed mean curvature — and seeks a positive conformal factor $\phi$ and a vector field $W$ such that
$$g = \phi^4 \tilde g, \qquad K = \phi^{-2}(\sigma + \mathcal{L}_{\tilde g} W) + \tfrac{\tau}{3}\, g,$$
solve the constraint equations, where $\mathcal{L}_{\tilde g}$ denotes the conformal Killing operator of $\tilde g$. This reduces the constraints to the coupled Lichnerowicz–vector equations for $(\phi, W)$ on $M$.

Problem. Determine the precise asymptotic conditions on the conformal data $(\tilde g, \sigma, \tau)$ at $\partial M$ — including the rates of decay or polyhomogeneous expansion of $\tilde g - \bar g$, $\sigma$, and $\tau - \tau_\infty$ near $\rho = 0$, as well as compatibility/boundary conditions at $\partial M$ — under which the conformal method produces a solution $(\phi, W)$ giving a vacuum hyperboloidal initial data set $(M, g, K)$ that is asymptotically hyperbolic with the prescribed asymptotic geometry, with $\mathrm{tr}_g K$ constant, and such that $\partial M$ corresponds to future null infinity of the resulting maximal Cauchy development.

Substantial partial results exist: Andersson–Chruściel–Friedrich and subsequent work established existence of CMC hyperboloidal solutions of the conformal constraints under suitable asymptotic conditions, while showing that generic solutions admit only polyhomogeneous (logarithmic) expansions at conformal infinity rather than smooth ones. Recent work (e.g. on parabolic-hyperbolic formulations and on hyperboloidal data without logarithmic singularities, 2024–2025) further characterizes subclasses of asymptotic data yielding smooth or Bondi-regular development. A complete characterization of the optimal asymptotic conditions for the conformal method in this setting is not yet established, so the problem is partially solved.

A linearly ordered topological space (LOTS) is a Hausdorff space whose topology is generated by the open intervals of some linear ordering on the underlying set. A generalized ordered space (GO-space) is a triple $(X,\tau,<)$ where $<$ is a linear ordering of $X$ and $\tau$ is a Hausdorff topology on $X$ that has a base consisting of $<$-convex sets and refines the open-interval topology of $<$; equivalently, GO-spaces are exactly the subspaces of LOTS.

Say that a topological space $X$ is divisible by open sets if for every subset $A \subseteq X$ there exists a countable family $\mathcal{C}_A$ of open subsets of $X$ such that for every $x \in A$ and every $y \in X \setminus A$ there is some $C \in \mathcal{C}_A$ with $x \in C$ and $y \notin C$.

Problem. Give an internal characterization of those GO-spaces $X$ which are divisible by open sets in the sense above.

Consider an asymptotically hyperboloidal initial data set $(M,g,K)$ for the vacuum Einstein equations, where $M$ is a 3-manifold with a conformal boundary at infinity $\mathscr{I}$, $g$ is a Riemannian metric on $M$, and $K$ is a symmetric 2-tensor representing the second fundamental form. Suppose $M$ admits a conformal compactification: there exists a defining function $\Omega$ for $\mathscr{I}$ such that the rescaled metric $\tilde g=\Omega^{2}g$ extends to the boundary with some prescribed regularity (e.g. $C^{k}$ up to the boundary, $C^{\infty}$, or polyhomogeneous with controlled logarithmic terms).

The Trautman–Bondi mass $m_{\mathrm{TB}}$ of such a data set is defined as a boundary integral at $\mathscr{I}$ involving the conformally rescaled geometry.

Problem: Classify the possible smoothness/regularity behaviors of hyperboloidal initial data at conformal infinity $\mathscr{I}$ (e.g. finite differentiability up to the boundary, full smoothness, polyhomogeneous expansions, possibly with logarithmic terms), and determine the weakest such regularity condition at $\mathscr{I}$ under which a proof of the positivity of the Trautman–Bondi mass, namely $m_{\mathrm{TB}}\ge 0$ with equality only for Minkowski space, can be carried out for data satisfying the vacuum (or dominant-energy) constraint equations.

Definitions. A linearly ordered topological space (LOTS) is a triple (L,<,τ) where < is a linear order on L and τ is the topology generated by the open intervals of (L,<). A generalized ordered space (GO-space) is a triple (L,<,τ) where < is a linear order on L and τ is a Hausdorff topology on L that has a base consisting of order-convex sets (equivalently, a subspace of some LOTS).

A topological space X is said to be cleavable over a class 𝒞 of topological spaces if for every subset A ⊆ X there exists a space Y ∈ 𝒞 and a continuous map f : X → Y such that f^{-1}(f(A)) = A; in this situation one says that A can be separated from its complement by a continuous map into a member of 𝒞. Given a single space L, we say X is cleavable over L if X is cleavable over the class {L}.

Question. (a) Suppose X is a compact Hausdorff space and there exists a linearly ordered topological space (or, more generally, a generalized ordered space) L such that X is cleavable over L. Must X be homeomorphic to a linearly ordered topological space?

(b) Does the answer to (a) become affirmative under the additional assumption that X is zero-dimensional?

Let $I \subset \mathbb{R}$ be a compact interval and let $p$ be a positive integer. Given continuous maps $f_0, f_1, \dots, f_{p-1}: I \to I$, consider the $p$-periodic non-autonomous discrete dynamical system
$$x_{n+1} = f_{n \bmod p}(x_n), \qquad n \ge 0.$$
A point $x \in I$ is called periodic of least period $k$ for this system if $k$ is the smallest positive integer with the property that
$$f_{(k-1) \bmod p} \circ f_{(k-2) \bmod p} \circ \cdots \circ f_{1 \bmod p} \circ f_{0 \bmod p}(x) = x$$
and the corresponding orbit $(x_n)_{n \ge 0}$ has minimal period $k$ as a sequence. Define
$$\mathrm{Per}([f_0, \dots, f_{p-1}]) := \{k \in \mathbb{N} : \text{the system has a periodic orbit of least period } k\}.$$

For $p = 1$, Sharkovsky's theorem completely characterizes the possible sets $\mathrm{Per}(f_0)$: they are exactly the tails of the Sharkovsky order on $\mathbb{N}$ (together with the empty set and certain $2^\infty$-related cases). For $p = 2$, an analogous exact characterization of the possible sets $\mathrm{Per}([f_0, f_1])$ is known.

Problem: For an arbitrary positive integer $p$, give a complete characterization of the family of subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ that arise as $\mathrm{Per}([f_0, \dots, f_{p-1}])$ as $(f_0, \dots, f_{p-1})$ ranges over all $p$-tuples of continuous self-maps of $I$.

Consider a smooth four-dimensional Lorentzian spacetime $(M,g)$ that is static and asymptotically flat: there exists a smooth, complete, hypersurface-orthogonal timelike Killing vector field $\xi$ on $M$, and outside a compact set the spatial slice (the quotient by the $\xi$-flow) is diffeomorphic to the complement of a closed ball in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with the metric and lapse function approaching the standard flat values at the appropriate decay rates. Suppose the Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g) - \tfrac{1}{2} R\, g = 8\pi T$ hold on $M$ for a stress-energy tensor $T$ supported in a compact "matter region" $\Omega \subset M$.

(a) Identify general structural conditions on the stress-energy tensor $T$ (for example, energy conditions, isotropy, equation-of-state hypotheses) which force the metric $g$ to be spherically symmetric, i.e. to admit an effective $SO(3)$ action by isometries whose orbits are the level sets of a radial function.

(b) (Static star conjecture.) In the special case where $T$ is the stress-energy tensor of a perfect fluid,
$$T_{\alpha\beta} = (\rho + p)\, u_\alpha u_\beta + p\, g_{\alpha\beta},$$
with $u$ the unit timelike four-velocity aligned with $\xi/\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}$ inside $\Omega$, energy density $\rho \geq 0$, pressure $p \geq 0$ vanishing on $\partial\Omega$, and a barotropic equation of state $p = p(\rho)$ satisfying physically reasonable monotonicity conditions, prove that $(M,g)$ must be spherically symmetric, with $\Omega$ a metric ball.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The static star (fluid ball) conjecture remains open in full generality. Partial results are known: spherical symmetry has been established under additional hypotheses such as the existence of a spherically symmetric comparison model with the same equation of state and surface potential (Beig–Simon, Lindblom–Masood-ul-Alam), and recent work (Coutinho–Leandro and others) has further refined these conditions, but a fully general rigorous proof for arbitrary physically reasonable equations of state has not been obtained.

Definitions. A linearly ordered topological space (LOTS) is a linearly ordered set endowed with the open-interval topology. A generalized ordered space (GO-space) is a Hausdorff space (X,τ,<) where < is a linear order on X and τ is a topology on X having a base of order-convex sets and refining the open-interval topology of <. A topological space X is perfect if every closed subset of X is a G_δ. A space is hereditarily P if every subspace has property P. A Souslin line is a LOTS that has the countable chain condition (every family of pairwise disjoint nonempty open sets is countable) but is not separable.

A topological space X is monotonically Lindelöf if to every open cover U of X one can assign a countable open refinement r(U) of U such that whenever U and V are open covers of X with U refining V, the assignment satisfies that r(U) refines r(V). A space is hereditarily monotonically Lindelöf if every subspace (with the subspace topology) is monotonically Lindelöf.

Questions. Decide each of the following.
(a) Is every perfect monotonically Lindelöf GO-space separable?
(b) Is every hereditarily monotonically Lindelöf GO-space separable?
(c) If a Souslin line exists, must there exist a compact Souslin line that is hereditarily monotonically Lindelöf?
(d) If a Souslin line exists, must there exist a Souslin line that is not monotonically Lindelöf?

representations.normalized:
Let $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be a compact interval and let $f_0, f_1, \dots, f_{p-1} : I \to I$ be continuous maps. Consider the non-autonomous periodic difference equation
$$x_{n+1} = f_{n \bmod p}(x_n), \qquad n = 0, 1, 2, \dots,$$
and write $F = [f_0, \dots, f_{p-1}]$ for this $p$-periodic system. A point $x \in I$ is called a periodic point of $F$ of period $m$ if $m$ is the least positive integer such that $(f_{m-1} \circ \cdots \circ f_1 \circ f_0)(x) = x$ when iterating the system starting at index $0$, and more generally $m$ is a period of $F$ if some orbit of the system has minimal period $m$. Let $\mathrm{Per}(F)$ denote the set of all such minimal periods.

For $q \in \mathbb{N}$, define the cluster
$$A_{p,q} \;=\; \{\, n \in \mathbb{N} : \mathrm{lcm}(n, p) = q \cdot p \,\} \;=\; \{\, n \in \mathbb{N} : q = n / \gcd(n, p) \,\}.$$

Question: Suppose there exists $m \in \mathrm{Per}(F)$ with $m \in A_{p,q}$, where $q > 1$ is an odd integer. Must it follow that $pq \in \mathrm{Per}(F)$? Either prove that $pq \in \mathrm{Per}(F)$ in this situation for every such $p$-periodic system of continuous interval maps, or exhibit a $p$-periodic system $F$ and odd $q > 1$ for which $m \in A_{p,q} \cap \mathrm{Per}(F)$ but $pq \notin \mathrm{Per}(F)$.

Let $S^1$ denote the unit circle. Given two continuous maps $f_0, f_1 : S^1 \to S^1$, consider the non-autonomous (2-periodic) discrete dynamical system
$$x_{n+1} = f_{n \bmod 2}(x_n), \qquad n = 0, 1, 2, \dots$$

Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth, $4$-dimensional, globally hyperbolic, asymptotically flat solution of the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$. Recall that a Cauchy surface is a smooth spacelike hypersurface $\Sigma \subset M$ such that every inextendible causal curve in $M$ meets $\Sigma$ exactly once, and the induced Cauchy data on $\Sigma$ consists of the pair $(h,K)$ where $h$ is the Riemannian metric induced on $\Sigma$ and $K$ is the second fundamental form of $\Sigma$ in $(M,g)$. Two Cauchy data sets $(\Sigma_1,h_1,K_1)$ and $(\Sigma_2,h_2,K_2)$ are called isometric if there exists a diffeomorphism $\phi:\Sigma_1\to\Sigma_2$ with $\phi^*h_2=h_1$ and $\phi^*K_2=K_1$. The spacetime $(M,g)$ is said to be stationary if it admits a smooth Killing vector field that is timelike in the asymptotic region.

Question: Suppose $(M,g)$ admits two disjoint Cauchy surfaces $\Sigma_1$ and $\Sigma_2$ whose induced vacuum Cauchy data $(\Sigma_1,h_1,K_1)$ and $(\Sigma_2,h_2,K_2)$ are isometric. Must $(M,g)$ be stationary, i.e., must it admit a Killing vector field that is timelike at infinity?

representations.normalization_method: unicode-preserving newline and trailing-whitespace normalization v1
representations.normalized:
Background and definitions. A linearly ordered topological space (LOTS) is a set X equipped with a linear order < and the topology generated by the open intervals of <. The lexicographic product [0,1] × {0,1} is the LOTS whose underlying set is [0,1] × {0,1} ordered by (x,i) < (y,j) iff x < y, or x = y and i < j.

For a topological space X, let O(X) denote the collection of open covers of X, and refine the covers in the natural sense (V refines U if every member of V is contained in some member of U).

(i) X is monotonically compact if there is an operator r assigning to each U ∈ O(X) a finite open refinement r(U) of U such that whenever V refines U, r(V) refines r(U).

(ii) X is monotonically Lindelöf if there is an operator r assigning to each U ∈ O(X) a countable open refinement r(U) of U such that whenever V refines U, r(V) refines r(U).

A space is first-countable if every point has a countable neighborhood base.

Resolve the following three questions:

(a) Is the lexicographic product LOTS [0,1] × {0,1} monotonically compact?

(b) If X is a first-countable compact LOTS, must X be monotonically Lindelöf?

(c) If X is a first-countable monotonically compact LOTS, must X be metrizable?

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

All three questions appear to have been resolved. Gruenhage proved that every monotonically compact Hausdorff space is metrizable; this gives (c) and also implies the negative answer to (a), since the lexicographic LOTS [0,1] × {0,1} is a compact Hausdorff non-metrizable (double-arrow type) space, hence not monotonically compact. For (b), it is known that every first-countable Lindelöf GO-space (in particular every first-countable compact LOTS) is monotonically Lindelöf.

Let $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be an interval and let $f_0, f_1, \ldots, f_{p-1}: I \to I$ be continuous maps. Consider the non-autonomous (periodic) difference equation
$$x_{n+1} = f_{n \bmod p}(x_n), \qquad n \ge 0,$$
and call $[f_0, f_1, \ldots, f_{p-1}]$ the associated $p$-periodic system. A point $x \in I$ is said to be a periodic point of least period $m$ of this system if the sequence $\{x_n\}$ starting at $x_0 = x$ satisfies $x_{n+m} = x_n$ for all $n \ge 0$ with $m$ minimal. Define
$$\mathrm{Per}([f_0, \ldots, f_{p-1}]) := \{m \in \mathbb{N} : \text{the system has a periodic point of least period } m\}.$$

Fix an integer $k$ with $1 \le k \le p$, and define the folded maps
$$F_j := f_{(j+1)k - 1} \circ f_{(j+1)k - 2} \circ \cdots \circ f_{jk} \pmod{p}, \qquad j = 0, 1, 2, \ldots$$
Then $[F_0, F_1, \ldots, F_{q-1}]$ is a $q$-periodic system with $q = p/\gcd(p,k)$.

Determine the precise relationship between $\mathrm{Per}([f_0, \ldots, f_{p-1}])$ and $\mathrm{Per}([F_0, F_1, \ldots, F_{q-1}])$.

The folding/unfolding framework for periodic difference equations was introduced by Al-Salman and AlSharawi, and determining the exact relationship between the set of least periods of a periodic system and that of its folded counterpart remains an active research question. Let p and k be positive integers. A p-periodic non-autonomous discrete dynamical system on a set X is a sequence of maps [f_0, f_1, …, f_{p-1}] with f_i : X → X, generating the dynamics x_{n+1} = f_{n mod p}(x_n).

The k-folding of such a system produces a new periodic system [F_0, F_1, …, F_{q-1}], where q = p/gcd(p,k), defined by composing every k-th map along the period: explicitly, for each j,
F_j = f_{j+(k-1) mod p} ∘ f_{j+(k-2) mod p} ∘ ⋯ ∘ f_{j mod p},
so that the iterates of the folded system at step k correspond to iterates of the original system.

Suppose the original p-periodic system [f_0, …, f_{p-1}] is unknown, but one of its folded systems [F_0, F_1, …, F_{q-1}] (with q = p/gcd(p,k)) is known. Consider the q-periodic delay difference equation
x_{n+1} = F_{n mod q}(x_{n-(k-1)}),
whose state at time n depends on x_{n-(k-1)}.

Determine what similarity, if any, must hold between the set of periodic orbits (and more generally the periodic structure) of the unknown unfolded p-periodic system [f_0, …, f_{p-1}] and that of the q-periodic delay system x_{n+1} = F_{n mod q}(x_{n-(k-1)}). In particular, can the periodic behaviors of one system be characterized in terms of the periodic behaviors of the other?

Consider the Einstein–Yang–Mills (EYM) equations on a 4-dimensional Lorentzian spacetime with gauge group SU(2): the coupled system consisting of Einstein's field equations $G_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi T_{\mu\nu}$, where $T_{\mu\nu}$ is the stress-energy tensor of a Yang-Mills connection $A$ with curvature $F$, together with the Yang-Mills equations $D^\mu F_{\mu\nu} = 0$ for $A$ on the resulting spacetime. Seek static, spherically symmetric solutions; with the standard ansatz, the metric takes the form
$$ ds^2 = -A(r) C(r)^2\, dt^2 + A(r)^{-1}\, dr^2 + r^2 (d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\, d\phi^2), $$
and the Yang-Mills connection is given by a single real "magnetic" potential $w(r)$. The reduced equations are
$$ r A' = 1 - A - \frac{(1-w^2)^2}{r^2} - 2 A (w')^2,\qquad r^2 A w'' + \big(r(1-A) - \tfrac{(1-w^2)^2}{r}\big) w' + w(1-w^2) = 0, $$
together with an ODE for $C$. Prove the existence of a globally defined, nonsingular (i.e. $A(r) > 0$ for all $r \ge 0$ with $A(0)=1$ and $w(0)=\pm 1$), asymptotically flat (i.e. $A(r) \to 1$, $C(r) \to 1$, $w(r) \to \pm 1$ as $r \to \infty$ with finite ADM mass) solution $(A, C, w)$ on $[0,\infty)$. Equivalently, establish the existence of static spherically symmetric soliton (particle-like) solutions of the SU(2) Einstein–Yang–Mills equations on $\mathbb{R}^{3+1}$.

Define the merged sequence $[a_n,b_n]$ by concatenating, in order, $k_1$ consecutive terms of $\{a_n\}$ followed by $k_2$ consecutive terms of $\{b_n\}$, and repeating this pattern indefinitely. Explicitly, the merged sequence is
$$a_1,a_2,\dots,a_{k_1},\,b_1,b_2,\dots,b_{k_2},\,a_{k_1+1},a_{k_1+2},\dots,a_{2k_1},\,b_{k_2+1},b_{k_2+2},\dots,b_{2k_2},\,a_{2k_1+1},\dots$$
so that each successive block of $k_1$ terms is drawn (in order, continuing from where the previous $a$-block ended) from $\{a_n\}$, and each successive block of $k_2$ terms is drawn (in order, continuing from where the previous $b$-block ended) from $\{b_n\}$. Determine, in full generality (with no assumption that the ranges of $\{a_n\}$ and $\{b_n\}$ are disjoint), a closed-form expression for the least period of the merged sequence $[a_n,b_n]$ in terms of $q_1$, $q_2$, $k_1$, and $k_2$ (and, when necessary, the values of the sequences themselves).

The question of whether commuting continuous interval maps must share a periodic point appears to remain open. While Boyce and Huneke (1969) showed that commuting continuous interval maps need not share a fixed point, the analogous question for periodic points is still unresolved. Recall the following definitions.

(1) The Sorgenfrey line S is the set of real numbers equipped with the topology generated by the basis of half-open intervals { [a,b) : a < b in R }.

(2) A poset (P,≤) is directed-complete (a dcpo) if every directed subset has a supremum. For x,y ∈ P, write x ≪ y (x is way-below y) if every directed set D with y ≤ sup D contains some d with x ≤ d. A dcpo P is continuous if for every y ∈ P the set { x : x ≪ y } is directed and has supremum y. The Scott topology on P has as open sets those U ⊆ P that are upward-closed and inaccessible by directed suprema. A continuous dcpo P is a Scott domain if it is bounded-complete (every subset bounded above has a supremum). The set max(P) of maximal elements of P, with the relative Scott topology, is the space of "maximal points."

(3) A topological space X is domain-representable if there exists a continuous dcpo P such that X is homeomorphic to max(P) with the relative Scott topology. X is Scott-domain-representable if such a P can be chosen to be a Scott domain.

It is known that S is Scott-domain-representable, and that any G_δ subspace of a domain-representable space is domain-representable.

Let P_S denote the set of irrational numbers, regarded as a subspace of the Sorgenfrey line S (so P_S is a G_δ subspace of S, and is therefore domain-representable).

Question: Is P_S Scott-domain-representable?

representations.normalized:
Let $I=[0,1]$ and let $C(I)$ denote the set of continuous self-maps of $I$. Given an ordered pair $(f_0,f_1)$ with $f_0,f_1\in C(I)$, consider the non-autonomous (2-periodic) discrete dynamical system
$$x_{n+1}=f_{n\bmod 2}(x_n),\qquad n\ge 0.$$
A point $x\in I$ is called periodic of least period $p\ge 1$ for this alternating system if $x$ is fixed by the $p$-fold composition along the alternating sequence and is not fixed by any shorter such composition; here, if $p$ is odd, the $p$-fold composition is understood as $f_{(p-1)\bmod 2}\circ\cdots\circ f_1\circ f_0$ (and analogously for the shifted starting index). Define
$$\mathrm{Per}([f_0,f_1])\subseteq\mathbb{N}$$
to be the set of least periods of periodic orbits of the alternating system.

Assume in addition that $f_0$ and $f_1$ commute, i.e. $f_0\circ f_1=f_1\circ f_0$.

(a) Characterize all subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ that arise as $\mathrm{Per}([f_0,f_1])$ for some commuting pair $f_0,f_1\in C(I)$.

(b) For every set $S\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ known to be realizable as $\mathrm{Per}([g_0,g_1])$ for some (possibly non-commuting) pair $g_0,g_1\in C(I)$, decide whether $S$ is realizable by a commuting pair.

Let $I = [0,1]$ and let $C(I)$ denote the set of continuous self-maps of $I$. For $f \in C(I)$, let $D(f)$ denote the collection of dynamical properties of $f$ (e.g., positive topological entropy, Li–Yorke chaos, existence of periodic points of given periods, transitivity, etc.).

Given a compact subinterval $J \subseteq I$ that is invariant under $f$ (i.e., $f(J) \subseteq J$), let $f_J \in C(I)$ denote the map obtained by restricting $f$ to $J$ and conjugating by the unique increasing affine bijection from $J$ onto $[0,1]$, so $f_J : [0,1] \to [0,1]$ is the natural rescaling of $f|_J$.

Call a dynamical property $P$ an $L$-property if, for every $f \in C(I)$ and every compact invariant subinterval $J \subseteq I$, one has $P \in D(f)$ whenever $P \in D(f_J)$ (that is, the property lifts from rescaled invariant subintervals to the full map).

It is known that for any three $L$-properties $P_1, P_2, P_3$ there exist maps $f_0, f_1 \in C(I)$ such that $P_1 \in D(f_0)$, $P_2 \in D(f_1)$ and $P_3 \in D(f_0 \circ f_1)$.

Question: Prove or disprove that, for any three $L$-properties $P_1, P_2, P_3$, the maps $f_0$ and $f_1$ above can be chosen to additionally commute, i.e., $f_0 \circ f_1 = f_1 \circ f_0$, with $P_1 \in D(f_0)$, $P_2 \in D(f_1)$, and $P_3 \in D(f_0 \circ f_1)$.

Background. The Majumdar–Papapetrou family of solutions to the source-free Einstein–Maxwell equations on a 4-dimensional Lorentzian manifold consists of static metrics of the form
  g = -U(x)^{-2} dt^2 + U(x)^2 (dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2),
together with electromagnetic potential A = U(x)^{-1} dt, where U: R^3 \ {p_1,...,p_N} -> (0,∞) is any positive harmonic function on Euclidean R^3 with isolated singularities at points p_1,...,p_N. After analytic extension, each singularity p_k becomes a degenerate (extremal) Killing horizon, so the solution describes an arbitrary number of extremal Reissner–Nordström black holes held in static equilibrium by the exact balance of their gravitational attraction and electrostatic repulsion. The defining feature is that the linearity of the harmonic equation for U allows arbitrary superposition of single-black-hole solutions.

Problem. Construct a non-Abelian Einstein–Yang–Mills analogue of this Majumdar–Papapetrou superposition. More precisely: for a compact non-Abelian gauge group G (e.g. SU(2)), find static, asymptotically flat solutions of the coupled Einstein–Yang–Mills equations on R x (R^3 \ {p_1,...,p_N}) which (i) describe an equilibrium configuration of N ≥ 2 extremal black-hole-type horizons located at prescribed points p_1,...,p_N in R^3, with (ii) the metric and Yang–Mills connection determined by a superposition principle reducing the problem to a (possibly non-linear) elliptic system on R^3 with isolated singularities, and which (iii) reduces to the Majumdar–Papapetrou solution upon restriction of the gauge field to an Abelian subgroup. Alternatively, prove that no such Einstein–Yang–Mills multi-black-hole equilibrium analogue of Majumdar–Papapetrou exists.

A linearly ordered topological space (LOTS) is a topological space whose topology is generated by the open intervals of some linear order on the underlying set. A topological space $X$ is monotonically normal if there exists an operator $H$ assigning to each ordered pair $(p, U)$, where $p \in U$ and $U$ is open in $X$, an open set $H(p, U)$ with $p \in H(p, U) \subseteq U$, such that whenever $H(p, U) \cap H(q, V) \neq \emptyset$ either $p \in V$ or $q \in U$.

It is known (combining theorems of Mary Ellen Rudin and of Jacek Nikiel) that a topological space $X$ is a continuous image of a compact connected LOTS if and only if $X$ is compact, connected, locally connected, and monotonically normal.

Provide a proof of this characterization that uses the technique of elementary submodels: that is, a proof which works inside (or systematically uses) countable elementary submodels $M \prec H(\theta)$ of a sufficiently large fragment of the set-theoretic universe to construct the required continuous surjection from a compact connected LOTS onto $X$.

Consider the logistic family of maps on the unit interval defined by
   f_a : [0,1] → [0,1],  f_a(x) = a x (1 − x),
for parameter values a ∈ [1, 4]. For a finite word w = (c_1, c_2, …, c_n) ∈ {a, b}^n with a, b ∈ [1,4], let F_w denote the composition
   F_w = f_{c_n} ∘ f_{c_{n−1}} ∘ ⋯ ∘ f_{c_1},
and consider its iterates (which gives a non-autonomous, periodic dynamical system obtained by alternating f_a and f_b in the pattern w).

Say that the pair (a, b) exhibits the dynamic Parrondo paradox if, for every finite word w ∈ ⋃_{n≥1} {a,b}^n that uses both letters at least once, the qualitative dynamical behavior of F_w (in terms of chaos vs. order, e.g., topological entropy or the existence of an attracting periodic orbit) differs from that of the individual maps f_a and f_b — realizing one of the regimes "order + order = chaos" or "chaos + chaos = order".

(1) Give a complete characterization of the set
   P := { (a, b) ∈ [1,4]² : (a,b) exhibits the dynamic Parrondo paradox in the above sense }.
(2) Determine whether P is nonempty.

Existing literature on Parrondo's paradox for the logistic family (Cánovas and coauthors, and subsequent surveys including a 2026 overview on chaos and Parrondo's paradox) identifies many specific parameter pairs realizing "order+order=chaos" or "chaos+chaos=order" and shows the parameter regions with such effects can have fractal structure. Let $M$ be a smooth manifold of dimension $n\ge 3$ (Riemannian or Lorentzian setting may be specified). The vacuum Einstein equations on $M$ are the equation $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$ for the Ricci curvature of a metric $g$. Call a metric $g_e$ on $M$ an "approximate vacuum metric" if $\mathrm{Ric}(g_e)$ is small in some suitable function-space norm $\|\cdot\|_X$ on symmetric $(0,2)$-tensors (for example, a weighted Hölder or Sobolev norm appropriate to the asymptotic geometry of $(M,g_e)$).

Problem. Formulate and prove a perturbation/stability theorem of the following form: there exist constants $\varepsilon>0$ and $C>0$, depending only on $(M,g_e)$ through controlled geometric quantities, such that whenever $g_e$ is an approximate vacuum metric with
$$\|\mathrm{Ric}(g_e)\|_X < \varepsilon,$$
there exists an exact Ricci-flat metric $g$ on $M$ (a solution of $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$) satisfying
$$\|g - g_e\|_X \le C\,\|\mathrm{Ric}(g_e)\|_X.$$

In particular, identify suitable norms $X$, geometric/analytic non-degeneracy hypotheses on the linearization of the Ricci operator (modulo diffeomorphism gauge) at $g_e$, and asymptotic conditions on $(M,g_e)$ under which such a quantitative existence-and-closeness statement holds.

representations.normalized:
Recall the following definitions. A linearly ordered topological space (LOTS) is a triple $(X,\tau,<)$ where $<$ is a linear order on $X$ and $\tau$ is the open-interval topology generated by $<$. A generalized ordered space (GO-space) is a triple $(X,\tau,<)$ where $<$ is a linear order on $X$ and $\tau$ is a Hausdorff topology on $X$ having a base consisting of order-convex sets; equivalently, a GO-space is a subspace of some LOTS. A space $X$ is Lindelöf if every open cover of $X$ has a countable subcover. A space $X$ has a small diagonal if for every uncountable subset $A \subseteq X^2 \setminus \Delta_X$ (where $\Delta_X = \{(x,x):x\in X\}$) there exists an uncountable $A' \subseteq A$ whose closure in $X^2$ is disjoint from $\Delta_X$. A subspace $X$ of a space $Y$ is said to be p-embedded in $Y$ if every continuous pseudometric on $X$ extends to a continuous pseudometric on $Y$.

Question: Suppose $X$ is a Lindelöf GO-space that has a small diagonal and can be p-embedded in some LOTS. Must $X$ be metrizable?

Let $f:[0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ be a continuous function and consider the periodically forced stocking difference equation
$$x_{n+1} = x_n f(x_n) + h_n, \qquad n=0,1,2,\dots,$$
where $\{h_n\}_{n\ge 0}$ is a $p$-periodic sequence of nonnegative stocking quotas (so $h_{n+p}=h_n$ for all $n$ and some fixed integer $p\ge 1$). Assume that, for the given quota sequence $\{h_n\}$, the equation admits a globally attracting $p$-periodic cycle $\{\bar x_0,\bar x_1,\dots,\bar x_{p-1}\}$ in $(0,\infty)$; define the average of this global attractor by
$$x_{\mathrm{av}} \;=\; \frac{1}{p}\sum_{n=0}^{p-1}\bar x_n.$$
Let $\sigma$ be any permutation of $\{0,1,\dots,p-1\}$ and let $\hat h_n = h_{\sigma(n)}$ (extended $p$-periodically); i.e.\ $\{\hat h_n\}$ is a reordering of the same multiset of quotas. Assume the equation with quotas $\{\hat h_n\}$ also has a globally attracting $p$-periodic cycle, and let $\hat x_{\mathrm{av}}$ denote the average of that attractor.

Determine the relationship between $x_{\mathrm{av}}$ and $\hat x_{\mathrm{av}}$: in particular, decide whether $x_{\mathrm{av}} = \hat x_{\mathrm{av}}$ holds for every permutation $\sigma$, or otherwise characterize how reordering the stocking quotas changes the average of the global attractor (e.g.\ identify inequalities such as $x_{\mathrm{av}}\le \hat x_{\mathrm{av}}$ or $\ge$ in terms of properties of $f$ such as monotonicity or concavity).

Let f:[0,∞)→(0,∞) be a continuous function such that the map x↦x f(x) models the per-capita reproduction of a population. Consider the periodically forced harvesting difference equation
    x_{n+1} = x_n f(x_n) − h_n,  n = 0,1,2,…,
where {h_n} is a p-periodic sequence of nonnegative harvesting quotas (i.e., h_{n+p}=h_n for all n) taken from a fixed multiset H = {h^{(1)}, h^{(2)}, …, h^{(p)}} of p nonnegative real numbers. For each permutation σ of {1,…,p}, define the σ-ordered system by setting h_n = h^{(σ(n mod p)+1)}, which produces a p-periodic non-autonomous dynamical system whose composition map admits (under appropriate hypotheses) a globally attracting p-cycle A_σ ⊂ [0,∞) with basin of attraction B_σ ⊂ [0,∞).

Determine which permutation σ of the multiset H is most favorable to the population in the following two senses:
(a) σ maximizes (in the sense of set inclusion or of size) the basin of attraction B_σ of the attracting p-cycle of the harvested system;
(b) σ maximizes the arithmetic mean (1/p)·Σ_{x ∈ A_σ} x of the points of the attracting p-cycle.

Characterize the optimal permutation(s) for each of the two criteria, and compare them.

Consider the Einstein field equations of general relativity, $\mathrm{Ric}(g) - \tfrac{1}{2} R(g)\, g = 8\pi T$, for a Lorentzian metric $g$ on a $4$-manifold, possibly coupled to a matter model (e.g., a perfect fluid of compact spatial support or a vacuum source). Two formal approximation schemes for solutions are commonly used:

(a) The post-Newtonian (PN) expansion: a formal expansion of $g$ and the matter variables in powers of $1/c$ (equivalently, in a small parameter $\varepsilon$ measuring the ratio of typical velocities to the speed of light), assuming slow motion and weak fields.

(b) The post-Minkowskian (PM) expansion: a formal expansion of $g = \eta + \sum_{n\geq 1} G^n h^{(n)}$ around the Minkowski metric $\eta$ in powers of Newton's constant $G$, without an a priori slow-motion assumption.

Formulate and prove precise conditions—on the initial data, the matter model, the gauge, and the regime (e.g., isolated systems with prescribed asymptotic flatness, bounded velocities, compact support, etc.)—under which:

1. The PN and/or PM series, possibly after suitable regularization of the divergent integrals that arise at higher orders, converges to a global-in-time solution of the Einstein equations; or, failing convergence,

2. The truncations of these series at order $N$ provide a genuine asymptotic approximation to such a global solution, in the sense that for each $N$ there exist function-space norms $\|\cdot\|_N$ and constants $C_N$ with
$$\bigl\| g_{\text{exact}} - g_{\text{PN},N}\bigr\|_N \le C_N\, \varepsilon^{N+1}, \qquad \bigl\| g_{\text{exact}} - g_{\text{PM},N}\bigr\|_N \le C_N\, G^{N+1},$$
uniformly on appropriate space-time regions.

Identify the obstructions (e.g., the logarithmic terms appearing at $4$PN order in harmonic gauge, the nonlinear far-field tail effects) and determine the largest class of initial data and matter configurations for which (1) or (2) can be rigorously established.

(b) The post-Minkowskian (PM) expansion: a formal expansion of $g = \eta + \sum_{n\geq 1} G^n h^{(n)}$ around the Minkowski metric $\eta$ in powers of Newton's constant $G$, without an a priori slow-motion assumption.

Formulate and prove precise conditions—on the initial data, the matter model, the gauge, and the regime (e.g., isolated systems with prescribed asymptotic flatness, bounded velocities, compact support, etc.)—under which:

1. The PN and/or PM series, possibly after suitable regularization of the divergent integrals that arise at higher orders, converges to a global-in-time solution of the Einstein equations; or, failing convergence,

2. The truncations of these series at order $N$ provide a genuine asymptotic approximation to such a global solution, in the sense that for each $N$ there exist function-space norms $\|\cdot\|_N$ and constants $C_N$ with
$$\bigl\| g_{\text{exact}} - g_{\text{PN},N}\bigr\|_N \le C_N\, \varepsilon^{N+1}, \qquad \bigl\| g_{\text{exact}} - g_{\text{PM},N}\bigr\|_N \le C_N\, G^{N+1},$$
uniformly on appropriate space-time regions.

Identify the obstructions (e.g., the logarithmic terms appearing at $4$PN order in harmonic gauge, the nonlinear far-field tail effects) and determine the largest class of initial data and matter configurations for which (1) or (2) can be rigorously established.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The rigorous mathematical justification of the convergence (or asymptotic validity) of post-Newtonian and post-Minkowskian expansions remains an open problem. Living Reviews and recent literature note that there is no proof that the PN approximation is even an asymptotic sequence in general, and divergences (e.g., at 4PN order in harmonic coordinates) and far-field tail terms involving logarithms remain serious obstructions. Establishing global existence and uniqueness results adequate to underpin the expansions for general compact matter sources is also lacking.

Definitions. Let ω₁ denote the first uncountable ordinal. An Aronszajn line is a linearly ordered set L of cardinality ω₁ such that L contains no suborder isomorphic to ω₁, no suborder isomorphic to ω₁ with the reverse order (i.e., ω₁*), and no suborder isomorphic to any uncountable set of real numbers. Equip every linearly ordered set with the open-interval topology, whose basic open sets are the open intervals (a,b) = {x : a < x < b}. A topological space is Lindelöf if every open cover admits a countable subcover, and it has countable cellularity (the countable chain condition) if every collection of pairwise disjoint nonempty open sets is countable. A Souslin line is a linearly ordered set of cardinality ω₁ whose open-interval topology has countable cellularity but is not separable. An Aronszajn tree is a tree of height ω₁ all of whose levels and chains are countable; a Souslin tree is an Aronszajn tree in which every antichain is countable. Every Aronszajn line arises canonically from an Aronszajn tree (its underlying tree).

Questions. (a) Does there exist an Aronszajn line that is Lindelöf in its open-interval topology and that contains no Souslin line as a suborder?

(b) If an Aronszajn line L has countable cellularity in its open-interval topology, must the Aronszajn tree from which L arises contain a Souslin subtree?

Let $T=(V,E)$ be a finite simple tree. For a function $f:V\to\{0,1,2\}$, the weight of $f$ is $w(f)=\sum_{v\in V}f(v)$. A vertex $v$ with $f(v)=0$ is said to be defended by a neighbor $w$ with $f(w)\ge 1$ if the function $f'$ obtained from $f$ by setting $f'(v)=1$, $f'(w)=f(w)-1$, and $f'(u)=f(u)$ for all other $u$ has the property that every vertex $u$ with $f'(u)=0$ has a neighbor $x$ with $f'(x)\ge 1$. The function $f$ is a weak Roman dominating function if every vertex $v$ with $f(v)=0$ has some neighbor $w$ that defends it. The weak Roman domination number $\gamma_r(T)$ is the minimum weight of a weak Roman dominating function on $T$.

For a function $g:V\to \mathcal{P}(\{1,2\})$, the weight is $w(g)=\sum_{v\in V}|g(v)|$. The function $g$ is a 2-rainbow dominating function if for every vertex $v$ with $g(v)=\emptyset$ one has $\bigcup_{u\in N(v)} g(u)=\{1,2\}$. The 2-rainbow domination number $\gamma_{r2}(T)$ is the minimum weight of such a function.

Characterize the family of all trees $T$ for which $\gamma_r(T)=\gamma_{r2}(T)$.

representations.normalized:
Consider an isolated astrophysical system modeled as a solution of the Einstein vacuum (or Einstein–matter) field equations
\[ R_{\mu\nu} - \tfrac12 R\, g_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi T_{\mu\nu}, \]
on a 4-dimensional Lorentzian manifold which is asymptotically flat at spatial and null infinity, with compactly supported (or sufficiently localized) stress-energy tensor $T_{\mu\nu}$ describing the matter source.

Develop a simple, usable approximation scheme (for example, a controlled post-Newtonian or post-Minkowskian expansion together with a near-zone/far-zone matching) that accurately determines the gravitational radiation emitted to null infinity by such an isolated source. In particular, give a mathematically rigorous derivation, within general relativity (not merely linearized theory), of the quadrupole radiation formula
\[ \frac{dE}{dt} \;=\; -\frac{G}{5c^{5}}\,\Big\langle \dddot{Q}_{ij}\,\dddot{Q}^{ij}\Big\rangle, \]
where
\[ Q_{ij}(t) \;=\; \int \rho(t,\mathbf{x})\Big(x_i x_j - \tfrac{1}{3}\delta_{ij}|\mathbf{x}|^{2}\Big)\,d^{3}x \]
is the trace-free mass quadrupole moment of the source, $\rho$ is its mass-energy density, and $\langle\,\cdot\,\rangle$ denotes a suitable time average. The derivation must:
(i) start from the full nonlinear Einstein equations,
(ii) yield error estimates controlled by an explicit small parameter (e.g. the ratio of source velocity to the speed of light, or the ratio of Schwarzschild radius to source size), and
(iii) justify the formula as an asymptotic statement about energy flux through future null infinity.

Substantial progress has been made: Blanchet and Damour developed a multipolar post-Minkowskian formalism that systematically expands the vacuum Einstein equations exterior to the source and matches it to a post-Newtonian near-zone expansion, leading to a derivation of the quadrupole formula and its higher-order corrections. These results are widely accepted within the post-Newtonian framework and are central to gravitational-wave template construction, but a fully rigorous mathematical proof from the nonlinear Einstein equations with controlled error bounds (in the sense of mathematical relativity) remains incomplete. Hence the broader problem is partially solved.

Let $b:[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ be a Borel time-dependent vector field whose spatial part $b(t,\cdot)$ has bounded variation (BV) for almost every $t\in[0,T]$, and assume suitable integrability (e.g.\ $b\in L^1((0,T);BV_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^d))$ with $|b|/(1+|x|)\in L^1((0,T);L^1+L^\infty)$). Suppose that the continuity equation
$$\partial_t \rho_t + \mathrm{div}(b\,\rho_t)=0,\qquad \rho_0\equiv 1,$$
admits a solution $\rho_t\in L^\infty((0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^d)$ in the sense of distributions.

A regular Lagrangian flow associated to $b$ is a map $X:[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ such that for a.e.\ $x$, $t\mapsto X(t,x)$ is an absolutely continuous integral curve of $b$ with $X(0,x)=x$, and such that the push-forward $X(t,\cdot)_\#\mathcal{L}^d$ is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure with bounded density.

Question: Under the above assumptions, does there exist a unique (up to negligible sets in the initial datum) regular Lagrangian flow associated to $b$? Equivalently, can the DiPerna–Lions/Ambrosio theory of flows for weakly differentiable vector fields be extended to BV vector fields under the sole structural assumption that the continuity equation starting from the constant density $1$ admits a bounded distributional solution?

Ambrosio (Invent. Math. 2004) established existence and uniqueness of regular Lagrangian flows for BV vector fields under the stronger hypothesis of bounded distributional divergence (so that the constant density is automatically preserved). The more general formulation, requiring only that the continuity equation with initial datum 1 has a bounded solution (i.e. the "nearly incompressible" BV case), is the Bressan compactness conjecture and remains open in general dimensions; partial results exist (e.g. one-dimensional and two-dimensional cases, autonomous settings, and various special structures), but the full BV nearly incompressible case has not been settled.
