Let $\mathcal{M}_g$ denote the moduli space of smooth projective complex curves of genus $g \geq 2$. For a smooth projective curve $X$ of genus $g$, let $SU_X(r)$ denote the moduli space of semistable rank-$r$ vector bundles on $X$ with trivial determinant, and let $\mathcal{L}$ be the ample generator of $\mathrm{Pic}(SU_X(r)) \cong \mathbb{Z}$ (the determinant line bundle). For a positive integer $k$ (the level), consider the finite-dimensional complex vector space of generalized (non-abelian) theta functions
$$V_X := H^0(SU_X(r), \mathcal{L}^{\otimes k}).$$
As $X$ varies, these spaces form a holomorphic vector bundle $\mathcal{V}_{r,k}$ over $\mathcal{M}_g$ (and over Teichmüller space $\mathcal{T}_g$), which carries a natural flat projective connection (the Hitchin connection). Parallel transport with respect to this connection induces a projective representation of the mapping class group $\mathrm{Mod}_g = \pi_1(\mathcal{M}_g)$:
$$\rho_{r,k}: \mathrm{Mod}_g \longrightarrow PGL(V_X).$$

Question: Does there exist, for each $X$, a Hermitian inner product $H_X$ on $V_X$ that is flat with respect to the Hitchin connection (equivalently, varies in a parallel manner with $X$), so that the image of $\rho_{r,k}$ is contained in the projective unitary group $PU(V_X, H_X)$?

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

The projective unitarity of the Hitchin/KZ connection on bundles of generalized (non-abelian) theta functions has been established. Ramadas proved unitarity of the KZ/Hitchin connection on conformal blocks in genus 0, and Andersen (2012, arXiv:1206.2635) established mapping-class-group-invariant unitarity of the Hitchin connection over Teichmüller space, constructing a geometric Hermitian structure projectively preserved by the connection. Thus a flat Hermitian metric $H_X$ exists with $\mathrm{Im}(\rho_{r,k}) \subset PU(H_X)$.

Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface of genus $g \geq 2$. Let $\mathcal{SU}_X(r)$ denote the moduli space of semistable rank-$r$ holomorphic vector bundles on $X$ with trivial determinant, and let $\mathcal{L}$ be the determinant line bundle on $\mathcal{SU}_X(r)$ (the ample generator of $\mathrm{Pic}(\mathcal{SU}_X(r)) \cong \mathbb{Z}$). For an integer $k \geq 1$, the global sections $H^0(\mathcal{SU}_X(r), \mathcal{L}^k)$ are called non-abelian (generalized) theta functions of rank $r$ and level $k$. In the abelian case $r=1$, such sections admit a classical description as explicit holomorphic theta series in coordinates on the Jacobian.

Provide a sufficiently simple and flexible analytic description that realizes the elements of $H^0(\mathcal{SU}_X(r), \mathcal{L}^k)$ as concrete holomorphic functions (in suitable coordinates or on a suitable covering/parameter space), generalizing the classical theta-series description available for $r=1$.

The problem of giving an explicit, flexible analytic realization of non-abelian theta functions as holomorphic functions appears to remain open. A radio labeling (also called L(2,1)-style distance-2 labeling in the broad sense, here in its "radio" form) of a simple graph G=(V,E) is an injective assignment f: V → Z_{>0} of pairwise distinct positive integers to the vertices such that |f(u) - f(v)| ≥ 2 whenever u and v are adjacent in G. The span of f is max_{v ∈ V} f(v). The minimum span over all radio labelings of G is denoted rn(G).

Consider the following decision/optimization problem, called p-RL(*): the input consists of a graph G=(V,E) together with an arbitrary subset W ⊆ V and an injective pre-assignment g: W → Z_{>0} of distinct positive integer labels to the vertices in W. The task is to extend g to a radio labeling f: V → Z_{>0} of all of G (so f restricted to W equals g) whose span is as small as possible.

Restrict the input graph G to be bipartite. Determine the computational complexity of p-RL(*) on the class of bipartite graphs: is it solvable in polynomial time, or is it NP-hard?

Let $d\ge 3$ and let $\mathcal{K}^d$ denote the space of convex bodies (compact convex sets with nonempty interior) in $\mathbb{R}^d$, endowed with the Hausdorff metric (which makes $\mathcal{K}^d$ a complete metric space, so Baire category applies). For a convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, the covariogram of $K$ is the function
$$g_K(x)=\mathrm{vol}_d\bigl(K\cap(K+x)\bigr),\qquad x\in\mathbb{R}^d.$$
For two convex bodies $K,H\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, say that the condition $\mathrm{GC}(\{o\})$ holds if there exists an open neighborhood $U$ of the origin $o\in\mathbb{R}^d$ such that $g_K(x)=g_H(x)$ for every $x\in U$.

A subset of $\mathcal{K}^d$ is meager if it is a countable union of nowhere dense sets; a property is said to hold for most convex bodies if the set of bodies failing it is meager.

Question: Is it true that for most $K\in\mathcal{K}^d$, every convex body $H\in\mathcal{K}^d$ such that $K$ and $H$ satisfy $\mathrm{GC}(\{o\})$ must coincide with $K$ up to translations and point reflections (i.e., $H=\pm K+t$ for some $t\in\mathbb{R}^d$)?

The Baire-generic determination of convex bodies by their covariogram in higher dimensions is known. Definitions. A generalized ordered space (GO-space) is a triple $(X,\tau,<)$ where $(X,<)$ is a linearly ordered set and $\tau$ is a Hausdorff topology on $X$ that has a base consisting of order-convex sets (a set $C\subseteq X$ is order-convex if $a,b\in C$ and $a<x<b$ imply $x\in C$). A linearly ordered topological space (LOTS) is a GO-space whose topology coincides with the open-interval topology induced by $<$. A topological space is perfect if every closed subset is a $G_\delta$. A space has local density at most $\kappa$ if every point has a neighborhood of density at most $\kappa$. A subset $D\subseteq X$ is $\sigma$-closed-discrete if it is a countable union of subsets each of which is closed and discrete in $X$. A topological space is non-Archimedean if it has a base $\mathcal B$ such that any two members of $\mathcal B$ are either disjoint or one contains the other. A space has a point-countable base if it admits a base $\mathcal B$ such that every point belongs to at most countably many members of $\mathcal B$.

Question. Let $\kappa$ be a cardinal with $\kappa>\omega_1$. Is it consistent with ZFC that every perfect GO-space of local density at most $\kappa$ has a $\sigma$-closed-discrete dense subset? Equivalently, is it consistent with ZFC that every perfect non-Archimedean space of local density at most $\kappa$ is metrizable, and is it consistent with ZFC that every perfect GO-space of local density at most $\kappa$ admitting a point-countable base is metrizable?

A matroid $M$ on ground set $E$ is a pair $(E,\mathcal{I})$ where $\mathcal{I}\subseteq 2^E$ satisfies the usual independence axioms. For an independent set $V\subseteq E$ that is a basis of $M$ and an element $e\in E\setminus V$, the fundamental circuit of $e$ with respect to $V$ is the unique circuit contained in $V\cup\{e\}$.

Call a matroid $M$ a framed Dowling matroid with joint set $V$ if $V$ is a basis of $M$ and every fundamental circuit of $M$ with respect to $V$ has size at most $3$. Call a matroid $N$ a Dowling matroid if there exists a framed Dowling matroid $M$ with joint set $V$ such that $N = M\setminus V$ (the matroid obtained from $M$ by deleting the elements of $V$).

Assume matroids are presented by an independence oracle (or rank oracle) on $n$ elements. Does there exist an algorithm that, given such a matroid, decides whether it is a Dowling matroid using a number of oracle calls and arithmetic operations bounded by a polynomial in $n$?

Let G = (V, E) be a finite simple graph and let H be a spanning subgraph of G (the "backbone"). A backbone coloring of (G, H) is a proper vertex coloring c : V → {1, 2, 3, ...} such that |c(u) − c(v)| ≥ 2 for every edge uv of H (while |c(u) − c(v)| ≥ 1 is required for every edge uv of G). The backbone chromatic number bbc(G, H) is the smallest integer k such that there exists a backbone coloring of (G, H) using colors from {1, 2, ..., k}.

Prove or disprove: for every planar graph G and every spanning tree T of G,
    bbc(G, T) ≤ 6.

(Equivalently, can the universal upper bound bbc(G, T) ≤ 7 — which follows from the Four Color Theorem combined with the general spanning-tree bound bbc(G, T) ≤ 2χ(G) − 1 — always be improved by one when G is planar?)

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The conjecture, due to Broersma et al. (2007), that bbc(G,T) ≤ 6 for every planar graph G with spanning tree T appears to remain open in general. Partial results are known: it has been proved when T has diameter at most four, and related circular-backbone variants have been studied. There exist planar graphs with a Hamiltonian-path backbone achieving bbc = 6, showing the bound (if true) is tight. No source found claiming a complete resolution.
